News.title: Horror moment Russian paratrooper plunges to his death as chute fails to open during botched display near Moscow
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a Russian paratrooper plunges to his death after he jumped from a plane and his parachute failed to open.

The 41-year-old veteran leapt from the plane flying at nearly 2000ft (600m) above the ground during a display to celebrate Airborne Forces Day, Russian media reported.



Horrifying footage captures the elite soldier’s parachute failing to inflate and the man twisting desperately in the air as he falls.

The paratrooper attempted to activate his reserve parachute but the distance to the ground was too short for it to expand in time to save his life, according to Visegrád 24.



The tragedy unfolded near Moscow on Sunday, when Russia observes a military holiday honouring the nation’s paratroopers.

An image of the aftermath of the horrific accident shows a white parachute spread across the grass and the soldier’s body blurred out.



Airborne Forces Day is celebrated on August 2 in Russia and commemorates the role of paratroopers during military operations.

The celebration comes as Vladimir Putin continues his brutal invasion of Ukraine.



As the war grinds on, both sides have resorted to drone attacks as a way to gain the upper hand and grind down the other side’s resources.

This includes Ukraine launching drone attacks on a holiday spot on the Black Sea near one of Putin’s palaces, as well as a fatal bombing in Moscow on the weekend.

In the face of recent military blows, the Russian dictator would have sought to use Airborne Forces Day as an opportunity to project strength.

He said in a post on the Kremlin’s website that airborne divisions had “always been filled with men of exceptional fortitude, indomitable spirit, unwavering resolve, a profound sense of comradeship, and mutual support”.

He said: “You are rightfully proud of the founders of the Airborne Forces, the immortal deeds and outstanding achievements of those who came before you, and you honour your veterans as role models.



“I would like to particularly note the skillful and resolute actions of the paratroopers who are defending Russia in the special military operation zone, shoulder to shoulder with their brothers in arms, displaying heroism and courage in the most critical sectors of the front.”

News.title: Watch as brazen airline pilot is caught trying to smuggle 70,000 ecstasy pills through airport security
News.content:
THIS is the moment a pilot under the influence of drugs is busted trying to smuggle 70,000 ecstasy pills through airport security.

Wild footage shows the moment customs officers ordered the brazen pilot to unzip his case before uncovering a huge stash of pills.



The pilot arrived in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Malaysia Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur in the early hours of July 29.

The man, identified as a 39-year-old Malaysian national, was selected for a bag inspection after officers noticed irregularities in his profile and movements.



It did not take a thorough search for the officers to locate the large bag of pills, which appeared to be concealed in a hidden pocket.

A total of 70,114 pills were uncovered as well as 4g of methamphetamine.



A small bottle of urine was also seized, which investigators believe had been prepared to falsify the results of a drug test if one was required.

He underwent a drug test and reportedly tested positive for methamphetamine, ecstasy and cocaine.



The Soekarno-Hatta Customs Office said: “Through risk analysis, profiling, officer observations, and X-ray and physical inspections, the smuggling attempt was successfully foiled.

“The suspect and the seized evidence were subsequently handed over to the Indonesian National Police Criminal Investigation Agency for further investigation and efforts to identify the wider trafficking network.”

During questioning, the pilot allegedly admitted he had been promised £9,086 to deliver the ecstasy, which was to be collected from his hotel.



He also confessed to transporting methamphetamine on two previous occasions once to Sabah, Malaysia, and once to Jakarta.

Malaysia Airlines said in a statement that it: “Does not tolerate any form of misconduct and is currently undertaking an internal review of the matter.”

It comes as a fake pilot was caught with 10kg of cocaine strapped to his body before boarding a Europe-bound flight.

The man – dressed in a navy pilots blazer complete with gold epaulettes – was thwarted at El Dorado International Airport, Colombia.

Wild footage shows police cutting away white wrapping from around the man’s torso before removing several packages taped to his body.



Officers recovered five rectangular packages and a specially adapted belt containing cocaine hydrochloride.

His subsequent arrest stopped almost 25,000 doses of cocaine from reaching international markets and dealt a significant financial blow to organised crime groups, Colombia’s Anti-Narcotics Police said.

News.title: Three boys rushed to hospital after moped they were riding crashed with patrolling cop car as teen arrested
News.content:
SMASH SHOCK Three boys rushed to hospital after moped they were riding crashed with patrolling cop car as teen arrested

THREE boys riding a stolen moped have been rushed to hospital after crashing into a police car on patrol.

The collision occurred at around 3.45pm on Monday in Wythenshawe, Manchester.



The boys, aged between 14 and 16, collided with a Greater Manchester Police car while cruising down a street on the stolen vehicle.

Cops say the officers in the car were travelling at a “low speed” when the moped, travelling in the opposite direction, collided with them.



One boy has been discharged from hospital while the other two are still receiving treatment.

They have been placed under arrest on suspicion of going equipped and theft of a motor vehicle.

The police have referred themselves to the Professional Standards Directorate, which has made a referral to IOPC.

A spokesperson for GMP said today: “An investigation is ongoing following a collision between a police car and a moped shortly after 3.45pm on Monday 4 August 2026.



“Officers were patrolling at low speed around Broadoak Park, Wythenshawe, when their vehicle collided with a moped travelling in the opposite direction.

“Three boys aged between 14 and 16 who were riding the bike have been arrested on suspicion of going equipped and theft of a motor vehicle.

“Further enquiries established the moped was stolen.

“The three boys were taken to hospital – one has been since been discharged with two remaining for further treatment.

“In line with force policy, this incident has been referred to our Professional Standards Directorate, who have made a referral to IOPC.”

News.title: ‘I showed it our veg and it flew at me’: Ukrainian grocer tells of horror after being hunted by Russian suicide drone
News.content:
A UKRAINIAN grocer who was “hunted” by a Russian suicide drone has recounted the horror attack.

Yuriy, 52, said he was laying out vegetables for sale when he heard the terrifying hum of the approaching UAV.



“We couldn’t see it – it came flying out from somewhere behind the market, where the bushes are, and flew so low”, he said in a video shared on Telegram.

But when his wife ran away, the killing machine turned to him.



In a desperate bid to save himself, he gestured to his vegetables to signal to the drone operator he was not a threat.

“I pointed it out to him – look, it’s just vegetables. But then it started coming at me, so I started to run away,” Yuriy said.



“I didn’t take any pictures of it. Nothing. I actually had garlic in my hands and I was showing it to him”, he added.

The grocer turned to run away but said the drone “came out from under the umbrella” to hunt him down.



At first the UAV fired at his car, with the force of the strike ripping metal sheets back across the bonnet.

Yuriy, who was right next to the vehicle at the time, was thrown to the ground by the impact.

Shrapnel sliced through his skin across his torso and arms.



Yuriy also suffered an injury to his ear and bruises across his body from the blast.

The horror attack was caught on camera in the bloodbath Ukrainian city of Kherson.

Police said the clip “makes your blood run cold”.

Chilling footage shows Yuriy, from neighbouring Mikolaiv, clasping his hands in prayer and running around his stall as he is chased by the Russian quadcopter.

Police published the clip with the warning: “This is how the Russians fight. They are purposefully hunting civilians.”



Putin’s invading forces have been repeatedly accused of launching “human safaris” to murder civilians in Kherson.

The attack comes a week after a volunteer distributing aid was targeted inside his van by a Russian drone.

Hope for Ukraine, the charity that he was working with, said: “Oleksandr was targeted and killed by a Russian drone while delivering vital humanitarian aid to frontline communities.



“He was always drawn to where he was needed most, risking everything to save others. His bravery will forever inspire us.”

Kremlin troops captured the provincial capital Kharkiv in the first days of the full- scale invasion but they were forced to make a humiliating retreat in October 2022.

But since they have hammered the city with rockets, artillery and drone attacks – as it is only separated from Russian-controlled territory by a 1,000ft wide river.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly raised the alarm over escalating drone attacks, saying just weeks ago: “The situation is especially difficult in Kherson, where the Russians are conducting a safari against people.

“Defences must be significantly strengthened with more interceptors, more electronic jamming systems, and more gun crews operating in the city.”

News.title: UK seaside town will celebrate Christmas TOMORROW with Santa on the beach, festive music and grotto
News.content:
A SEASIDE resort town is preparing to celebrate Christmas on the beach tomorrow (August 5) as part of an unusual tradition.

Locals have been encouraged to put on a Christmas jumper and a pair of flip flops for a day of carolling and ice creams.



Residents of Bridlington, on the East Yorkshire coastline, are set to celebrate Christmas tomorrow in a packed programme of festive entertainment.

Known as “Bridmas Day”, the jam-packed day of activities is organised by East Riding of Yorkshire council to promote the town as an all-year-round destination.



A cabinet member for the council, Nick Coultish, said Bridmas Day has become “one of the highlights of Bridlington’s events calendar”.

Throughout the day, families will be able to buy goodies at the Christmas Market, enjoy their favourite festive music, and watch a showing of The Grinch.



Children can even meet Santa at his summertime grotto on Bridlington South Beach, where a Christmas tree will be put up to mark the occasion.

Local businesses are expected to take part in the celebrations by dressing up their stores in Christmas decorations.

For Bridlington, the festivities mark the beginning of its seasonal offers launch, where locals can snap up prizes and exclusive offers for a number different winter activities.

These include a family day pass to the historic country house Sewerby Hall and Gardens, tickets on the Santa Express, and two tickets to see a Shania Twain tribute act at Bridlington Spa on Friday night.



Visitors can also secure a 10 per cent discount for the local Pantomine of Cinderella, starring Celebrity Big Brother winner, David Potts.

Despite the positivity from East Riding of Yorkshire council, who have counted down the days with 12 Days of Christmas posts, others are more sceptical.

One local said: “Come on guys. Let’s enjoy our lovely summer holidays without being reminded of Christmas just yet.”



Bridmas Day will be celebrated in Bridlington Spa from 10am to 4pm tomorrow, with a number of free events on offer.

News.title: Man, 35, arrested on suspicion of murder after beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site as family pay tribute
News.content:
MURDER ARREST Man, 35, arrested on suspicion of murder after beloved dad, 36, shot dead at UK traveller site as family pay tribute

ANOTHER man has been arrested on suspicion of murder following the fatal shooting of a “much-loved” husband and father.

Jimmy Ward, 36, was pronounced dead at Calcutt traveller site near Cricklade, Wiltshire, on Sunday morning.



A man, 35, has been arrested today on suspicion of murder after Jimmy was shot dead.

Wiltshire Police have said that a total of five people have been arrested in connection with Jimmy’s death.



Two other men, aged 53 and 29, were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender following a vehicle stop on the A419 road today.

On Sunday, a 74-year-old man and 42-year-old woman were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and possession of a firearm.

All five people are in custody for questioning, police confirmed.

Tributes have poured in for Jimmy, with people leaving flowers and cards at the traveller site.



One mourner wrote: “RIP to my daughter-in-law’s dad Jimmy Ward. Please everyone pray for all the family, my heart goes out to them all.’

Another said: “Very hard to believe. Rest in heavenly peace my cousin Jimmy Ward,” added another.”

“Thinking of all the family and friends at this very sad time, sending lots of love to his wife and children. Far too young to die, rest in peace,” said another local.

Others have described him as “a gentleman”.

It’s believed Jimmy leaves behind a wife and children.



Senior Investigating Officer Detective Chief Inspector Phil Walker said: “This is a significant development in our investigation.

“I can confirm that a man has been arrested on suspicion of Jimmy’s murder and is now in police custody, along with four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender.

“Jimmy’s next of kin have been informed of this development and my thoughts continue to be with them.

“They are being supported by specially trained officers.

“A scene and heavy policing presence remain in place at the traveller site in Calcutt while further inquiries are carried out. I continue to ask that this cordon is respected.



“I’d like to thank the local community for their support and patience since Sunday.

“We understand this incident has caused significant concern, so please consider speaking with officers about any information or concerns you may have.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting log 95 of August 2.

Information can also be passed to Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Inexplicable decision to free thugs who killed PC Harper is final betrayal – it’s an insult to us all, says police chief
News.content:
NO police officer will forget where they were on that summer’s night in 2019 when the radio call came through about the death of our colleague PC Andrew Harper.

Harps had been brutally killed.



Dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His injuries were catastrophic.



Nor will we forget the faces of Andrew’s smirking killers – Henry Long, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers – as they attended the Old Bailey to be found guilty of his manslaughter.

These low lifes showed no remorse. They offered no apology.

Equally, neither will we forget the Government’s inexplicable and unforgivable decision to allow those who kill police officers to be released early from jail.

It is a final betrayal from the politicians, who are supposed to be on our side.

A smack in the face to every one of us police officers across the United Kingdom, who are out there now risking our lives to keep you, the public, safe.

I am absolutely outraged that Justice Secretary Alex Norris, and Prime Minister Andy Burnham, have decided that killing a police officer in the execution of their duty is somehow less serious than other offences deemed too dangerous for early release.



Both said they wanted to do more to stop the release of two of the young men convicted of killing Harps after serving just 40 per cent of their 13-year tariffs.

They may have claimed they wanted to do more but facts matter. They did not.

Let me be clear now, on behalf of thousands of Thames Valley Police Officers.



I challenge the Prime Minister and Justice Secretary to stand before Andrew’s widow, Lissie, his parents, his brother, his loved ones, or indeed any police officer in this country.

Stand before them and explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should still be eligible for early release.

Try telling the officers who attended the scene where Andrew died on 15 August 2019 and witnessed the horrific consequences of that crime.

And the friends and colleagues who had to hear about Andrew’s death on their radio.

Explain to them why the life of a police officer does not warrant the same protection as other serious crimes under this legislation.



This decision pours salt into wounds that have never healed.

It is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family.

Time and again they have been forced to relive their grief while watching a justice system that they trusted, fail to recognise the unique sacrifice made by those who serve and protect the public.



We stood side by side with Lissie as she successfully campaigned for Harper’s Law in Andrew’s name following their pitiful manslaughter sentences these three teenagers received.

As a result of the campaign, those who kill emergency service workers now receive mandatory life sentences.

If Andrew’s killers were convicted today, they would receive life sentences due to the law that was created in his name.

They would not be eligible for early release.

I completely agree that rapists and child sexual offenders should not be released early from their sentences.



However, you cannot say in the next breath that people who kill people – and in particular police officers out there protecting society – can be subject to that release.

It’s perverse to say that, and it does not make sense. And that’s what I need to understand.

So what next?



We will throw everything at this through a proper legal challenge from KCs, barristers, you name it. Our colleagues will accept nothing less.

This decision is totally demoralising for all police officers and our fellow emergency service workers, who put themselves in harm’s way to protect and serve their community.

And not just in Thames Valley, but right across the country.

We will do what we have to do to protect Andrew Harper’s legacy and other victims up and down the country who don’t have a platform to put their points across on radio, television and in newspapers.

Because make no mistake there are silent victims, families and loved ones of other individuals who have been killed, who will also be outraged at this.



Police officers put themselves in harm’s way every day.

They run towards danger when everyone else is running away.

They do so knowing that they may never come home to their families.



For the Government to exclude the killers of police officers from these protections sends a deeply troubling message about the value placed on those who make that sacrifice.

Andrew Harper’s family deserved better. Every police officer in this country deserves better.

I will not stand by while the voices of Andrew’s family, his colleagues and police officers across this country continue to be ignored.

We will take this to Parliament. We will not stop. Andy Burnham may be on his holidays but we won’t rest on this.

And you can help us.



We have launched a petition – Stop the early release from jail of PC Andrew Harper’s killers – and would encourage all right-minded members of the public to please sign and share this link.

We will be working hard with both local and national politicians to right this wrong.

How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer is not serious enough to merit the stiffest of punishments.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you kill a police officer there should be no early release. No ifs. No buts.

Somebody, somewhere, must finally listen.

News.title: Severed heads & bombs as wedding gifts… ISIS breeding ground minutes from Ceuta with new migrant invasion feared in days
News.content:
A MOROCCAN town next to Spanish enclave Ceuta that saw an influx of migrants last week is an ISIS breeding ground once home to a terrorist brute who posed with severed heads and gifted his bride a bomb belt.

The border town of Fnideq, which hosts 85,000 inhabitants and is known in Spanish as Castillejos, is the closest Moroccan urban centre to Ceuta.



It comes amid fears jihadist’s could cross into Ceuta – after 70,000 migrants breached the border on Thursday.

Fnideq is a primary recruitment hub for Islamic State extremists in North Africa.



In 2015, at the height of the Syrian conflict, it was estimated around 400 of the 1,200 Moroccans who had travelled to Syria and Iraq to join ISIS came from Fnideq.

One of them, Mohamed Hamdouch, became notorious for posing with the severed heads of his victims – and was known as The Decapitator.

In one image that appeared on jihadist forums he held a bloody knife in his hand and showed off the severed heads of five Syrian soldiers.

The Moroccan ISIS fighter, also known as Kokito Castillejos, gained notoriety in Spain for marrying a woman from Ceuta and giving her an explosive belt as a wedding gift.



He was killed while fighting in Syria in November 2015.

Many Islamic extremists have snuck into Spain as irregular migrants in the past before going on to be arrested or linked to terror.

This includes former rapper-turned-jihadist Abdel-Majed Abdel-Bary, who was raised in Maida Vale, West London.



The dual British-Egyptian national quit his music career to join ISIS in Syria in 2013, quickly becoming one of the group’s most infamous British faces.

He sparked horror after posting a picture holding the severed head of a Syrian soldier, captioned: “Chillin’ with my homie, or what’s left of him.”

The image even led to him being briefly misidentified as ISIS executioner “Jihadi John”.



After fleeing ISIS, Abdel-Bary sneaked into Spain by migrant boat from Algeria in April 2020 alongside two accomplices – Abderrazak Seddiki, 31, and Kossaila Chollouah, 28.

All three were arrested in a hideout in Almería.

While his two companions were later convicted of terror offenses, Abdel-Bary was found dead in his Cadiz prison cell in July 2023, just days into his Madrid trial.

Some 70,000 people swam from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta located in North Africa on Thursday – with dramatic images and videos showing the chaos unfold.

There are fears another mass border crossing is being planned in the coming days – as social media posts calling for a second invasion gain traction.



Reports say the peninsula could see scenes of mayhem play out on the streets yet again, as plans are being made for another mass border crossing on August 15.

On social media, posts appear to be plotting another storming of the shores of Ceuta, with one message reading: “Everything will be seen that day.”

Another appears to call for the creation of a WhatsApp group, saying: “Our appointment is on 15/08/2026.”

Migrants desperate to try to reach Europe are reportedly being encouraged to join the group by sending a private message using the password “Ceuta”.

The revelation of the messages and posts – written in Darija, an Arabic dialect spoken in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia – has sparked major concern in Ceuta.



It also comes after Spanish cops claimed today at least a dozen convicted terrorists were among those who went across the border last week.

Terrorists previously deported to Morocco after arrests in Spain were part of the mass crossing, local outlet El Espanol reported.

Authorities believe it is “very possible” the number of criminals with links to Islamic extremists could increase.

The Spanish territory is still reeling from the “apocalyptic” scenes last week.

Up to 70,000 migrants were believed to have entered the city during the frenzied ordeal.



Over 48,000 have been frogmarched back across the frontier by Spanish cops and military personnel.

But there are currently an estimated 5,000 migrants, including nearly 1,000 children, remaining in the Spanish territory trying to dodge the security sweep.

Distressing pictures have shown dozens of North African youths sleeping on the pavement on makeshift beds made out of cardboard boxes.

The children will most likely end up being transferred to the Spanish mainland to ease overcrowding in Ceuta.

The city is already caring for some 850 children, but is planning to expand its facilities with two more centres, as the number of youngsters is expected to rise over the coming days.



Fights broke out on Monday during the first Red Cross handout of food and drinks at Trampolin Beach.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Several police clashes also erupted last week amid the chaos, and at least 72 people were killed due to drowning or the resulting beach stampede after the migrants crossed into the Spanish territory.

News.title: Toddler, 3, dead after getting stuck in kitchen play set at babysitter's house
News.content:
Toddler, 3, dead after getting stuck in kitchen play set at babysitter's house

A three-year-old girl has died after becoming trapped in a toy kitchen play set at a babysitter's home in Boynton Beach, Palm Beach County, in the state of Florida

View 2 Images A three-year-old girl died at her babysitter's home in Boynton Beach (Image: WPBF 25 News)

A three-year-old girl has tragically died after her head became stuck in a kitchen play set at her babysitter's home.

‌



The horror unfolded at a property in the Meadows neighbourhood of Boynton Beach, a city in Palm Beach County, Florida, on July 23. The Boynton Beach Police Department said officers were called shortly after 11am EDT (4pm BST) to a report that a child was unresponsive and not breathing.

‌



Officers immediately began life-saving measures before Boynton Beach Fire Rescue arrived. The toddler was rushed to hospital in a critical condition and died several days later on July 27, the police department said.

‌



Investigators said the girl and her sibling had been staying at a babysitter's home. Police said the babysitter had left the property and placed the children in the care of their spouse at the time of the incident, CBS12 News reports.

View 2 Images No criminal charges have been filed, but the investigation is ingoing (Image: WPBF 25 News)

‌



According to investigators, the spouse checked on the children periodically and, during one of those checks, found the girl with her head trapped inside the play kitchen. He freed her and began emergency aid.

Investigators said the child’s sibling told them the three-year-old had become trapped while trying to retrieve toys that had fallen inside the play set.

Boynton Beach Police Public Information Officer Chelsea Sanabia told CBS12 News that the toy kitchen was "an old wooden set that was bought off of Facebook Marketplace a few years ago". She added that investigators have not identified the make, model or brand.

Article continues below

The child's cause of death has not yet been revealed. It is also not known for how long she may have been trapped or whether the case has been submitted for criminal review.

Police have not identified the girl, her parents or the babysitter. The investigation is ongoing.

News.title: Hormuz could open 'today or tomorrow' in new US-Iran deal as oil prices tumble
News.content:
Hormuz could open 'today or tomorrow' in new US-Iran deal as oil prices tumble

Oil prices fell sharply Tuesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated there may be a deal to open the key Strait of Hormuz as soon as this week.

View 2 Images US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent says the Strait of Hormuz could reopen 'today or tomorrow'

US officials are optimistic about striking a fresh deal with Iran that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz - sparking a major fall in oil prices.

‌



Treasury secretary Scott Bessent said there was "a chance" the US could reach a deal with Iran to reopen the key waterway, which Iran has blockaded, "today or tomorrow".

‌



State secretary Marco Rubio said there has been "progress made in those talks, but not finality yet". He said the US was "hoping that will happen very shortly".

‌



View 2 Images Scott Bessent said there was a chance of a new deal (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump said yesterday (Monday) that talks with Tehran were ongoing and the country had a "last chance" to reach a deal.

‌



However, Iranian officials insisted no negotiations with the US were taking place.

Brent the international oil benchmark, slid more than 5.4% to $79.21 per barrel after Mr Bessent's comments. Petrol prices drop when oil prices fall, but the change is delayed and usually happens slower than when prices go up.

When Bessent was asked whether Iran would be allowed to charge a toll, he told CNBC's Sqawk Box: "It would be freedom of movement."

Article continues below

Oil prices should drop further when hundreds of ships stuck in the Persian Gulf are able to exit, Bessent said. “It’s not just energy. It’s fertilizer, it’s refined products, it is the various industrial gasses,” he said. “We could see a big relief trade as those prices go down.”

News.title: Facebook rants of dad accused of murdering Elisabeth-Jane Ross and stuffing body in suitcase
News.content:
Facebook rants of dad accused of murdering Elisabeth-Jane Ross and stuffing body in suitcase

Sharif Ahmadzai, a father of one, will appear in court in Athens on Wednesday on suspicion of murdering Elisabeth-Jane Ross, an aid worker originally from Edinburgh

View 4 Images Sharif Ahmadzai is suspected of killing Elisabeth-Jane Ross in Athens (Image: INSTAGRAM)

A young man accused of killing a British charity worker and stuffing her body in a suitcase posted social media rants about "corruption wearing a Christian mask", it has emerged.

Sharif Ahmadzai, who has allegedly killed Elisabeth-Jane Ross in Athens, converted to Christianity after meeting now wife Alaina Hall through charity work. Together, Ahmadzai and Ms Hall run a charity called Love Every Nation, which supports homeless people and refugees in the Greek capital.

But Ahmadzai, 26, will appear in court there on Wednesday charged with Ms Ross' murder. Her body was discovered by a homeless man in an abandoned building in Athens on July 18. CCTV footage emerged this week and appears to show Ahmadzai, a champion boxer, wheel through the city centre a suitcase, which it is said contained Ms Ross' body. Ms Ross, originally from Edinburgh, was an aid worker who met Ahmadzai and his wife through volunteering efforts.

View 4 Images Ms Ross, an aid worker, was found dead on July 18 (Image: Facebook)

Today, it emerged Ahmadzai had posted a string of rants on Facebook since May last year, taking aim at the actions of Christian NGOs he previously encountered on Lesvos, Greece.

Ahmadzai, who proposed to Ms Hall in 2022 and has a baby son with the woman, also posted photos of t-shirts decorated with the message: "Boycott corrupt NGOs" and told how vetween 2016 and 2019, when he was aged between 16 and 20, he was a volunteer translator in the Lesvos' Moria refugee camp.

In May, he wrote: "Shame on corruption dressed like charity. Shame on business wearing the name of Christ. In the name of Christ, people are being used. Volunteers, students, churches, and families from America and Europe are giving their time, money, and trust but many of them never stop to ask the most important question: 'Where is the money really going?'

"When an NGO charges volunteers hundreds of euros for 'registration,' takes cash for housing, places 15 or 16 people in apartments meant for one or two, and collects far more than the real cost that is not ministry. That is business. And when vulnerable refugee stories are used to raise money while the real support goes into private pockets, that is not the work of Christ. That is corruption wearing a Christian mask."

He added: "I have met good people there. I will never deny that. But good volunteers do not automatically make a corrupt system holy."

View 4 Images Chilling CCTV appears to show Ahmadzai wheel a suitcase through Athens city centre - and it is said to contain the woman's remains (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Ahmadzai, who was born in Afghanistan and settled in Greece after travelling there as a teenager, was arrested after police collaborated with the UK’s National Crime Agency and Police Scotland.

Ms Ross's mobile phone – which had been off for days – was suddenly switched on earlier this week with police immediately tracing it to a residence in Athens where Ahmadzai was staying.

George Kalliakmanis, honorary president of the police officers’ association in Athens, said: “He has admitted to carrying her body in a trolley to the site. Police have CCTV footage of him doing this on the night of July 16. He has also confessed to withdrawing €10,000 [£8,500] from ATMs using credit cards that belonged to her. But he has denied murder, which police do not believe.”

Mr Kalliakmanis added that Ahmadzai's US-born wife Ms Hall, who is understood to have been friends with Ms Ross, was very helpful to detectives. Officers reportedly began investigating Ahmadzai last Thursday after she reported he had been behaving suspiciously and woke to find him missing and checked the location of his phone, which allegedly showed he was at Ms Ross’s apartment on Rethymnou Street in central Athens.

View 4 Images Ahmadzai is pictured with his US-born wife Alaina Hall whom he met through charity work (Image: FACEBOOK)

Close relatives of Ahmadzai's wife Hall have spoken out about the man with whom she has a young son. Her aunt, Leanne Hall, said her pilot brother, Thomas, 65, and sister-in-law Susan, 61, always had grave doubts about their daughter's choice of husband.

Asked about Ahmadzai, she told the Daily Mail: "I've never met him, I've only heard about him. But I can tell you my brother and sister-in-law never wanted them to get married."

Ms Ross had been a regular visitor to Greece over the past seven years, volunteering as an aid worker with NGOs helping refugees, homeless people and other vulnerable groups and had previously volunteered with the One Heart organisation, which specialises in providing medical support to refugees, particularly those from Afghanistan and Iran.

Ms Ross' aunt, Anne Bangham, said of the 38-year-old woman's death: “It is horrific. She was such a beautiful, loving and kind young lady. She had not long arrived there to work.” Ms Ross, known as Lisa, has been praised for her "unstoppable passion" for helping those less fortunate. Senior pastors and the congregation at Destiny Church, Edinburgh, where she was a member of the church, have paid tribute to her.

Pastor Peter Anderson speaks on killing of Elisabeth-Jane Ross

In a statement, senior pastors, Andrew and Sue Owen, said: "Lisa will always be remembered for her unstoppable passion to help those who were less fortunate than herself.

‌



"This passion and deep sense of calling sometimes took her to challenging places. Lisa was determined not to leave this world the same way she found it."

They added their thoughts and prayers are with Ms Ross's family, who have lost "a beautiful daughter and sister".

Ms Ross had also been a member of City on a Hill church, in Edinburgh, for 20 years. Pastor Peter Anderson said she was a precious member of the congregation.

Article continues below

In a video posted on the City on a Hill's Facebook page, he said: "It's been a really tough week for our church. We have lost a precious church member, Lisa. She was a member of our church for 20 years, and a very, very precious girl, and it's a real tragic loss."

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said: "Our thoughts are with Elisabeth's family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities."

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland."

News.title: Smartphones, street food and Boho chic: Biggest festival trends of 2026 revealed
News.content:
Smartphones, street food and Boho chic: Biggest festival trends of 2026 revealed

Smartphones, social media and street food top the list of things festival goers-can't go without while enjoying a weekend of music - while 77% say they plan their outfits in advance

View 2 Images Festival goers would rather lose their phones than their friends, according to a new survey (Image: IMAGO/Vlad Bereholschi)

The biggest trends for festival season 2026 have been revealed - and top of the list come smartphones, social media and street food.

‌



New research has revealed that keeping in touch during this summer’s live music events is now more important than traditional essentials such as tents and wellies.

‌



A staggering 87% of festival-goers say reliable connectivity is crucial to making the most of a festival weekend, according to Vodafone's Connected Crowd Report.

‌



In fact, 14% of festival goers would rather lose their tent, 20% would prefer to wave goodbye to their wellies and 16% would rather lose their friends than their phones.

View 2 Images The biggest trends for festivals this summer have been revealed - and it's not just about the music (Image: Cover Images )

The study also found that phones and connectivity are increasingly influencing every aspect of festival life, from discovering artists and planning outfits to tracking down the hottest food stalls.

‌



Social media plays a huge role in deciding who to watch at a live event with 81% searching online to discover new acts before attending.

Charli XCX is the most talked about act across social media this summer with viral sensation Sienna Spiro shaping up to be the breakout star.

Festival fashion is also increasingly dictated online, with 77% planning their outfits in advance and TikTok overtaking friends, Instagram and celebrities as the biggest source of inspiration.

‌



Meanwhile, glitter and glam are giving way to more practical looks, with searches for "comfy festival outfits", "festival head scarf" and "boho festival outfits" among the biggest trends of summer 2026.

Food has become as important as the music itself, with 67% expecting high-quality options and 63% seeking out globally inspired dishes. Six in 10 said posting a picture of their meal on social media is now as important as actually eating it.

The trend feeds into what is expected to be the most shared festival season yet, with 76% planning to document their weekend online.

‌



For eight in 10 (80%) festival goers, having good connectivity matters to them so they can stay in touch with friends and family on site and back home during a festival weekend.

The rise of the "remote festival goer" is also gathering pace, with two thirds saying they have video-called friends or family during a live performance so they can experience the moment in real time.

A Vodafone spokesperson said: “At Vodafone, our ambition has always been to connect people to the UK’s biggest moments, on The Nation’s Network.

‌



“We've seen data usage continue to grow across the festivals we support, reflecting the increasingly important role connectivity plays in the festival experience.

“Whether it's helping people stay in touch with friends in a busy crowd, navigate the site, or share unforgettable moments as they happen, reliable connectivity has become an essential part of making the most of a festival.

“That's why we're committed to providing the best possible network experience, so festival goers can stay connected and enjoy every moment.”

Article continues below

As the Official Connectivity Partner of nine music festivals across the UK, Vodafone is helping festival goers stay connected to every unforgettable moment. This festival season, non-Vodafone customers can try their network for free, with no commitments and no strings attached. They'll receive 7-days on The Nation's Network, including 50GB of data, 500 minutes and 500 texts, so they can stream, share and stay connected all weekend long.

News.title: Woman pleads for help on husband's 999 call to confess he had 'killed his wife'
News.content:
Woman pleads for help on husband's 999 call to confess he had 'killed his wife'

Anthony Buxton's mental health had deteriorated in the months before his wife, Michelle, died at their home in Camelford, Cornwall

View Image Police outside the couple's property in Camelford, Cornwall (Image: Adrian Jasper/Cornwall Live)

A husband told emergency services "I've done it, no one can stop me" when he called 999 to confess to killing his wife before taking his own life.

‌



Anthony Buxton's mental health had deteriorated in the months before he strangled his wife, Michelle, 69. An inquest held at Cornwall Coroner's Court in Truro today (Tuesday) heard that, during the call on September 24 last year, Mr Buxton, 71, was heard saying "I've killed her" after a woman was heard groaning and saying "help".

‌



PC Jacob Double was one of the officers sent to the scene, along with another colleague. In a written statement, PC Double said: "As we were travelling, further information came to light, which stated in the call to ambulance a female voice could be heard groaning and saying, 'help', and a male voice was heard saying, 'I’ve done it, no one can stop me, I’ve killed her."

‌



The officers forced entry to the property in Camelford, Cornwall, and found the couple unresponsive and with fatal injuries. Both were pronounced dead a short time later.

Dad tried to save his daughter on Fistral Beach before both swept to their deaths READ MORE :

Post-mortem examinations showed Mrs Buxton died from compression of the neck, while Mr Buxton died from a stab wound to his chest. The couple’s son, Daniel, told the inquest his father had become unusually quiet in the months before his death and was becoming paranoid.

The civilian police worker said: "Eventually it got to the point where mum seemed to be struggling and dad was getting quite anxious and really not wanting to tell us any information and would get defensive when pressed.

‌



"It was anxiety trying to assuage any fears he might have. We installed CCTV cameras in the house because he was concerned there was an overarching delusion he had. He had this idea or beliefs that an organised crime gang was targeting him and had access to the house and had bugged the house with microphones and cameras, and his family were in danger.

"The overarching goal of this crime gang was to exhort mum and dad for police secrets from me because I work for the police." Georgina Clark, from the Cornwall Partnership Mental Health Trust, said Mr Buxton had been referred to them by his GP on August 29 and an assessment was carried out on September 2.

She said: "Because of Mr Buxton’s age and the possibility of an organic cause, as there had also been mention from the GP of short-term memory loss over the past couple of years, it was felt it should be discussed with the dementia and older people’s service first.

‌



"The assessing clinician took that to the duty worker and had that discussion and what they said was that he noted to be presenting with severe anxiety and that would need to be treated first as someone who is very anxious that can affect their ability to retain memory."

Andrew Cox, senior coroner for Cornwall, asked Ms Clark: "Mr Buxton was not a natural fit for any service because he is not typically presenting as a dementia patient, and he is too old to fit into the early intervention for psychosis? You are left with having to make a best fit where there isn’t an obvious pathway for him to follow? Is that fair?”

She replied: "To a degree. I think that service would be offered by the community mental health team."

‌



Mr Buxton was referred to the community mental health team, who felt talking therapy would be appropriate to deal with his anxiety, the inquest heard. Detective Constable Tom Graham, who investigated both deaths, said there was no evidence of third party involvement.

Mr Cox returned a conclusion of unlawful killing for Mrs Buxton and said her husband had taken his own life. He said: "I think what has become apparent subsequent to these events is that no one had the full picture.

"What is abundantly clear from the papers is that no one, family members or mental health practitioners, seriously felt that Michelle was at risk of harm from her husband Anthony. I have accepted as fact that on September 24 Anthony strangled his wife, and I’m also further going to accept the evidence from the police that having done that he’s then stabbed himself in the chest.

Article continues below

"If Anthony had survived, he would inevitably have been charged with a homicide offence." Addressing the family, the coroner added: "This is a dreadful set of circumstances, completely unexpected, and you have my deepest sympathies for what has occurred."

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to third child and says she is 'beyond in love'
News.content:
Princess Eugenie gives birth to third child and says she is 'beyond in love'

Princess Eugenie and husband Jack Brooksbank have welcomed their third child together, a daughter, who is a little sister for their sons August and Ernest

View 6 Images Princess Eugenie has announced the birth of her third child - a daughter born in Portugal (Image: @princesseugenie/Instagram)

Princess Eugenie has given birth to her third child - a girl - and said she and husband Jack Brooksbank are "beyond in love".

‌



The youngest daughter of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson, who already has two children with her husband, shared the happy news with a picture of the newborn and a post on Instagram. It read: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!! We are beyond in love with our girlie" followed by five heart emojis.

‌



A statement from Buckingham Palace also announced the birth, saying Eugenie's uncle the King was 'delighted'. It said: "Her Royal Highness Princess Eugenie and Mr Jack Brooksbank are delighted to announce the safe arrival of their daughter, born on Monday, 3rd August 2026, at 6.20pm, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

‌



Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades READ MORE :

6 View 6 Images Eugenie's pregnancy announcement in May with sons, August and Ernest (Image: PA Wire) 6 View 6 Images Jack Brooksbank with the couple's two sons, August and Ernest (Image: Instagram)

"The baby was born weighing 6 pounds 9 ounces. Their Majesties the King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

Eugenie and Jack split their time between the UK and Portugal, with Jack's job based out there. It is understood they are deeply grateful to the hospital staff for their care and are taking time to decide on a name for their daughter while spending time with sons, August and Ernest.

‌



The new baby, who is not an HRH and will not receive a royal title, is born 15th in line to the throne, with their great uncle Prince Edward, the Duke of Edinburgh, now moving down to 16th place. The infant is also the 15th great-grandchild of the late Queen Elizabeth II, and the third to be born since her death in 2022.

The new arrival is also the fifth grandchild of Mr Mountbatten-Windsor and his former wife Fergie, the former Duke and Duchess of York, after the birth of their older daughter Princess Beatrice’s second daughter Athena Mapelli Mozzi in January last year.

Eugenie revealed her third pregnancy back in early May when an official announcement came from Buckingham Palace, which added that the King was 'delighted' at the news. At the time, the princess and the Palace shared a sweet snap of her two sons looking down at a print of an ultrasound.

‌



View 6 Images Eugenie with husband Jack, sister Princess Beatrice and brother-in-law Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi and Peter and Harriet Phillips' wedding in June (Image: Ben Birchall/PA Wire)

The princess posted on her Instagram page: “Baby Brooksbank due 2026!” followed by a series of red heart emojis and one of a baby. While in a statement, Buckingham Palace said: “Her Royal Highness Princess Eugenie and Mr Jack Brooksbank are very pleased to announce that they are expecting their third child together, due this summer.

“August (aged five) and Ernest (aged two) are also very excited to have another sibling join the family. His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news.”

‌



Before welcoming their children, Eugenie and husband Jack tied the knot back in 2018 in a grand wedding at Windsor Castle - just months after the nuptials of her cousin Prince Harry and Meghan Markle.

View 6 Images Eugenie and Jack married in 2018 (Image: Getty)

Guests at the wedding included the late Queen, the Prince and Princess of Wales and celebrities including Robbie Williams and Ellie Goulding.

‌



Jack was educated at Stowe private school in Buckinghamshire and went straight into a career in hospitality. He worked at London nightspots Mahiki and Peyote, before landing a job at Chelsea’s Tonteria with the help of Guy Pelly - businessman and close personal friend of Princes William and Harry. He's also been the European brand director of Casamigos Tequila, which is owned by Hollywood actor George Clooney.

The baby's birth comes just weeks after Eugenie and her sister Beatrice were seemingly brought in from the cold to join the Royal Family at the wedding of their cousin Peter Phillips - following revelations about their parents.

View 6 Images Eugenie with sister Beatrice and father, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. Eugenie's baby daughter is a fifth grandchild for the former Duke of York (Image: Getty Images Europe)

‌



They had previously stayed away from the traditional royal gathering on Easter Sunday, with the agreement of Charles, amid the furore over their father, who was arrested in February. They also did not attend Royal Ascot this year, at which they are usually regulars, or other summer events such as Wimbledon.

They also came under more scrutiny when it emerged that neither of them personally pay rent for their London homes with royal palaces.

Article continues below

The National Audit Office published a report into the royal family’s residential property arrangements after controversy surrounding the disgraced former prince Andrew's lease of the Crown Estate home.

Other findings by the public spending watchdog include the revelation that the King foots the bill for Beatrice and Eugenie's accommodation in royal palaces despite both Andrew’s daughters being non-working royals.

News.title: Firefighters face huge flames as they deal with wildfire near Athens
News.content:
Firefighters face huge flames as they deal with wildfire near Athens

The record-breaking hot and dry summer tightened its grip today with wildfires still raging in areas of Greece and France.

Europe's Wildfires Hit Greece & Turkey

The record-breaking hot and dry summer tightened its grip today with wildfires still raging in areas of Greece and France.

‌



Europe is Earth’s fastest-warming continent, heating at more than twice the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Union’s Copernicus climate service.

‌



Rising temperatures and prolonged drought leave vegetation drier and more combustible, allowing fires to spread faster.

‌



The wildfires west of Athens jumped containment lines a day after a midair collision between two helicopters killed two crew members.

A British national working for the Greek firefighting service survived the crash.

He was set to be released from a local hospital this week after making a good recovery from the accident.

‌



View 2 Images Firefighters tackle a blaze which continues to rage in Greece (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Tragedy as Brit mum-of-three dead after becoming trapped in raging Spain wildfires READ MORE :

In France, firefighters near Bordeaux guarded against potential flare-ups inside a still-burning scar four times the size of Paris.

The Athens region remains at high risk with hundreds evacuated. Strong winds returned to southern Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway.

‌



Areas surrounding the Greek capital remain at high risk through the week with temperatures set to rise further.

View 2 Images Firefighters work to extinguish a wildfire raging for four days in the Megara Region, west of Athens (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

More than 1,000 people have been evacuated from around the seaside resort of Porto Germeno and other areas west of the capital, including more than 250 rescued by boats from beaches in the area.

‌



“This is a difficult fire that has troubled us,” Fire Service spokesman Yiannis Artopios said, adding that 12 water-dropping planes and 11 helicopters were operating in the area.

The blaze was blamed on a faulty power line from a wind farm, leading to the arrests of two contractors on charges of negligent arson.

Authorities say 33 people were arrested from June 29 to Aug. 2 for starting fires, including 30 through negligence and three on suspicion of arson.

Article continues below

Most of the negligence cases involved farm work carried out despite local bans, including prohibited welding.

From first light today, crews were working against the clock. Winds typically pick up in the afternoon. The army deployed tracked earth movers to carve fire breaks across the scorched hillsides. Specialist units pushed into forest areas on foot to extinguish embers before they could reignite.

News.title: B&Q issues urgent fan recall during heatwave amid 'electric shock and fire' warning
News.content:
B&Q issues urgent fan recall during heatwave amid 'electric shock and fire' warning

Customers should stop using the nine-inch Kingfisher table fan, sold at B&Q, 'immediately' and request a refund for the faulty appliance

View 2 Images The fans were sold in B&Q between March and July (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

B&Q has recalled one of its table fans due to a potential fire risk, asking customers to stop using their appliances "immediately".

‌



As England and Wales continue to battle scorching temperatures, the home improvement giant has identified a potential safety issue with its White 9 Inch Table Fan. The appliance, made in China, was sold between March and July this year.

‌



In its notice about the 30W fan, B&Q said: "A potential safety issue has been identified in relation to the White 9 Inch Table Fan sold between March 2026 and July 2026. In some cases, an electrical component may overheat leading to a fire or electric shock risk.

‌



"If you think you have this product, please stop using it immediately and return to your nearest B&Q store for a refund."

View 2 Images The notice posted by B&Q (Image: B&Q)

‌



The Office for Products and Safety Standards, the UK's national regulator for consumer products, construction products and measurement standards, has also issued a notice about the faulty product. It reads: "The product presents a risk of electric shock and fire as there is a fault within the oscillation mechanism that can damage internal wiring.

"The product does not meet the requirements of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016." The recall comes as the whole of Wales and half of England remain in drought.

Last week, drought was declared across seven areas in England. These are East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Hampshire & the Isle of Wight, Devon & Cornwall, The West Midlands and Wessex.

Article continues below

In Wales, July is set to be the driestsince records began 190 years ago. Natural Resources Wales explained that the country only got 8 per cent of its long-term average rainfall throughout July.

News.title: Afghan boxer arrested in Greece over discovery of Scottish woman's body in suitcase
News.content:
The man suspected of killing Scottish aid worker Elisabeth Jane Ross in Greece is 26-year-old Sharif Ahmadzai, the BBC understands.

He was arrested after the body of the 38-year-old was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, several days after she was reported missing.

Ahmadzai, who was born in Afghanistan and is a champion boxer, settled in Greece after travelling there as a teenager.

Both Ross and Ahmadzai had worked with refugees and Greek police are investigating whether the pair knew each other through the charity sector.

Ahmadzai was arrested on suspicion of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences, and is expected to appear in court in Athens on Wednesday.

Police said the coroner's initial report failed to determine a cause of death, but more detailed examinations concluded it was an "obvious criminal act, likely asphyxiation".

News.title: Top Fifa official Wenger says scrapping World Cup plan 'absolutely necessary'
News.content:
Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says scrapping the plan to have private investment in Fifa competitions was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Fifa president Gianni Infantino planned to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, with external investors able to buy stakes.

Infantino had offered Fifa's 211 member associations $40m (Â£30m) each if they backed the proposal.

But after days of criticism - including Uefa's 55 nations threatening to boycott all Fifa tournaments - Infantino was forced to withdraw the plan.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from world football's governing body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to baby girl in Portugal
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has given birth to a baby girl at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

The baby was born on Monday at 18:20 BST, weighing 6lbs 9oz.

This is Princess Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, following the births of her sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, who was born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, who was born in 2023.

A statement from Buckingham Palace read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

In a post on Instagram, the princess, 36, wrote: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

"We are beyond in love with our girlie."

They are yet to announce a name.

The new arrival - who will not be an HRH - will be 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of their great-uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

The couple live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

They announced Princess Eugenie's pregnancy in May. She posted a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

The Palace said on social media at the time: "His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news."

News.title: Bono, Eddie Vedder and Hozier among mourners at Glen Hansard's funeral
News.content:
Stars from the world of music including U2's Bono, Pearl Jam's lead singer Eddie Vedder, and Hozier, attended the funeral of Glen Hansard on Tuesday.

The 56-year-old Oscar-winning Irish singer and songwriter died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin last week.

Hansard, who shot to prominence in 1991 musical comedy film The Commitments, was long-time frontman of acclaimed rock band The Frames.

News of his sudden death shocked the music world and fans alike, with tributes being paid from the likes of Ed Sheeran and Bruce Springsteen, who said he was "heartbroken".

News.title: Justice secretary apologises to families affected by early release scheme
News.content:
Justice Secretary Alex Norris has apologised to families affected by the early release scheme, saying they were "carrying the can from previous failures".

Families, including a man whose pregnant partner died after being hit by a speeding driver, criticised the prisoner early release scheme, saying it comes "at the expense of victims".

Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales. The prime minister said he wanted to exclude more, but prison overcrowding prevented this.

Calvin Buckley said he was "shocked and disappointed" the killer of his partner and unborn child could be released early.

The mother of PC Andrew Harper also said she was "devastated" to learn two men jailed after her son was killed will still be eligible.

The prime minister said making more prisoners exempt was not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris later said he spoke to the families as "it is really important to express that this shouldn't be where it is".

He also said he was confident the prisons would have adequate room now that about 1,000 extra prisoners will not be released early.

"We have modelled it very carefully," he said.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice confirming that two of the offenders could be included in the early release scheme.

While the driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter could apply for early release after serving half of their sentences.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

But last month the prime minister promised to "review the policy" and paused the scheme after a backlash from survivors.

Announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam, told BBC Newsnight: "It feels like we're letting Andrew down again" to hear his killers might still be eligible for release.

"We've been through the justice system, we thought we'd done as best as we could.

"Now we're standing up to fight again... so I just feel really let down, for Andrew's sake as well as ours."

She added that Norris had called her to explain the situation and apologise.

Later, on BBC Breakfast, Adlam called for more support from the probation service, stressing: "I need to know at the very, very least if they are going to be released that we're kept in mind of what's happening and we are informed".

Other families have also criticised the early release scheme.

Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough and unborn child died in May 2023.

"Our justice is being taken away, I understand there's a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," he told BBC Breakfast.

News.title: Scottish exam pass rates rise as students find out results
News.content:
Pass rates for Scottish exams have increased as students across the country received their results.

More than 148,000 learners have been finding out the results of their Nationals, Highers, Advanced Highers and Skills for Work Awards.

Qualifications Scotland - which replaced the Scottish Qualifications Authority last year after a number of controversies - said a record number of vocational and technical qualifications were awarded.

Figures show that the poverty-related attainment gap has narrowed compared with last year.

Admissions service Ucas said a record number of Scottish students aged 18 and under had been accepted into university or college. In total, 32,370 Scottish students of all ages secured places, up from 31,850 in 2025.

News.title: Athletes go 'missing' after Commonwealth Games ends
News.content:
Several athletes have disappeared after competing in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, failing to return home with the rest of their teams.

Police Scotland said it had received reports of various athletes "unaccounted for" in the aftermath of the Games, which concluded on Sunday.

The sports website NBS Sport, external said four members of the Ugandan boxing squad had not turned up to fly home, adding that one member of the team had told the website the athletes intended to seek asylum in Scotland.

Pakistan Today also reported, external that the boxer Qudratullah had not joined the rest of his team mates in flying home to Pakistan, and that he was not found in his room when officials went to search for him.

News.title: Surgeon struck off after wrongly connecting organs
News.content:
A doctor who botched an operation so badly it was described as "not compatible with life" has been struck off the medical register.

Dr Yasser Adly Abdel Rahman, an NHS locum surgeon from Egypt, carried out the flawed emergency bowel procedure on a young man.

It meant the contents of the patient's bowel, leaving his stomach, were re-deposited back into his stomach through a circular "closed loop", the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) heard.

The patient was left in "uncontrollable pain" and could have died but for another surgeon correcting the error in a second operation, the misconduct hearing, sitting in Manchester, was told.

Rahman at no time considered that something may have gone wrong surgically, the tribunal heard, despite the patient's parents and other medics expressing concerns.

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

Natasha Finch was diagnosed with an aggressive breast cancer at just 23 despite having no known risk factors.

She has since become an advocate for breast cancer awareness and wants young women to take symptoms seriously.

"I'm six years on and still here, still winning. Going to the GP was scary, but I'm so glad I went when I did â because if I hadn't, who knows?"

"I just want to advocate for girls."

This study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.

News.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
News.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

Seventeen-year old Lily-Mae from Blackpool told the BBC the move would save her "a few hundred [pounds] a year".

She uses the train to travel regularly from Blackpool North to Preston and Manchester.

"I have been planning to see my boyfriend and my friends, and it's just not really happened because of the price of the trains," she said.

"Also getting to college for me is hard as I go to a college in Preston, but I live in a different town, so now I won't have to save as much money to get there."

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of Â£175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs Â£35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The government said the measure would be paid for through increased train ridership, with more passengers as a result of more people being able to access the discounted fares.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from Â£3 to Â£2 next year.

News.title: Boy, 14, dies after going into water at dock
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has drowned after going into the water at a dock in east London.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) and the Metropolitan Police searched the Millwall Outer Dock near East Ferry Road after being alerted at about 18:50 BST on Monday.

His body was recovered at about 22:30 and he was pronounced dead at the scene. His family have been informed, police said.

In a post on social media, Mayor of Tower Hamlets Lutfur Rahman named the teenager as Banta Sillah and said he was "a talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week".

The Met Police has not confirmed the identity of the boy.

The mayor said Banta "had immense potential and was dearly loved by his peers".

He added: "As we mourn Banta, I urge families to speak with children and young people, we should all be aware of the dangers swimming in open water.

"Swimming should only take place in officially designated areas with lifeguards present."

News.title: Campaigners denied appeal over Gatwick expansion
News.content:
In a 29-page ruling, they said: "We conclude that each of the grounds of appeal raised by each appellant is unarguable.

"Neither appeal has a real prospect of success. We also consider that there are no other compelling reasons for either appeal to be heard."

The two senior judges also said that the previous ruling was "detailed and thorough".

Gatwick is the UK's second busiest airport and one of the busiest single-runway airports in the world.

The expansion will allow the site to be used for the departures of narrow-bodied planes such as Airbus A320s and Boeing 737s.

Following the decision, Barclay said: "We are very disappointed with the Court's decision. We took this challenge as far as we could because we believed that the decision to allow Gatwick to expand was fundamentally flawed.

"It was not supported by government policy, would only serve to line the pockets of the airport and airlines, and would do so at the expense of local residents and the climate."

Cagne said: "Residents should be immensely proud of what they have achieved in holding Gatwick Airport's shareholders to account.

"This proposed new runway will come at a significant cost to both the taxpayer and the planet."

News.title: Star Wars dubbed in Welsh for the first time to celebrate landmark anniversary
News.content:
Star Wars is to be dubbed into Welsh for the first time as the classic film prepares to celebrate its 50th anniversary next year.

Welsh language broadcaster S4C and Creative Wales announced the project, in partnership with Lucasfilm and Disney, at the National Eisteddfod on Tuesday.

The Welsh language version of Episode IV - A New Hope will broadcast on S4C and its platforms from Christmas Day.

Actor Matthew Rhys will voice Han Solo, with Rhys Ifans as Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Princess Leia.

Star Wars veteran Mark Lewis Jones, who portrayed Captain Moden Canady in Episode VIII - The Last Jedi, will take on the role of Darth Vader and Osian Morgan will voice Luke Skywalker.

Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd is directed by Ellyn Stern and produced by Michael Kohn, director of distribution operations at Lucasfilm.

"We're really excited about this project for many reasons," Kohn said.

"I've been involved in a few indigenous dubs of Star Wars over the years that aim to preserve and revitalise interest in learning the language.

"The chance to celebrate the Welsh language through Star Wars is one we couldn't pass up."

News.title: Ex neo-Nazi activist selected as Tory candidate
News.content:
A man who was jailed over his neo-Nazi activism will stand as a Tory candidate in council elections after being offered a "second chance" by the party.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally and a year later he was also convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Luciana Berger.

Bonehill-Payne has been selected to stand in the new Somerset Council seat of Crewkerne South in 2027. He said he wanted to "give back" to a community which had supported him.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said he had "shown contrition for his crimes" but the Board of Deputies of British Jews said the move "beggars belief".

News.title: 'Rape list' part of misogyny girls face at school
News.content:
A group of teenage girls have said they feel "worthless" and "frightened" as a result of the extreme misogyny they regularly experience.

The students, from Tyneside, have spoken out after making a film about the language they endure at school and online.

Many comments are too explicit to share, but they include threats of violence and rape often masked as "banter". One girl described how disturbed she had been after a "rape list" was made by boys in her school.

The government said it was "taking bold and decisive action to halve violence against women and girls", with changes being introduced from September to help teachers challenge misogyny.

The North East has the highest rate of violence against women and girls in England and charities warned unchallenged attitudes could lead to abuse in early relationships.

Misogyny is defined as a contempt for, hatred of or prejudice against women.

One girl told the BBC she felt "worthless" after learning of the "rape list" made by boys in her school.

"Boys ordering girls, who they want to rape the most and then the least," she explained.

"It is frightening because you don't know people's real intentions."
