A vegan diet may not be for everyone but a new small study revealed how forgoing animal products for even just a few weeks could slow the signs of aging.

There was also changes in the immune system tied to reduced inflammation, according to researchers in California and Germany, after people went vegan for a month.

Inflammation is the body’s natural reaction to injuries and germs but it can also be harmful to health longer term. Inflammation raises the risk of cancer and other diseases and drives accelerated aging in our cells, increasing the likelihood we die prematurely.

“Our study adds to growing evidence that nutrition can shape biology at the molecular level,” Dr. Max Storz, from University of Freiburg Medical Center and co-senior author of the study, explained in a statement.

Just one percent of Americans identified as vegan in 2024, according the most recent Gallup on the issue.

open image in gallery ‘Our study adds to growing evidence that nutrition can shape biology at the molecular level,’ researcher says ( AFP/Getty )

‘An important foundation’

There were two key findings in the research: a vegan diet altered DNA methylation gene patterns and two epigenetic clocks used to determine a person’s biological age suggested the diet could decelerate that process.

“DNA methylation” sounds complicated but the idea is simple. The term refers to the process that regulates whether certain genes are more or less active. More active genes determine our physical traits, such as eye and hair color and how we respond to health problems.

DNA methylation also determines if we have higher or lower amounts of neutrophils, which are immune cells that drive inflammation.

Examining this process using blood samples from nearly 50 adults - half meat-eaters and half vegans who both consumed similar calories each day - revealed people on the vegan diet would likely have lower amounts of neutrophils.

These individuals would also have higher amounts of CD4 T cells - a type of white blood cell that helps regulate immune response.

The study also examined participants’ biological age based on their DNA methylation, finding that biochemical tests - also known as epigenetic clocks - suggested the diet could decelerate that aging.

Further research is needed to confirm the results and determine whether the changes the researchers observed could help indicate reduced disease risk.

“The next step is to understand whether these epigenetic changes persist over time and whether they translate into meaningful improvements in long-term health. That will require larger clinical studies, but these findings provide an important foundation,” said Storz.

Processed pain

The study builds on years of past research showing a plant-based diet can lead to a healthier life - though highly processed vegan junk food can be bad, too, according to the American Heart Association.

People with diets heavy in fruit, veggies, nuts and less red and processed meats had an 86 percent greater chance of healthy aging at age 70, a 105,000-person study from Harvard researchers last year showed.

open image in gallery Hot dogs and other processed meat are tied to harmful inflammation that raises the risk of heart disease ( AFP/Getty )

Whereas, a red meat-heavy diet - especially processed meat, such as bacon or hot dogs - has long been tied to inflammation that increases the risk of heart disease.

“There have been innumerable studies that show a connection between eating red meat, getting heart disease and dying from heart disease,” Cleveland Clinic cardiologist Dr. Dennis Bruemmer said in a statement earlier this year. “It’s remarkably consistent.”

Some sources of animal protein are healthier than others, according to experts.

Those include white-meat poultry, fish, pork tenderloin, lean cuts of beef, eggs and non-fat or low-fat dairy products, according to Razan Hallak, a registered dietitian at The Ohio State University.

A well-balanced diet is still recommended for most people. That means variety, registered dietitian Paige Welsh told the Clinic.

“At its core, a balanced diet isn’t about picking and choosing ‘best’ foods or focusing on ‘superfoods.’ It’s about eating a range of nutritious, whole foods,” she said.

Princess Eugenie has announced the birth of a baby girl.

Eugenie, who is married to Jack Brooksbank, made the announcement on her Instagram page on Tuesday.

The birth took place at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, on Monday evening, Buckingham Palace said.

This is the couple’s third child, following sons August and Ernest, and it is understood they are taking time to decide on a name.

In a short post, Eugenie, who is the daughter of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, wrote: “Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!”

“We are beyond in love with our girlie.”

The birth is a rare occasion where a member of the royal family has been born overseas, with Eugenie and Mr Brooksbank having a home and other connections in Portugal.

Buckingham Palace said: “Her Royal Highness Princess Eugenie and Mr Jack Brooksbank are delighted to announce the safe arrival of their daughter, born on Monday August 3 2026, at 6.20pm, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

“The baby was born weighing 6lb 9oz.

“Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of the royal family were delighted to be informed of the news.”

The new arrival will be the fifth grandchild of the former Duke and Duchess of York, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson, after the birth of Princess Beatrice’s daughter Athena Mapelli Mozzi in January last year.

open image in gallery Princess Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank ( PA )

The happy family news is in stark contrast to Andrew’s fall from grace over his friendship with the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Earlier this year the former duke left his Windsor home after a public outcry about his “peppercorn rent” and moved to the Sandringham estate, and he was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office before being released.

Eugenie and Beatrice, who are granddaughters of the late Queen Elizabeth II, have faced scrutiny themselves after their names appeared in the Epstein files, the US Department of Justice’s document dump relating to the late convicted sex offender.

One email exchange suggested their mother Sarah took her daughters to see Epstein in the US days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes.

Eugenie and Beatrice were 19 and 20 at the time.

The sisters stayed away from the traditional royal gathering on Easter Sunday, with the agreement of Charles, amid the furore over their father.

It is not known at which hospital the baby was delivered but the couple are said to be deeply grateful to medical staff for their care.

Eugenie and Jack will be taking time to decide on the name of their new daughter while they enjoy time as a family.

The baby girl will not be an HRH, and is 15th in line to the throne, with her great uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, moving down to 16th place.

She will also be the 15th great-grandchild of the late Queen, and the third to be born since her death in 2022.

The pregnancy was announced in May with Eugenie sharing on Instagram a picture of her young son Ernest, wearing a Chelsea football kit, and her other child August, wearing a long-sleeved grey T-shirt, holding a picture of a baby scan.

A divided federal appeals court on Tuesday said the Trump administration improperly terminated billions of dollars in funds to boost clean energy projects, handing a win to a coalition of nonprofits picked to run the Biden-era effort.

Climate United Fund and other nonprofits won’t have access to their funds immediately as the decision will be put on hold for several days giving the Environmental Protection Agency time to ask the Supreme Court to step in.

The closely divided ruling by the full U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia is a loss for the Trump administration in one of its earliest efforts to dismantle President Joe Biden’s campaign to reduce climate-warming greenhouse gases. The Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, commonly referred to as a “green bank,” is a $20 billion congressionally authorized program that provided money to nonprofits that would then make loans and invest in small energy projects, energy-efficient buildings and transportation.

EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin accused Climate United Fund and other nonprofits picked to run the green bank of mismanagement and potential fraud. He froze billions that had been placed in a Citibank account for the program and then terminated their grants. The groups disputed any wrongdoing and sued, arguing the Trump administration broke the law and violated the Constitution by not spending money authorized by Congress.

“Despite efforts to harm the awardees with false allegations and misinformation, there remains no legal basis for terminating our grant award and clawing back funds that were already disbursed in our bank accounts,” Climate United Fund said in a statement.

In September, a divided three-judge panel of the same appeals court overturned a lower court and said the Trump administration had broad power to cancel grants without having to face charges of illegality in federal court. The full appeals court agreed to revisit that decision, a rare occurrence reserved for the most important cases.

The green bank was created by the Inflation Reduction Act. President Trump’s tax and spending bill last year, however, repealed part of the law that established the bank and rescinded money that hadn’t already been obligated to its recipients. That added a layer of complication.

Six of 10 judges agreed with a lower court judge that the EPA likely violated the law when it terminated the grants and tried to claw back funds based on a policy disagreement. This would likely contradict the law's direction to spend money on the program, they said.

Zeldin early last year told Fox News that he suspected the green bank “was a clear-cut case of waste and abuse” that “in my opinion, is criminal.”

The EPA did not immediately provide comment.

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan last year said that when the federal government was asked for evidence of fraud, the agency didn’t provide it and shifted its position to more general concerns about the level of EPA oversight over the program. Chutkan ruled the government can’t violate the law and terminate the contracts and that the groups should have access to some of their frozen money. That order was put on hold during appeal.

A lawyer for the nonprofits argued that the agency had already allocated the money by putting it in the Citibank account for the program’s use.

The agency argued the nonprofits are making constitutional and statutory arguments that don’t apply in a simple contract fight, and that the matter should be heard by a different court that can only award a lump sum — not force the government to keep the grants in place. Federal officials argue there is no law or provision in the Constitution that compels the EPA to make these grants to these groups.

The extension of the National Guard deployment in Washington, D.C. until January 2029 will cost roughly $1.4 billion, according to a Defense Department estimate provided to Congress.

The figure offers a glimpse of how much taxpayer money will be spent on a deployment that has been criticized by local officials as an infringement of their city's autonomy and by Democrats who say it has militarized the streets of nation's capital at the public's expense.

The cost estimate is for fiscal years 2027-2029 and came in response to questions from Massachusetts Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren and was provided to The Associated Press.

The deployment began last summer, when President Donald Trump issued an emergency order that launched a law enforcement surge in the city which the administration says was meant to fight crime. Hundreds of armed Guard troops have been deployed to city streets, supporting arrest operations but also helping with snow removal and carrying out beautification projects. This summer, as the city marked the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, their numbers surged to about 5,000.

The Defense Department said in its estimate the cost assumes there will be an average of 2,500 National Guard members in Washington through January 2029.

"While American families are getting flattened by skyrocketing costs, Donald Trump is spending $1.4 billion to keep troops on the streets in Washington for years on end," Warren said in an emailed statement. "The National Guard are not pawns and taxpayer dollars are not a piggy bank for Trump’s political stunts.”

The cost was first reported by The Washington Post.

The Pentagon said last month the Guard mission will continue until Jan. 20, 2029, “or until terminated by the President.” The deployment was set to expire at the end of this year after previously being extended.

While the use of National Guard members has been restricted by courts elsewhere, their presence continues in large numbers in D.C. where the president is the direct commander of the D.C. Guard.

What's not clear is whether the governors will extend their state units for more than two years. As of late July there were 4,600 military personnel from D.C. and 23 states and territories still in the city, some sent to help with security and other functions as part of events around July 4th.

One state, Georgia, had roughly 800 personnel here, more than the D.C. National Guard. Maj. R. Dustin Cole, spokesperson for the Georgia Air National Guard, said in an email the increased number is temporary. He stopped short of saying how many Georgia troops might be pulled away, and when.

Col. Joel Lynch of the Arkansas National Guard said about half of the state’s 238 soldiers in D.C. will return home the end of this month and 123 are projected to return near the end of October.

Hawaii said it will bring home its 27 members later this month after the Freedom 250 Grand Prix. Louisiana will have about 150 Guard members in the city through January 2027.

Don and Donna Powell, residents of the city who split time between Washington and Texas, said the money being spent on the National Guard could be used for other necessities.

“They’re everywhere. They’re just hiding wherever it’s shady,” said Donna Powell, while attending a FreeDC protest Monday against the continued surge. The money being spent for them “could be spent on healthcare and food for families that need it and instead we’re wasting our money.”

Donald Trump Jr. paid his ex-fiancée, Kimberly Guilfoyle, $7.6 million for her share of their six-bedroom, 11-bathroom home in Jupiter, Florida, according to a deed record filed in Palm Beach County Monday.

The warranty deed for the former couple’s home, which they purchased together in 2021 for $9.7 million, was transferred into Trump Jr.’s name on July 25th. It comes more than a year and a half after Trump Jr. and Guilfoyle called off their engagement.

The Palm Beach Post was the first to report news of the deed transfer.

The 16,477 square-foot waterfront home sits on 1.18 acres of property in Admirals Cove, an exclusive neighborhood within a private golf course. It comes with an in-ground pool, a boat lift, a four-car garage, a spa and an elevator – among other luxuries.

In 2025, Palm Beach County estimated the home’s market value was $13.6 million.

open image in gallery Nearly two years after splitting, Kimberly Guilfoyle sold her share of a Jupiter, Florida, home co-owned with Donald Trump Jr back to the president’s eldest son ( AFP/Getty )

Trump Jr., 48, and Guilfoyle, 57, were together for roughly six years and purchased two homes together during that time, one in Jupiter and another in The Hamptons in New York. However, the two sold their Hamptons home in 2021.

While Trump Jr. and Guilfoyle were engaged for roughly four years, the two never wed. Shortly after the president was re-elected in 2024, Trump Jr. was spotted holding hands with Bettina Anderson, a Palm Beach socialite and influencer.

Trump Jr. married Anderson, 39, earlier this year in a private ceremony.

Meanwhile, Guilfoyle has taken a position in the Trump administration, being named ambassador to Greece. Guilfoyle’s signature on the deed warranty document, posted Monday, also contained a stamp from the U.S. Embassy in Athens – where she is now based.

However, there appears to be no bad blood between Guilfoyle and Trump Jr., as she told the New York Times earlier this year, “I’m happy for Don. I wish him, of course, all the best.”

open image in gallery The Jupiter, Florida, property owned by Donald Trump Jr has a market value of more than $13 million, according to property records from Palm Beach County ( Google Maps )

It’s unclear what Trump Jr. plans to do with the Jupiter property now. In June, the New York Post reported that the eldest Trump son was planning to sell the home, with the asking price starting at $30 million.

A source told the New York Post that there was some back and forth between Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. over the potential sale of the home.

As of now, the home is not on the market.

Should Trump Jr. choose to sell the house, he could be eyeing a move to the Prospect Park neighborhood of West Palm Beach. The Palm Beach Post reported in June that Trump Jr. may be the owner of an empty lot where he could build a new home for his family.

A Democratic senator lit into his Republican colleagues on the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday over their vote to advance the nomination of Todd Blanche to be Donald Trump’s attorney general.

Sen. Cory Booker gave a fiery performance before the committee as he derided how two Republican senators had given away their votes for “nothing” after Blanche rescinded an order directing the creation of a $1.776 billion “weaponization” fund by the Department of Justice — which many feared would be used to hand payouts to January 6 rioters.

The New Jersey Democrat noted that the fund could simply be created at a later time, through another order.

“This is ridiculous! We got nothing! No guarantees whatsoever that this slush fund can’t go forward.” shouted Booker, holding up a blown-up tweet showing a conservative supporter of Blanche making that exact argument. “Dear God, folks.”

“[Todd Blanche] is about Trump and not truth. He is about corruption and not the Constitution. He is about being Donald Trump's lawyer and not the people's lawyer,” an impassioned Booker said.

open image in gallery Sen. Cory Booker attacked Republican senators for taking the administration's word on the DOJ 'weaponization' fund ( Reuters )

“This is so deeply wrong. We will rue the day that we let this man have this much power under such a corrupt president,” said Booker as he announced his “no” vote on Blanche’s nomination in committee.

Blance was advanced through the Judiciary Committee shortly after on a 12-10 party line vote.

Two Republican senators on the panel, Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, were threatening to vote “no” over the creation of the fund as well as the terms of a settlement between the IRS and Donald Trump dictating that the president and his family businesses received total immunity from IRS audits and the potential resulting prosecution for financial crimes.

But both senators dropped their opposition Sunday night when Blanche, under pressure, agreed to rescind the order. The text of an agreement he released on X confirmed that the order was rescinded, but did not bar the agency from issuing related directives in the future.

“It's hard for me to say this as a plant-based guy, but where's the beef? Where's the beef?” quipped Booker, directing jabs at Tillis and Cornyn, who is from Texas.

open image in gallery Booker and other Democrats questioned why Republicans were taking Blanche at his word when Donald Trump still wants to see the fund established ( Getty )

Numerous senators including Booker pointed this out on Tuesday. They also attacked Blanche over his participation in the Justice Department’s response to demands for release of the Epstein files, including the interview he conducted with Epstein’s ex-girlfriend and accomplice, Ghislaine Maxwell.

"Ghislaine Maxwell is sitting in the lowest possible confinement after giving no information that helped us get one more investigation started and has been silent, and the man responsible for that we're about to make the attorney general of the US,” derided Booker. “This is farcical."

Booker went on to describe Blanche as the worst choice for attorney general by a president in history.

Blanche’s fate now rests on a full Senate vote, which the chamber may or may not hold this week before leaving for the August recess on Thursday or Friday. No GOP senators have come out and said that they will vote against his final confirmation yet, but the margins are narrower due to the ongoing absence of Sen. Mitch McConnell, who remains hospitalized.

Cornyn, addressing the holes Democrats say remain in the DOJ agreement with the Senate, told Blanche at the hearing that he expects the adminstration to live up to his word going forward.

"Given this agreement with Mr. Blanche, I expect the DOJ to live up to this in future litigation, and I will vote to advance him out of the committee today,” said Cornyn.

open image in gallery Cornyn said after the vote that there was 'nothing' he could do to 'rein in' Trump ( Getty )

Tillis, his holdout colleague, also said he’d vote for Blanche’s nomination even as he admitted that weaponization of his agency was growing worse under Trump’s second term.

“Maybe it's a little bit more intense in this administration than the last one,” said the North Carolina senator.

And Cornyn, after the hearing, gave a more revealing admission. Speaking to reporters, he insinuated that the deal he and Tillis secured was the extent of their ability to restrain the administration and the DOJ.

"There's nothing we could do to rein in the president when he says he likes the fund and he wishes it still exists,” he said. “But the fact of the matter is, it’s dead, and that’s all we could do under these circumstances.”

Both he and Tillis originally had said they were prepared to vote “no” on Blanche’s advancement from committee.

open image in gallery Tillis admitted during the vote that 'weaponization' of the DOJ was growing worse under Blanche ( Getty )

Republicans in both the House and Senate have complained about the fund and senators previously confronted Blanche over it at a tense lunchtime meeting of the GOP caucus in June. Top Republicans like Mitch McConnell have condemned its potential use to reward January 6 rioters, including those who got in violent fights with police during their assault on the Capitol and were later pardoned en masse by Trump after returing to office.

But the fund has picked up some supporters from Trump’s close loyalists, like House Judiciary Committee chairman Jim Jordan.

Booker, who ran for president in 2020, is once again being looked at as a potential contender for the Democratic nomination in 2028 as the party eyes the next election cycle with cautious excitement.

In a March 2026 interview, he said he was “definitely not ruling out” a presidential run in 2028, but hadn’t made a decision yet.

News.content:

The devastating Eaton Fire in Los Angeles was caused by Southern California Edison equipment, fire officials said in a report released Tuesday.

Los Angeles County Fire officials found that the cause of the fire that killed 19 people and destroyed or damaged more than 9,000 homes and businesses in 2025 was a tower that was not in service, according to the report.

“After 18 months of thorough review of all evidence, alongside retained electrical and metallurgical experts, the investigation concluded that the cause of the wildfire conflagration was due to the electrical arcing events that took place on the out-of-service Southern California Edison (SCE) tower,” the agency said in a statement.

It took firefighters nearly a month to extinguish the blaze, which scorched 22 square miles (57 square kilometers).

Thousands of burned properties are seen following the Eaton fire in the Altadena area of Los Angeles County, California on January 21, 2025 ( AFP via Getty Images )

Kathleen Dunleavy, a spokesperson for Southern California Edison, said the utility has received the report and is reviewing it.

“We have taken our potential role in the start of this fire seriously from the very beginning,” Dunleavy said. She said SCE previously acknowledged “it was likely our equipment was associated with the ignition of the Eaton Fire.” She said the utility continues to support the community as it recovers.

SoCal Edison claimed in lawsuits earlier this year that Los Angeles County agencies failed to send timely evacuation warnings to residents in east and west Altadena. Eighteen of the 19 people who died in the fire lived in west Altadena.

The utility also has claimed water agencies, including Pasadena Water and Power, did not provide enough water as the fire spread, leaving firefighters with limited resources. Los Angeles County declined to comment about the latest court filings.

The Los Angeles County Arson Fire Investigation Unit jointly conducted the investigation with California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection or Cal Fire. It found electrical arcing on the utility’s out-of-service tower sparked the dry brush below and that the utility was responsible for maintaining and operating its electrical lines and equipment “in a manner that would minimize the risk of catastrophic wildfire posed by them.”

The blaze was sparked during extreme weather conditions that included high temperatures, low humidity and powerful winds. Two “electrical arcing events” occurred in quick succession, causing an unknown burning material to fall from the tower to the ground below, according to the report. Within 12 seconds, dry grass and brush was ignited and the fire swiftly developed “into a conflagration engulfing the areas of the San Gabriel Mountains, Altadena, Pasadena, Sierra Madre and La Canada Flintridge,” the report said. It took more than two weeks to fully contain the wildfire.

The Eaton Fire burned at the same time as the Palisades Fire, the most destructive blaze in Los Angeles to date and among the five worst in California’s history. The blaze killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 homes and buildings in Pacific Palisades as it ripped through hillside neighborhoods, destroying mansions with spectacular ocean views.

The man accused of sparking the Palisades Fire will be tried again this fall after his first federal arson case ended in a mistrial in June. Prosecutors said Jonathan Rinderknecht used a barbecue lighter on Jan. 1, 2025 to spark a blaze that burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up Jan. 7.

Ariana Grande is reportedly retreating from public life after intense scrutiny over her appearance and weight, with fans and celebrities insisting that she is too thin and drawing comparisons between her and Karen Carpenter, who was anorexic.

The ongoing obsession with the singer’s shrinking frame reached fever pitch with the release of her music video “Petal” on Friday [31 July]. It was announced today that Grande, 33, will “step back from visibility”, as soon as she gets off the stage of London’s O2, where she is due to perform 10-nights of her Eternal Sunshine Tour from 15 August to 1 September.

The singer will no longer be co-starring in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George that was due to open at London’s Barbican Centre next summer, alongside Grande’s Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey.

“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” her spokesperson told People magazine.

open image in gallery Author Charli Howard wrote a lengthy Instagram post condemning the pop star’s latest pop video ‘Petal’ ( Instagram )

It doesn’t take much reading between the lines to see that Grande has had enough of the body shaming, and is struggling under the constant obsession over her weight. In short, the Wicked star has been hounded out of public life over inappropriate comments – and it’s our fault.

Of course it is always worrying when somebody looks gaunt or loses a lot of weight, but a witch hunt doesn’t help anybody, and it’s not our place to label her as anorexic. We have no idea what is going on behind closed doors or what she is going through and criticism won’t help her.

Regardless, everybody is up in arms about her body weight, with worried fans taking to social media to vent their concerns:

“This is like looking at Karen Carpenter and everyone was like [shrug],” wrote one fan. Another wrote: “For the love of God, please eat something,” while a third person commented: “Her bones are literally popping out.”

It doesn’t take much reading between the lines to see that Grande has had enough of the body shaming, and is struggling under the constant obsession over her weight

And women who support women are piling it on the pop star too, with model, author and body positivity activist Charli Howard, who herself has suffered with an eating disorder, piping in with stark and scary warnings.

“What I see is someone in desperate need of hospitalisation and care, and while I know it’s often impossible to help someone at this stage of anorexia, there HAS to be an immediate intervention,” she posted to Instagram.

“I think it’s appalling ... to have released these videos and an album when this person needs psychiatric help and hospitalisation. The teams involved should be absolutely ashamed...”

Actor and presenter Jameela Jamil weighed in on the discussion with comments on Instagram that have now been removed, claiming that Grande is “possibly dying in front of us”.

open image in gallery Grande became very tearful when asked about maintaining beauty standards in an interview in 2024 ( Sally/YouTube )

Jamil, who has previously battled an eating disorder, criticised the fact Grande’s thinness was celebrated in the “Petal” video, and that her team didn’t guide her away from “this deeply damaging image for her young fans to see so glamourised”.

After receiving backlash for her post, Jamil defended herself on Instagram, explaining: “I said possibly. My god. And my point stands, that this is deeply irresponsible for all the people involved to deliver this aesthetic as glamorous to the many billions of girls and women consuming this imagery.”

I understand Jamil’s concerns, but female celebrities already face far too much scrutiny over their appearance. Grande is a role model to young women and girls – but she’s also a person in her own right, and it must be insufferable to have people commenting on your body 24/7. I understand it myself as I’ve yo-yoed from being overweight to underweight and back to normal, and have experienced people commenting on my weight the whole way.

We have no idea what is going on behind closed doors or what she is going through and criticism won’t help her

When I eventually lost three stone using weight loss drugs in 2024 after piling on the pounds with two pregnancies and developing an unhealthily high cholesterol level, I was scrutinised by mums at the school gate, with one asking me if I had a terminal illness and another offering to drive her electronic scales over to my house to watch me as I weighed myself. I found thin shaming is considered to be far more acceptable than fat shaming.

But no one deserves to be named and shamed for their body weight and to live under that sort of intense judgment. Grande has been incredibly vocal about how it feels to have people comment on her appearance, yet we choose not to listen to her and instead take the medical diagnosis into our own hands.

In her 2024 song, “Yes, And?”, the pop star addresses the scrutiny over her appearance, singing: “My face is sitting, I don’t need no disguise/ Don't comment on my body, do not reply. Your business is yours and mine is mine/ Why do you care so much whose – I ride? ‘Why?’”

And, that same year, Grande held back tears during an interview with Sally Poumbga on YouTube. The French reporter asked her how she copes with society’s “beauty standards” and the “overwhelming” pressure women feel “to always look perfect”. “I’ve been kind of doing this in front of the public and kind of been a specimen in a petri dish really since I was 16 or 17, so I have heard it all,” was Grande’s response.

The ex-Nickelodeon star said that it’s “hard to protect yourself from that noise” when you’re young. “I think that it’s something that is uncomfortable no matter what scale you’re experiencing it on,” she revealed, “even if you go to Thanksgiving dinner, and someone’s granny says, ‘Oh my God, you look skinnier! What happened?’ or ‘You look heavier! What happened?'”

open image in gallery The pop star has addressed the public’s relationship with her weight in songs and interviews ( Getty )

Grande first confronted issues surrounding her body weight in April 2023 when she was filming Wicked in London. She posted a TikTok video in which she urged others to be “gentler and less comfortable commenting on people’s bodies”.

“Personally for me, the body that you’ve been comparing my current body to was the unhealthiest version of my body,” Grande said directly at the camera in her trademark soft tone.

“I was on a lot of antidepressants, and drinking on them, and eating poorly, and at the lowest points of my life when I looked the way you consider ‘my healthy,’ but that in fact wasn’t my healthy”, she said.

Obviously we can’t be expected to live in denial that something isn’t right with Grande – and I’m not saying that people’s concerns aren’t coming from a place of love and care. But the barrage of attacks on her weight is counter-productive.

The people who are giving the advice and observations are strangers. We need to remember that she has friends and a very close and supportive family, specifically her mother Joan, her older half-brother Frankie, who shared on a podcast that Grande supported his sobriety by attending 12-step meetings with him around mid-2017 following the Manchester Arena bombing. It’s not as if she doesn’t know where help is should she need it, or be ready for it.

I can’t imagine the constant comments are helping her health. It’s time to stop pointing the finger

As she pointed out to Japan Vogue, however, she hasn’t had a break for 15 years – and clearly is oversubscribed with film and theatre roles, as well as her pop tour. The strain of living in a goldfish bowl of celebrity could be getting to her, along with the enormous pressure and onslaught of public scrutiny.

I can’t imagine the constant comments are helping her health. It’s time to stop pointing the finger because whether she is anorexic or not, it isn’t fair to subject her to such body shaming and judgment.

As Grande advised others dealing with body shaming in 2024: “You all can protect yourselves from that noise – whether it’s at a family reunion or online, if you gotta block people, I don’t care if you have to delete the app entirely – you keep yourself safe because no one has the right to say sh*t.”

Grande is true to her word – and what she is doing is blocking us all by stepping out of the limelight and finding some peace. She deserves it.

For anyone struggling with the issues raised in this article, eating disorder charity Beat’s helpline is available 365 days a year on 0808 801 0677. NCFED offers information, resources and counselling for those suffering from eating disorders, as well as their support networks. Visit eating-disorders.org.uk or call 0845 838 2040.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

Sports.title: Premier League club quietly increase stadium capacity ahead of new season as part of £40million redevelopment
Sports.content:
BRIGHTON have been giving the Amex Stadium a makeover ahead of the new season – leading to the capacity being increased.

The Seagulls are preparing to host Uefa Conference League action after sealing European qualification on the final day of last term.



Brighton, who allowed Danny Welbeck to join Chelsea last week, are set to face Romanian side CFR Cluj or Norwegian outfit Tromso in the play-off round later this month.

And they will now be able to welcome 800 more fans after quietly working on a £40million redevelopment project.



A new premium hospitality space, known as the 1901 Club, has been added to the North Stand.

It has resulted in the Amex Stadium’s capacity rising to 32,500 as the Seagulls prepare for their showdown with Aston Villa on the opening weekend of the 2026/27 season.



More changes are in the pipeline after Brighton chiefs have continued looking to improve facilities.

Plans have been made to expand the safe standing area to the lower rows of the North Stand.

It comes after the plan was initially announced by the Premier League side in January.

Construction work is scheduled to start during next month’s international break, meaning it will be ready for clashes in October.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A club statement read: “The club can confirm safe standing will be extended to the lower rows of the North Stand in September 2026.

“Following a review of the voting, safe standing is moving to lower rows but only in more central blocks where this had the most support.

“This may mean that sight lines are impacted for the seats situated immediately next to safe standing areas.

“For those supporters whose seats will be converted to safe standing, a priority window will be available to move elsewhere in the stadium.”



Away fans are also set to be relocated to the south-west corner of the arena at the end of the campaign.

It is the Amex Stadium’s biggest transformation since Brighton moved in 15 years ago.

Sports.title: Watch Lionel Messi and David Beckham’s Inter Miami and take luxury Caribbean cruise from just £1,479pp
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans can now score a sensational double deal to see the GOAT play for Inter Miami – and enjoy a luxury Caribbean cruise trip.

Our travel partners have come up with an incredible collection of cruise and stay travel packages that include tickets to see Lionel Messi‘s Inter Miami.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola’s assistant, 38, forced to join Liverpool training session with Reds facing defensive crisis
Sports.content:
ALARM bells over Liverpool’s scant squad depth have intensified after their assistant coach was forced to make up preseason numbers.

Reports that Iraola’s right-hand man Tommy Elphick had to double as a training ground centre-half epitomise the club’s current defensive crisis.



Plagued by personnel shortages, the Red’s recent tour of the US was far from the American dream.

Former Bournemouth captain Elphick hung up his boots after a 16-year playing career back in 2021, but had to pull on a training bib to fill Liverpool‘s defensive void.



Elphick’s presence in preseason is a stark manifestation of Liverpool’s lack of immediate options at the back.

Expectations of an exhilarating new era under Iraola’s intense pressing style were quickly dampened just eight minutes into the Basque’s reign when centre-back stalwart Joe Gomez limped off injured.

The Reds were already rife with defensive niggles when Gomez was sidelined in the 4-2 friendly win over Sunderland.

Despite signing two of the continent’s most promising centre backs last season, Liverpool’s attempt to future-proof their back line with Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni has been devastated by injuries.

Italian wonderkid Leoni suffered a freak ACL injury on a nightmare Anfield debut last September, and has been consigned to recovery ever since.

Meanwhile, a prolonged shoulder injury has hamstrung Jacquet, and Liverpool are yet to get a glimpse at £55 million worth of French talent.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Former Premier League player of the season Virgil van Dijk possesses indisputable class, but is past his very best at 35 and was absent from the America tour as he recuperates after the World Cup.

2024’s English champions have lost key bedrocks since tasting glory, with Ibrahima Konate and Trent Alexander Arnold both departing to the Bernabeu on free transfers.

With a string of stars either on the operating table or at new homes, Liverpool had to place 18-year-old Ifeanyi Ndukwe and 22-year-old Luke Chambers at the heart of their preseason defence.

While both showed flashes of brilliance, Chambers spent last season on loan in the Championship, and Ndukwe has been forced out on loan after failing to qualify for a work permit amid visa issues.



Liverpool’s makeshift defence was brutally exposed in a grisly second half against Leeds, with Daniel Farke’s men putting four past the Reds in 45 minutes in Chicago in their 4-2 victory.

Despite their bare bones back line, recent transfer speculation on Merseyside has centred around a potential £100million plus move for PSG’s attacking dynamo Bradley Barcola.

Sports.title: Former Subway worker who cycles to matches age 31 on brink of playing in Champions League after stunning rise
Sports.content:
A SWEDISH striker who worked at Subway until he was 24 faces Yaya Toure’s team for a place in the Champions League play-offs tonight.

Jacob Bergstrom will also travel on two wheels to the European clash between Swedish minnows Mjallby and 24-time Slovakian champions Slovan Bratislava.



The unconventional 31-year-old forward prefers a coastal cycle to Mjallby’s matches at the Strandvallen Stadium, situated next to a campsite and a mere 100 metres from the Baltic Sea.

When the former sandwich maker first signed for Mjallby, they were an obscure side in Sweden‘s third division.



Europe’s finest were a far cry for Bergstrom, who never managed to break into a youth academy and was stuck at amateur level even at 22.

Champions League glamour also seemed a faraway fantasy for Mjallby, who were on the brink of bankruptcy in 2016.



The team are based in the miniscule fishing community of Hallevik, which has a population of scarcely 1,000 people.

It has now become the second smallest place to hold a Champions League fixture in history.

Despite their village roots, Mjallby stunned Sweden‘s city-based elite and sent shockwaves throughout the footballing world by winning last season’s national championship.

They now hope to ink a new chapter in their seaside fairytale by beating the most successful club in Slovakian history.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Victory over former Champion’s League winner Yaya Toure‘s Slovan Bratislava would leave Mjallby just one tie away from facing the kings of the continent next season.

Whatever the outcome on the Swedish coast, the rural giant-killers are guaranteed a European stage in the Uefa Conference League.

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley owes huge debt to Newcastle as she fails to cut ties with ex-club ahead of proposed West Ham takeover
Sports.content:
EX-NEWCASTLE chief Amanda Staveley has failed to settle a £750,000 debt with her former club.

Staveley, leading a consortium to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham from the Gold family, has the outstanding six-figure loan with the Geordies.



Fresh paperwork for Redstart Leisure, the firm she used to buy and invest in Newcastle, shows that the debt hasn’t been settled within an agreed period.

Staveley also used the firm, which was previously called Cantervale Limited, for payments connected to advisory work for the club.



She placed it into voluntary liquidation in 2024 – however liquidators have revealed the debt remains outstanding.

Liquidators warned “the company would be unable to pay its debts in full within the period stated in the directors’ declaration of solvency.”



The loan from the club is described as an ‘unsecured trade and expense” debt.

In October 2024, she promised liquidators: “I Amanda Staveley, being the sole director of Redstart Leisure, have formed the opinion that this company will be able to repay its debts in full, together with interest, within 12 months. I make this solemn declaration believing it to be true.”

Staveley’s West Ham consortium contains private equity firm PCP Partners and is co-led by her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, who was also involved at Newcastle.

The consortium hopes to restore West Ham’s Premier League status and could even buy the London Stadium.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In 2024, Staveley was ordered to pay a Greek shipping magnate more than £3m after a high court legal battle.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘on brink of Pep Chavarria transfer with agreement set to be reached for Rayo star to travel for medical’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are on the brink of securing a deal with Rayo Vallecano to sign Pep Chavarria, according to reports.

And now the left-back is expected to be given permission to travel for a medical.



According to The Athletic, the Blues are closing in on sealing the terms for the transfer.

It is understood personal terms are already agreed between the Stamford Bridge club and the Spaniard.



Now it is a case of the final elements of the transfer terms being ironed out before the move can progress.

No hiccups are expected once the final fee has finally been decided upon.



Chavarria, 28, is under contract in Madrid until 2030 but does have a reported £42.8million release clause.

So that will pave the way for Chavarria to have his medical and be confirmed as the latest Blues signing.

Left-back is a major priority for Xabi Alonso.

The sale of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid left Jorrel Hato as the only recognised senior left-back at the club – although 18-year-old Landon Emenalo has featured in pre-season.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Alonso is keen for Chavarria to help both in their development – as well as being a direct replacement for Cucurella.

Chavarria joined Rayo Vallecano in 2022 and has played 125 times for the club, including in the Conference League final.

Rayo lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace in Leipzig.

Chelsea have already signed eight new players this summer – for more than £300m.

That includes a record £117m on Morgan Rogers and £52m on Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.



Jordan Henderson, meanwhile, arrived on a free from Brentford.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Blues out to exorcise infamous ghost on Sunday, shirt sponsor woes continue and Maignan transter update
Sports.content:
CHELSEA will have the chance to bury a few ghosts in Malaysia on Sunday.

Or one, at least.



Because the chief executive of local opponents Johor Darul Ta’zim is none other than former Liverpool star Luis Garcia.

The Spaniard scored what then Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho called the “ghost goal” at Anfield in May 2005 to decide a tense Champions League semi-final second leg.



In the fourth minute, Garcia jabbed the ball goalwards after Blues goalkeeper Petr Cech had brought down Milan Baros.

Although William Gallas cleared the effort, the near-side linesman ruled it had crossed the line.

Liverpool held on to secure a 1-0 aggregate win and went on to beat AC Milan in the final in Istanbul.

Garcia, now 47, spent many years as a TV pundit after hanging up his boots in 2016.

But in 2025, he agreed to take charge of Johor.

The club had been formed in 2012 in a radical revamp of football in the state of Johor, led by Crown Prince Tunku Ismail Idris, son of Malaysia’s ruling sultan.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Prince became the club’s owner in 2016.

Talks with Garcia were set up by fellow Spaniard Kiko Insa, who had become an agent after a journeyman career that ended at Johor.

Johor claimed Malaysia’s domestic Treble for the first time in Garcia’s first season in charge and have won the last 12 league titles.

But they lost in the quarter-finals of the AFC Champions League to reigning champions Al-Ahli.



And in goal for the Saudi side was Edouard Mendy, who was in Chelsea’s 2021 Champions League-winning side.

Sunday’s match at the Larkin Stadium is a chance for the Blues to gain some direct revenge over Garcia.

BLANK SLATE

IT is a year since Chelsea parted company with chief revenue officer Casper Stylsvig amid rows over the failure to secure a lucrative front-of-shirt sponsor.



But unless something happens very soon, the Blues will go into a new season for the fourth time under the current owners without a deal.

It is simply extraordinary that a big-name Premier League club, led by high-flying finance gurus, has “lost” tens of millions in revenue by not replacing previous long-term backer Three.

The mobile phone firm’s £40m-per-year contract ended at the conclusion of the 2022-23 season, the first year of the BlueCo regime.

Last season’s temporary fix was a deal with little-known AI firm IFS, which saw the company pay double-digit millions to have their name on the shirts from February until the end of the campaign.

IFS will continue as longer-term partners, but a blue-chip company willing to match the Blues’ demands remains elusive.



Chelsea are in a much weaker negotiating position than 12 months ago, when they had just won the Club World Cup and were preparing to return to the Champions League.

Even then, though, no-one was prepared to stump up the £60-65 million per year BlueCo wanted.

With no European football at all in 2026/27, the club cannot offer the same top-level visibility for a brand.

The Premier League ban on gambling firms being shirt sponsors has narrowed options for the Blues and other clubs.

Chelsea are not alone in lacking a backer barely two weeks before the new campaign begins, with Champions League participants Aston Villa among those still searching.



But fans remain frustrated the financial and commercial geniuses in charge of the club have still not secured a key source of revenue.

MIK DROP

CHELSEA have repeatedly denied any ongoing interest in AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan.

But if they have changed their mind again, then Saturday’s friendly in Jakarta between the two clubs would be a good chance to re-open talks.



Milan are said to be unconcerned about their captain recently deleting all mention of the club from his Instagram account, although you can never be sure of the truth in an era when social media makes kids out of grown adults.

Maignan himself is not due to be in Indonesia for the Chelsea game, as he and fellow France international Adrien Rabiot are not due to report back for pre-season until August 12, after their run to the semi-finals of the World Cup.

Mike Penders has joined up with the Blues in Hong Kong, though, after his own stint across the Atlantic.

Penders was Belgium’s No 3 ‘keeper behind former Chelsea star Thibaut Courtois and Manchester United’s Senne Lammens and remains uncapped after not playing a minute at the tournament.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Xabi Alonso will surely give Penders his club debut in one or more of the three remaining fixtures of the Asian tour.



Only then will Alonso be able to gain a better idea of whether he wants the club to go shopping for another ‘keeper or is willing to give Penders, back from loan at sister club Strasbourg, the chance to challenge Robert Sanchez.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club

Vito Mannone, the ex-Arsenal goalkeeper, signed for Crawley Town as a player-coach this summer and he's already been thrust between the posts by boss Colin Kazim-Richards

View 3 Images Vito Mannone made his first appearance in 18 months (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone kept a clean sheet to help new club Crawley Town beat York City 2-0 on Monday and reach the Carabao Cup first round proper. Mannone, 38, signed for the League Two side as a player-coach in June after spending last season as a free agent while earning his coaching badges.

‌



The Italian got the nod for Crawley's first game of the season, travelling to York's LNER Community Stadium in a preliminary round of the Carabao Cup. Mannone and his team-mates advanced thanks to goals from Gianmarco Di Biase and Danilo Orsi.

‌



The victory booked Crawley a trip to Watford this Saturday. It was Mannone's first competitive appearance since February 2025 with former club Lille.

‌



He was on Arsenal's books for eight years, making a total of 23 first-team appearances. Mannone left the Emirates in 2013 to join Sunderland for £2million, spending the next four seasons at the Stadium of Light before moving to Reading.

He then plied his trade in France after signing for Monaco in 2020, later joining Lorient and finally Lille. Crawley convinced Mannone to make the drop from the French top flight to the fourth tier of English football by handing him a dual role, with the 38-year-old having recently been coaching at Brighton.

‌



Mannone will head up Crawley's goalkeeping department, taking training sessions and leading player development. "I am delighted and proud to take on this role and can't wait to meet everyone at the club and to start working with the staff and players," he said.

"I'll give everything to the cause and hope to pass on my experiences as a player, leading into a successful season."

Crawley's manager, former Premier League striker Colin Kazim-Richards, explained: "To be able to add to my coaching staff, to the club, someone of Vito's calibre is a credit in itself.

"His knowledge, his footballing experiences, playing at the highest level with some of the best coaches in terms of standards, what it actually takes and ideas coming from a country that creates amazing goalkeepers, has really taken us up another level.

‌



View 3 Images Vito Mannone spent eight years at Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"Vito comes with an intensity, and it's something I'm looking forward to in terms of creating a relationship and benefiting from his skills from a goalkeeper's perspective, and also as a person. As soon as we spoke, I knew he was the right man, so I can't wait to work with him."

Sports.title: Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part
Sports.content:
Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part

The England captain will head back to his club in the next few days and Bayern will immediately resume talks over a new contract that will keep the striker in the Bundesliga beyond 2027

View 3 Images Harry Kane has had three very productive seasons with Bayern Munich (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Just over nine years ago, Harry Kane mildly surprised a small gathering of reporters when he declared winning the Ballon d’Or to be one of his prime ambitions. Nothing wrong with aiming high, of course. But, at the time, Kane was a 23-year-old striker who had made 17 appearances for his country and had scored five goals.

‌



His numbers with Spurs were very good - 78 goals in 113 Premier League appearances - but he had only been an established top-flight player for three seasons. But Kane believed in himself and lifting that Ballon d’Or is a realistic prospect when the awards ceremony, for the first time in its history, comes to London in October.

‌



Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bookmakers do not normally get these sorts of things wrong and every odds-maker has Kane as the favourite to become the seventh British player to receive the accolade. The influence of the World Cup, though, should not be under-estimated.

‌



Some of the 100 journalists who make the choice could well forgive Rodri an injury-interrupted and otherwise mediocre season with his club for his imperious role in Spain’s summer triumph. Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe would appear to be the only other realistic contenders.

And they are worthy contenders. If Kane does not win the 2026 edition, he will have the award in his sights for next year - a year with no major international tournaments.

And if he stays at Bayern Munich, goals are a guarantee. In three seasons in Germany, he has 146 in 147 appearances. If he moved to Barcelona - a switch that seems slightly fanciful but has been mooted reasonably strongly - goals would be a guarantee.

‌



View 3 Images Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and is a strong contender for this year's award (Image: Getty Images)

Kane is not coming back to the Premier League any time soon, we can be fairly certain of that. He will report back for training with Bayern after the Bundesliga champions have returned from a pre-season trip to Korea and Hong Kong on Saturday.

Contract talks will immediately resume, as his current deal expires in the summer of 2027. And quite frankly, it is hard to see why Kane would not want to extend his agreement.

‌



He could ask for a release clause at the end of next season if he feels he might have the urge to come back and break the Premier League goalscoring record - he is currently 47 short of Alan Shearer’s total of 260 - but he seems extremely content in Bavaria. Plus, the style of play, the quality of play, the guarantee of competing for honours on all fronts, are all factors that will help him stay in top shape for the international challenges that still lie ahead, most notably leading England into Euro 2028.

He turned 33 a week ago but Kane has looked a better, all-round player for his time in Munich. He was certainly more impressive for England at World Cup 2026 than he was at either Euro 2024 or World Cup 2022. He is not unusual but playing in a dominant team suits him.

View 3 Images Harry Kane has plenty of international challenges left despite his World Cup disappointment (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When he sits down with his advisers and the Bayern hierarchy in the next week, there will, of course, be no escaping the relevance of his age. But over the past few years, the longevity of marquee players - and of strikers, in particular - will have probably had a bearing on his plans.

Since his 34th birthday, Kane’s predecessor at Bayern, Robert Lewandowski, has scored 125 club goals. Kane could return to the Premier League as a 35-year-old - in two seasons’ time - and still fancy his chances of beating Shearer’s number.

But before then, he will have his eyes on another individual accolade. And if the Ballon d’Or does not come his way on the 70th anniversary of the award (the first one, in 1956, was won by Stanley Matthews, hence why the ceremony is in London), you can guarantee he will be a contender again if he stays at Bayern Munich. The Premier League and Shearer’s record are going to have to wait.

Anthony Taylor called time on his refereeing career last month, but he's already found a new position that will see him take his wealth of experience as a match official abroad

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor retired after 20-year refereeing career (Image: Ayman Aref/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Anthony Taylor has landed a new job in football just weeks after announcing his retirement from professional refereeing. The former Premier League match official has been appointed the director of elite refereeing for the Turkish Football Federation (TFF).

‌



Taylor, 47, hung up his whistle after his last match at this summer's World Cup, taking charge of Spain's 1-0 win against Portugal in the round of 16. But now he's back in football with the TFF.

‌



"I am delighted to be joining the Turkish Football Federation and very much looking forward to beginning this new role," Taylor said. "Elite refereeing has been at the centre of my professional life for many years, and this appointment gives me the opportunity to use that experience in a different way."

‌



His appointment comes 10 months after the conclusion of a five-year investigation which found that 371 of 571 match officials in Turkey had betting accounts. TFF president Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu stated at the time: "If we want to bring Turkish football to the place it deserves, we have to clean up whatever dirt there is."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Some of the clean-up job will be given to Taylor, who refereed 831 matches over a 20-year career. "I am excited by the Federation's ambitions for its match officials and by the opportunity to help shape the strategic and technical development of its refereeing programme," Taylor added.

‌



"There is already a great deal of talent and commitment within Turkey, and I look forward to working with colleagues across the Federation to build on those foundations and support the continued development of referees at every stage of the elite pathway.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor will bring his expertise to Turkey (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

"Retiring from elite refereeing was a significant decision, but I was always clear that I wanted to remain closely involved in the game and contribute to the future of officiating. This is an exciting opportunity to begin that next chapter, and I look forward to getting started."

‌



Taylor, from Altrincham, worked as a prison guard before becoming a professional referee. The 47-year-old suggested when announcing his retirement that the 'intense' pressure and 'constant' scrutiny had played a role in his decision.

In May 2023, Taylor and his family were harassed by Roma supporters at Budapest Airport following their Europa League final defeat to Sevilla and criticism from then-Roma manager Jose Mourinho. Taylor revealed last year that his family no longer came to watch matches that he refereed.
