Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's task at Chelsea: 46-player squad, baffling transfers and confusing hierarchy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso knew perfectly well what he was signing himself up for when he agreed to become the next Chelsea manager.

"I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," Alonso told reporters while on Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them.

"We had the same ideas, the same analysis, to start building momentum together. That is why we are taking these steps together and making decisions to build a good team."

We don't need to ask Alonso what view he had of Chelsea before he arrived, because the picture has been painted very clearly over the past few years. It is one defined by muddied thinking and a chaotic approach, which comes together to create the biggest circus in the Premier League.

‌



Alonso is only in the early stages of his Chelsea career and will obviously need time to stamp his authority on things and turn around a side which finished a lowly 10th in the Premier League last season. Yet, despite having the title of manager, rather than head coach, he will have to do so within the same parameters of his predecessors Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea sanctions reveal same punishment for sexual misconduct and ticket transferring READ MORE :

In the post-Roman Abramovich era, of which Todd Boehly has become the gormless face, Chelsea have become the most puzzling of entities where more confusion and baffling mismanagement is only around the corner. After all, this is a club that, defying convention, have five sporting directors.

It is a club, that at the time of writing, have 46 first-team players listed on their website. A club who have, despite their vast swathes of players, spent approximately £336million in the summer transfer window so far, with more no doubt to come.

‌



And a club which has, partly on Alonso's say-so, changed their youth-first transfer approach to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson.

View 4 Images Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea (Image: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC)

Welbeck's arrival means Chelsea currently have six senior strikers. Of them only Joao Pedro is assured of his position. Liam Delap, a £30m signing last summer, could be shipped out, Nicolas Jackson is looking for a new team after spending last season on loan at Bayern Munich and Marc Guiu is on the transfer list having been recalled from Sunderland last season due to injuries.

It is a muddled picture entirely in-keeping with Chelsea's modus operandi. Last summer, Maresca felt he had no other choice than to create a 'bomb squad', featuring the highly-paid group of Raheem Sterling, Axel Disasi, Joao Felix and Ben Chilwell.

‌



This summer it is Alonso who has the unenviable task of trying to work out which players he wants, which ones he doesn't and how to create some kind of squad unity amidst it all. Marc Cucurella may be gone after his frank criticism of the hierarchy, but senior players Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo - who both publicly flirted with rival clubs during the slide under Rosenior - remain.

View 4 Images Xabi Alonso has a tough task creating unity in such a fragmented squad (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

"You need the right balance of personalities and stages of maturity, with players in their early 20s, early 30s and everything in between," Alonso has said of his squad. Yet the list of new arrivals shows the complicated squad picture the Spaniard has inherited from owners BlueCo:

Geovany Quenda (Sporting CP, undisclosed), Denner (Corinthians, undisclosed), Dastan Satpaev (Kairat Almaty, undisclosed), Emmanuel Emegha (Strasbourg, undisclosed), Marco Palestra (Atalanta, £47m), Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa, £117m), Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace, £52m), Danny Welbeck (Brighton, £5m), Jordan Henderson (Brentford, free), Valentin Barco (Strasbourg, undisclosed).

‌



Good luck getting your head around that, Xabi. Oh, and your ranks have been swelled even further by the return from a doping ban of Mykhailo Mudryk, the Ukrainian winger who has not played competitive football since November 2024.

View 4 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has returned to bolster ranks that didn't need bolstering (Image: May JAMES / AFP via Getty Images)

Keeping everyone happy will be an impossible balancing act, given the lack of European football means fewer matches. Perhaps more so than any other elite club, Chelsea is a dog-eat-dog environment where team spirit has been sorely missing in recent years.

Off the pitch there are more factors to try and get your head around. The £10m fine a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows for historic off-the-books agent payments. The fact they are still yet to find a front-of-shirt sponsor, continuing their baffling commercial failure which stretches back to 2023.

‌



Yet, this being the ultimate club of contrasts, they have still splashed out six figures on a top-of-the-range private jet to whisk their players around during pre-season.

Chelsea have 20 days until their begin their Premier League campaign. The size of the task facing Alonso is such that it would be surprising if the picture appeared any clearer by then.

Sports.title: Why have Barcelona broken transfer records to sign Kerolin?
Sports.content:
It's been brief. Kerolin only joined the Women's Super League from the NWSL 18 months ago. She now leaves as the English top-flight's most expensive export.

Kerolin's £1.25m fee breaks record held by Olivia Smith's sale from Liverpool to Arsenal last summer. Barcelona were willing to smash their own transfer policy in pursuit of the Brazilian, too, having never previously paid a fee over £500k.

But Kerolin represents an exception to the rule. It's always been that way, from the start of her journey playing barefoot with boys on the streets of Sao Paulo. She was different. The ball hurt to kick, she confessed, but she did it anyway.

Image: Kerolin played a huge part in Man City winning their first WSL title for a decade in 2025-26

As such, there is perhaps an air of inevitability about the 26-year-old's switch to the four-time European champions. This is the path she expected to follow. "Always the most highly-ranked players are playing here or in Spain," she told Sky Sports upon signing for Man City in January 2025. "To be in the vision of the world."

She leaves a WSL champion.

Being considered among the game's most elite does not necessitate playing for Barcelona, but it helps. Each of the last five Ballon d'Or recipients were representing the Catalonia club at the time of winning the prize. Kerolin is now the team-mate of its current holder Aitana Bonmati.

Indeed, if Ballon d'Or is the mission Barcelona has proven the means. It's fertile ground for notoriety and success, with silverware almost guaranteed and the chance to star in a team undergoing reinvention under Pere Romeu. A summer of change has seen plenty of big names leave: Alexia Putellas, Ona Batlle and Mapi Leon among them.

Image: Former Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas is one of three players to join the WSL this summer

But the turning point for Kerolin follows the departure of forward Salma Paralluelo, a player similar in profile to her. The 22-year-old scored twice in last season's Champions League final, a precocious young talent with a huge appetite for success, now clubless after failing to agree terms.

Kerolin, who once held transfer interest from Arsenal, is perfectly poised to succeed her. Barcelona's need for a player of Kerolin's talents is greater than that of City's, flush with versatile wingers, while the considerable fee sends a well-timed message.

Maintenance as Europe's leading superpower does not come cheap. Barcelona have been burdened by financial constraints over the past few years, reliant on their global pull to attract and retain the game's top stars. But others have caught up; no longer is their lure enough in isolation.

To keep pace, Barcelona must show willing to be as financially front-footed as their European rivals. Kerolin's capture is a statement signing for a side in need of some validation after bidding farewell to four high-profile players in as many weeks. Proof that Romeu is remodelling, rather than revolutionising his team of aces.

Nor is this move an ego trip. Kerolin made 26 WSL appearances for Man City, scoring 12 goals. Only Khadija Shaw and Stina Blackstenius have a better goals-per-90 ratio during that time. No player can match Kerolin for take-ons attempted or completed.

In fact, very few forwards boast her complete skillset. She can balance scoring with creating, on-the-ball craft with off-the-ball industry, and has explosive speed in both directions. She scores screamers, too, with quality off both flanks.

Her departure less than two years after signing will feel premature for many in Manchester, not least City's leading scorer Shaw, for whom she made a habit of assisting.

But business is business; a rare deal where the benefits are mutually divided. Man City reap significant return on their investment and make space for one of their other wide forwards to make strides. Any one of Aoba Fujino, Mary Fowler, Iman Beney, or newly-recruited Beth Mead would fit the bill.

Barcelona, meanwhile, have a growing awareness of the increased competition they face to stay queens of Europe. They remain the highest benchmark for success for now, but need fresh impetus to stay there. Kerolin greatly enhances their chances.

Sports.title: Raducanu could benefit ending her season following US Open withdrawal
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu could benefit from ending her season early to focus on recovery and secure a protected ranking before making her return in 2027, according to former British No 1 Annabel Croft.

The 23-year-old suffered a stress fracture to her right lower leg during the grass-court season and made a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon.

And following consultation with her medical team, Raducanu on Monday concluded she will be unable to play at the US Open later this month - live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The US Open is live on Sky Sports Tennis this month

What is a Protected Ranking?

It is a provision in tennis that enables players who have been absent from the sport for an extended period to qualify more easily for tournaments upon their return.



The ATP and WTA Tours have different rules when it comes to protected rankings.



For ATP Tour or other men's tournaments, an eligible player could use a protected ranking calculated over the three months after they suffered an injury.



WTA Tour players see their protected rankings fixed as the same as it was at the time when the injury was first suffered.



A WTA player can use this protected ranking for eight tournaments in a year, or 12 if they miss more than a year.



Raducanu has only recently taken her first tentative steps back on court while wearing a protective boot, and the latest setback is another blow for the Brit after a frustrating 12 months plagued by persistent physical issues.

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, former player-turned-TV analyst Croft admitted "she's been unbelievably unlucky with injury problems."

"There are so many injuries out there but it seems like she never gets a clear run where she's able to really go for it with her tennis and her body and her mind and everything injury free and just keep the momentum going."

After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training, Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair's time on court together has been limited.

Raducanu enjoyed one of the best weeks of her career by reaching her biggest final since New York at Queen's Club in June but it was that effort that triggered her latest setback.

She was not among the players named in Great Britain's team for the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in late September.

"I've seen lots of pictures of her posting with the boot on her leg and just trying to serve, to keep her racket going and showing everybody that she's doing everything she can. But clearly, it's not healed up," said Croft, who retired from the professional tour at the age of 21.

A protected ranking for Raducanu?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look back at Emma Raducanu's incredible win at the 2021 US Open. The tournament is live on Sky Sports Tennis this month

There will now be question marks over whether Raducanu, who will slide from her current ranking of 49, will compete again in 2026 with the temptation of a protected ranking.

Should she miss at least six months of competition due to injury, she can use a special ranking for a select number of events upon her return. This would be her top-50 ranking from during the grass season - the last time she competed and received prize money for a tournament.

Raducanu is at the risk of dropping down the rankings with a lot of points to defend following last year's north American hard-court swing in Washington, Canada, Cincinnati, and the US Open.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Both Tim Henman and Laura Robson believe Raducanu reuniting with her former coach is a good move

"It wouldn't be a surprise if she made that decision [close down her season]," said Croft, a former world No 24. "That wouldn't be such a bad decision to take because you can fully heal, rest up, get as much treatment as possible and then come out fully fit, raring to go at the start of next year.

"Maybe if there's a worry about the ranking drop with so many points to defend and potentially that ranking could plummet, although she might benefit from the protected ranking.

"All of these factors have to be considered, don't they? But at the end of the day, your health is your wealth, as they say, and that is the most important factor and she just needs to get herself fit.

"It's an unusual injury. I mean, I've had calf muscle injuries, which were not nice at all. And the minute you push off, you tweak it and it feels tight but the one thing that I've always thought about Raducanu, particularly when we saw her at Queen's Club on the grass where she played such beautiful tennis, is that she's very light on her feet. Movement has always been one of her strengths.

"She's such a great athlete. She moves around the ball. She's light on her feet and gets into great positions where she never looks off balance. But movement will be part of a major strength of what she brings out onto the court. That needs to be absolutely 100 per cent."

Sports.title: McKenna to target Eubank Jr and more after dream world title fight
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna believes winning the middleweight title will pave the way for fights against some of the biggest names in boxing.

Ireland's McKenna gets his dream world title fight on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, when he boxes Etinosa Oliha for the IBF championship at the 3Arena in Dublin.

"It's something I've been dreaming of since I started boxing at six years old. Finally to get a fight for the world title and for it to be in Ireland makes it extra special," McKenna told Sky Sports.

"I have goosebumps just thinking about fighting in there with that Irish atmosphere.

"20 years I've been boxing and it's all going to come down to this night."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks up his IBF world middleweight title fight in Dublin where he takes on Etinosa Oliha. Ahead of the bout live on Sky Sports, Andy Scott talks to the Irishman.

McKenna believes victory would put him in the frame for more high profile fights.

"I want to become undisputed and then become a multiple weight world champion. I'm 6ft 2, I can go all the way to heavyweight with my size! By the time my career's over I'll be fighting at heavyweight! That said, I want to clean up the middleweight division because it definitely is there to be cleaned up and just have the biggest fights possible," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of his IBF world middleweight title fight against Etinosa Oliha, Aaron McKenna claims he's the best middleweight in the world.

He would welcome a fight with Chris Eubank Jr. The Brighton star, the son of British legend Chris Eubank, last boxed at middleweight and is expected to return at 168lbs. McKenna is convinced it could happen.

"100 per cent," he said.

"Try and get a win for the Eubank name [in Ireland]," McKenna urged. "You had Eubank [Senior] and Steve Collins, they fought in Cork on Sky Sports. So you never know. If he wants to run a similar story back we can do it in Ireland on Sky Sports again, just recreate history.

"After this show on August 8, Irish boxing will have a big star and it's going to bring massive, massive headlines and a new audience to Irish boxing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks about his unlikely friendship with Kendrick Lamar after meeting at a training session with his brother.

He knows though that Oliha harbours his own ambitions. "He's a very good fighter, strong, he'll be game and any man that's fighting for world titles is going to be giving it their all," McKenna said.

His faith in himself though is total. "I know what I have to do," he added. "I'm more than ready for it.

"The main goal has always been the world title since I started boxing and I've always believed I would become world champion. So on August 8 becoming world champion will definitely open a lot of doors for me."

Sports.title: Race to make Donald's 2027 Ryder Cup team begins this month
Sports.content:
The qualifying process to make Luke Donald's 2027 European Ryder Cup team will start at the British Masters later this month.

The August 27-30 tournament, which is being staged at The Belfry and is hosted by Sir Nick Faldo, will be the first event over the next year at which eligible DP World Tour members can earn Ryder Cup points in the race to make the cut to play at Adare Manor in Ireland next September.

As ever, the six leading players from the Ryder Cup points list will earn automatic places on Team Europe. That qualifying process ends on Sunday August 22, 2027.

Donald will then complete his latest 12-player line-up with six 'Captain's Picks', which he will make in the week commencing August 30 2027.

The 2027 Ryder Cup takes place at Adare Manor in County Limerick, Ireland on September 17-19, 2027 when the Donald-captained European side will bid for three wins in a row.

Donald, who will be the first golfer since Bernard Gallacher to skipper in three consecutive Ryder Cups, said: "The start of qualification is always a notable milestone in the Ryder Cup journey, so I am delighted to today confirm details of our process for the 2027 European Team.

Sports.title: Stokes confirms England coach ambitions, questions Brook captaincy snub
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes has said he would "absolutely" love to coach England one day, as he also suggested Brendon McCullum would still be in charge of the Test team had he not announced his own international retirement weeks beforehand.

Stokes gave up the England Test captaincy and retired from international cricket following his side's 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June, which followed a 4-1 Ashes loss to Australia over the winter.

Speaking at length for the first time since his retirement on the For The Love of Cricket podcast hosted by former team-mates Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler, the 35-year-old Stokes suggested he had 'definitely' retired for good and opened up on his longer-term goals.

"I want to be a coach," said Stokes.

"I know what I want to do in terms of staying within the game - which is to be a coach.

"Would I love to be coach of England one day? Absolutely. I would love to be able to do that. Do I think it's going to happen? I don't know. No idea.

"Then, further on from that, I don't know. I just really like the idea of being, again, in some form of leadership away from playing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes hit a match-winning century in his first game back for Durham after announcing his retirement from international duty

Stokes held the Test captaincy for four years from 2022, working alongside head coach McCullum as the pair reshaped England's playing style.

McCullum's exit from his Test role was announced two weeks after Stokes called time on his international playing career during the fourth day of England's third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

"I was [surprised]," said Stokes.

"If I hadn't made the decision that I made four weeks ago, Baz would still be coach.

"So it's my fault!"

On the discussions held between them around their respective exits, Stokes added: "When I told Baz [about Stokes' retirement] he was making toast and I just went 'oh, I'm done'. I'd obviously had discussions with him anyway and then told him over toast.

"Then, again, he was like 'yeah, I've been given the tap on the shoulder' and I was like 'oh'. But he's still very excited and very happy to be moving forward with the white-ball because he's doing a very good job there."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking to Michael Atherton on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, former Australian white-ball captain Aaron Finch labelled England cricket 'a circus' and admitted he's finding their current crisis amusing

Stokes on his 'concern' for Root over captaincy return and Brook snub

Stokes also had his say on the new era for the Test team after former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming was confirmed as the side's new head coach and Joe Root reappointed captain.

Stokes said he spoke with Root, his long-time team-mate and predecessor as captain in 2017-2022, when the news broke and backed him to succeed in his second spell in the role. However, Stokes said he did have "concern" for his friend given how the role hung heavily on England's highest run-scorer last time.

"I love Rooty. I wish him nothing but success," said Stokes.

"I hope he goes on to achieve amazing things in his role of captain, and I think he's going to really enjoy it with Flem. He's a great man. I've worked with Flem before.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"But I told Joe: 'my only worry is you'. And that's all I really care about now with Rooty just because I saw what he went through and how much he put himself through.

"He just always put the team first; he always came second. That is just my only concern with it: knowing what he went through last time he was in charge of the team because I don't want to see that ever happen again because I care for Joe a lot.

"But I wish him all the success in the world. I'm sure he's going to do great so I'm looking forward to seeing what the team does going forward."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook pays tribute to Ben Stokes following his retirement from international cricket and insists that he is up to the challenge of becoming the next England Test captain

But Stokes did question why Harry Brook, the vice-captain of the Test team and the white-ball captain, had not been named as his replacement.

Rob Key, England men's managing director, said recently "I don't feel like this is the right time" for Brook to be named Test captain but that the 27-year-old's "time will come".

But Stokes argued: "If you think someone is going to be a good captain or a good leader, just give it to them.

"Brooky [was] made vice-captain. I'm not there anymore but even when I missed that Test match [against New Zealand] I was like 'why is Brooky not captain? He's vice-captain.'

"And I understood the reasoning why they were saying it, but I was still like, what message is that sending to him? He's vice-captain and the captain is not playing but he's not captain. Then the same again here.

"I had no leadership or captaincy experience when I took over. It was just thought I was going to be a good captain."

Stokes rules out 2027 Ashes return

The 35-year-old also appeared to firmly rule out any playing return in next summer's home Ashes series against Australia after Key said he "wouldn't be surprised" if the all-rounder came out of retirement.

"I never once thought, 'I'm just going to give it up and just keep going as a player'," said Stokes of his decision to retire as captain and player.

"I'm 35. If I'm not going to be captain, I think I'd find it tough to do it. Not saying because I'd find it tough to be led by someone else. I just think because I've given so much of this part of my career to my job, if I'm going to be play for England it's going to be as captain.

"I was very comfortable retiring from playing and not thinking about playing for England."

And asked squarely if he had "definitely" retired, Stokes replied: "Defo."

Sports.title: Wenger and Infantino’s No 2 Grafström criticise ‘sad and reproachable’ World Cup plan
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s authority was dealt a further blow after his No 2, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, called the failed World Cup private investment plan a “sad and reproachable series of events”.

In further evidence that senior Fifa personnel continue to distance themselves from Infantino and his botched scheme, Arsène Wenger issued a statement on Tuesday morning saying the project’s withdrawal was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. The former Arsenal manager is Fifa’s chief of global development and had publicly been silent about the crisis unfolding in world football.

The comments by Grafström and Wenger follow the resignation last week of Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to Infantino, and a scathing rebuke from the Fifa chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, in which he said the administration had been “deceived” by its president.

Grafström spoke out in an email to Fifa staff, referring to an “extraordinary and challenging” week. His message stopped short of criticising Infantino by name and promised to shield colleagues from the strife ravaging their organisation.

In a section referring to the perceived success of the World Cup this summer, he wrote: “A sad and reproachable series of events – which were thankfully concluded with the FFE [Fifa Forward Enterprise] project permanently abandoned – for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

“We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as secretary general, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations, hand in hand with all relevant stakeholders and in full compliance with the Fifa statutes and Fifa regulations.

“I assure you that as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

“Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Such strong words from Infantino’s deputy will heighten the sense that the president is becoming isolated within the upper echelons of his own administration.

Meanwhile Wenger, who assumed his Fifa position in November 2019, confirmed he had been among the many senior Fifa staff sidelined by Infantino’s plan. “I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” he said.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity.”

Infantino’s tenure continues to be under severe pressure, a number of European federations retracting their support on Monday for his re-election with others expected to follow.

Sports.title: Manchester United set to appoint former Hearts manager Eva Olid as new head coach
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to appoint the former Hearts manager Eva Olid as their new head coach to replace Marc Skinner, following his exit on Monday, multiple sources have told the Guardian.

Talks with the 40-year-old are understood to be very advanced and she is expected to be introduced to the United squad on Wednesday.

United are confident that the Spanish coach is the right person to lead them into a new chapter, as first reported by the Telegraph, as the Women’s Super League club focuses on developing young, homegrown players.

Olid led Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last term on a dramatic final day of the season, but it had already been confirmed in April that she was to leave the Edinburgh club this summer by mutual agreement. She was in charge of Hearts for five years and also guided them to the 2024 Scottish Cup final, where they were beaten by Rangers.

She has previously coached in the United States with Houston Dynamo, working with their women’s team and their under-19s men’s squad, before she had a spell with the Catalan Football Association.

United are understood to be impressed by her playing style and her ability to develop and improve players, and they carried out extensive background checks on Olid prior to publicly announcing Skinner’s departure on Monday, with succession planning having already been well under way.

Skinner left partly because of frustration at United’s transfer strategy. The club are understood to feel the current level of spending across the WSL is unsustainable and they want a different approach, focusing on their own younger talents and improving their academy to deliver longer-term success.

View image in fullscreen Marc Skinner left Manchester United party because of frustration over the club’s transfer strategy. Photograph: John Clifton/Action Images/Reuters

United finished fourth in the WSL last term. They start the new season away to big-spending London City Lionesses on 4 September.

The news comes on the day that the United captain, Maya Le Tissier, said her team will “stick together” and be ready for the new WSL season, despite Skinner departing.

Le Tissier and the rest of the playing squad were informed by Skinner that he would be leaving, in a meeting on Monday morning shortly before the news was announced, and on Tuesday Le Tissier and her England teammate Ella Toone paid tribute to Skinner for his contribution to the club over five years in charge, which included winning the 2024 Women’s FA Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Le Tissier said the “energy he brought to the club was amazing”, while Toone told reporters: “He wanted to tell the team before it came out. It was nice that he was able to tell us [and] he was able to say goodbye, because he’s done a lot for the club. We can’t thank him enough for everything he’s done, the hard work and the passion that he’s put into leading this team.”

Le Tissier said that neither she nor Toone have been consulted on who the next head coach should be but added: “I think the club have been pretty clear with what they’ve said, bringing through the youth, that’s what something Manchester United has been kind of made for, and they’ve always done that historically. I think they’ve been pretty clear with that. When we speak to the new manager, the ambitions will be clear.

“Me and Tooney are at Man United because we want to win and we’ll be doing everything we can to make that happen. We’ve got a great team, a great squad, great girls. I’m ready to do that.

“No matter who comes and goes, we’ve always had that togetherness and that fight for each other and we stick together in tough moments. There’s been a few over the years and we’ve always come through as a team, and, yeah, this one might be difficult right now, we’re in the start of pre-season and we want to make sure that we’re 100% ready for the start of the season.

“We spoke to the girls today, we’ll stick together, we always do. We’ve got to go out on the pitch, enjoy playing football and being with each other and we’ll get through it.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Chelsea, Jordan Henderson and a transfer pivot for the ages
Sports.content:
A BRIDGE TOO FAR?

Who’s next? Can they convince Craig Gordon to reverse his recent retirement? Invite Bolo Zenden back for a second spell at Stamford Bridge? Get Kieran Richardson to replace Marc Cucurella? Chelsea really have cooked up a fascinating transfer policy: to recreate the Sunderland XI that triumphed 3-0 at the Bridge in November 2010. Danny Welbeck, 19 and on loan from Manchester United, sealed victory that day; Jordan Henderson, 20 and days away from his England debut, ran things in the middle alongside Lee Cattermole. Sixteen years later, Welbeck and Henderson are teammates once again, brought together by Chelsea’s sudden realisation that Alan Hansen had a point.

Henderson continues to surprise with his post-Liverpool career path, swapping Dammam for Amsterdam before exploring the different corners of west London, all in the space of three years. How can one say no to the charms of Xabi Alonso? “Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the ⁠players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,” Henderson bellowed, before awarding BlueCo a medal for participation. “I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.”

It’ll take some time getting used to Henderson in blue, though you wonder just how much we’ll see of him on the pitch, his reputation nowadays less focused on what he does with the ball at his feet. Now it’s all about his role as The Standard Setter, the peace lily that brings a dressing room together. “The best guy I’ve ever come across I think in football,” cooed Morgan Rogers while on duty for England this summer, a view also taken by Jude Bellingham. Chelsea’s new record signing will surely welcome the soothing instructions of Hendo at Cobham.

The club’s pivot in transfer strategy is, of course, incredibly amusing: spending gargantuan sums on young talent before clocking on to the grand idea that not all of your first-team players should be eligible for a railcard. And even then, old habits die hard: the signing of Welbeck is yet another from Brighton, following the same path taken in recent seasons by Cucurella, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and João Pedro. It all makes for a spectacular act of plagiarism, with Alonso’s Chelsea combining the Tony Bloom project down south with a flavour of Steve Bruce’s Sunderland. Football Daily looks forward to reading about Nedum Onuoha in Wednesday’s Rumour Mill.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports. The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity” – Arsène Wenger, these days Fifa’s chief of global development, puts a metaphorical moat between himself and his president, Gianni Infantino. Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafström, Infantino’s No 2, has also called the failed World Cup private investment plan a “sad and reproachable series of events”.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino watches the World Cup semi-final match between England and Argentina, flanked by Arsène Wenger (left) and Mattias Grafström (right). Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Big Website: on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, you name it.

“Whoever wrote the Uefa statements over the weekend deserves a pay rise. Crystal clear messages, each line dripping with contempt and – for once – speaking for millions of football fans. ‘Thou shalt not pass’ at its best” – Gabriele Weber.

“The sublime Marcus Stewart scored for Huddersfield at Wolverhampton in September 1999, the game’s only goal, with a Panenka. Steve Bruce, his manager, said that, if he ever tried to do that again, he’d chip him. He took the warning seriously and didn’t try another even after Bruce left the club. Please give this a little space in your diary; not for my sake, but for Marcus’s, as he contends with the most appalling illness” – Richard Askham.

“Has anyone ever seen Infantino and The Hood from Thunderbirds in the same room?” – Craig Fawcett.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Gabriele Weber. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard hails ‘huge’ signing as Coventry seal record £22.5m Rushworth deal
Sports.content:
Coventry have completed the club-record £22.5m signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton as Frank Lampard’s side continue to prepare for their return to the Premier League after 25 years away.

The 25-year-old excelled on loan at Coventry in the Championship last season, playing an instrumental role in their promotion as champions, starting all 46 league matches and earning the Golden Glove award for keeping 17 clean sheets.

“It’s great to have Carl back with us on a permanent basis,” said Lampard, whose side begin their season at Arsenal on 21 August. “He’s a top professional, a great character and he had a huge impact on the team to help us get promoted last season. I’m looking forward to working with him again and welcoming him back into the group.”

Rushworth, who is also highly regarded within the Football Association and the England setup, joined Brighton from non-league Halifax in 2019 but departed the club without making a senior appearance. Before his season at Coventry he had enjoyed loans across the league pyramid with Walsall, Lincoln City, Swansea and Hull.

Brighton’s sporting director, Mike Cave, said: “While we would have liked to keep Carl with the club for longer, we respect his decision to secure regular first-team football in the Premier League.” Brighton are thought to have negotiated a sell-on clause and a buy-back option as part of the sale, which could rise as high as £30m including add-ons.

Rushworth represents Coventry’s fourth summer signing. Last month they eclipsed their previous transfer record when paying Eintracht Frankfurt £17m to sign the Switzerland defender Aurèle Amenda, and have also signed Loum Tchaouna and Frank Onyeka. Until Amenda’s arrival, their record outlay was £7.7m, to Antalyaspor, for Haji Wright in 2023.



Elsewhere, Aston Villa have welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) upholding their appeal to register 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo. The teenager, who was born in London but raised in Luxembourg, joined Villa from Metz in January but had been ineligible to play owing to Fifa’s regulations on international transfers of minors. Madjo, who has scored four goals in pre-season, is now available to feature for Villa.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Vinícius says Mourinho ‘wants me to be happy’ at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is settling into life under the new Real Madrid manager, José ⁠Mourinho, with a smile on his face even as uncertainty swirls around the Brazil forward’s future at the Bernabéu.

The 26-year-old, who has ⁠been ​one of the linchpins of Real Madrid’s attack in recent years, gave an upbeat assessment of his second ⁠day of pre-season training under Mourinho despite speculation linking him with a possible move to Arsenal.

“It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new ​players, and training very hard,” ‌Vinícius told Real Madrid ‌TV. “Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football.”

Vinícius’s cheerful demeanour, however, masks a potentially thorny situation brewing behind the scenes. He is in the final year of his Real Madrid contract, with speculation that the club and player remain locked in negotiations while Arsenal explore a potential transfer.

Vinícius has scored 128 goals for Madrid and provided 100 assists, with the club reluctant to ​let one of their prized assets leave for free next year.

He had a busy summer playing for Brazil at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16, and his focus now is ⁠on preparing for the new campaign.

“We have to prepare physically ​so that during the ​season we have fewer ​injuries and can count on everyone,” said Vinícius, who was ​Brazil’s top scorer ‌at the ​World Cup with ​four goals.

“It was a good training session and we all left very tired, but now it’s time to rest for tomorrow. That’s how pre-season is and we have to be ready.”

Sports.title: Concacaf countries considering withdrawing support for under-fire Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
A number of Concacaf countries are considering following Europe’s lead by formally removing their ­support for the Fifa president, Gianni ­Infantino.

All 41 members of Concacaf – the confederation which represents North America, Central America and the Caribbean – are understood to have submitted ­letters of endorsement for ­Infantino’s re‑election campaign before the World Cup finals tournament, but many are now giving serious con­sideration to withdrawing them.

Finland became the first of Fifa’s 211 member associations to publicly withdraw its letter of support last Thursday, followed on Monday by the Football Association of Wales. The former Wales international Laura McAllister, a Uefa vice-president, had proposed the World Cup boycott at an emergency Uefa meeting last week, while the FA is also understood to have written to Fifa withholding its backing for Infantino.

Concacaf held an emergency meeting last Friday, with a source who attended telling the Guardian that all members are strongly aligned with Uefa, which has led the calls for Infantino to go.

The Concacaf meeting is understood to have featured pledges from several countries to withdraw their backing for Infantino, and some may have already done so in private.

One potential difficulty for Concacaf is the fact that four of its members – the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica – are bidding to stage the 2031 Women’s World Cup in the next hosting decision to be taken by Fifa.

While there are no other bids on the table at present, the decision still has to be approved by Fifa at an extraordinary general meeting to be held in November.

The US Soccer Federation is understood to be deeply unhappy with Infantino – particularly with the ­backlash his dealings with ­Donald Trump created for them over the Folarin Balogun affair – but, given the political sensitivities, may not feel able to take him on.

Another complicating factor is the fact that the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been widely touted as the potential candidate most able to take Infantino on in the presidential election next March.

Although Montagliani has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s ­governance, the Canadian has yet to decide whether he wants to stand, and told the Guardian in an interview last month that his priority is being re‑elected as president of ­Concacaf, with those elections also taking place next year.

While Concacaf is united, the Asian Football Confederation, which also backed the Uefa-led opposition to Infantino’s proposed World Cup sell‑off, appears to have splintered since the dramatic events of last week. Significantly, the financial powerhouses of Qatar and the United Arab Emirates have both publicly backed Infantino to stay on, as have smaller countries such as Sri Lanka, Lebanon, Kuwait and Bhutan.

11:54 Is Gianni Infantino’s time up as Fifa president? - The Latest

While most of the AFC’s 47 members – including Saudi Arabia – have stayed silent, Uefa is hoping it can attract their support, but it remains unclear whether the rebels have the numbers to force a genuine electoral contest.

New Zealand Football’s Andrew Pragnell says Fifa’s abandoned private equity proposal delivered a shock to confidence in world football’s governance, and he urged ­Oceania’s members to be united on the question of Infantino’s leadership.

Oceania’s confederation, which includes New Zealand among its 11 members, has yet to take a position on the Fifa president’s leadership, although Pragnall said there had been “enormous gains” for football associations outside the traditional powerhouses of Europe and ​South America under Infantino – “but the proposal itself, the way in which it was delivered, developed, the way members found out, and the shock to confidence among the international football system, has cast a pretty big shadow”.

Pragnell said that New Zealand would consult with Oceania members and other regional confederations before adopting a position, and said it would be preferable for the member nations to be aligned on the matter. “There’s obviously more power in numbers,” Pragnall said.

“Certainly it helps when a con­federation acts in unison. You’ve seen in some confederations, even in the last week, members go dif­ferent ways from other members.”

Sports.title: ‘I can’t wait’: Dominik Szoboszlai hungry for Liverpool reset under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai believes last season’s frustration can push Liverpool to challenge for the title again but admits the squad must produce “something special” if no reinforcements arrive before the transfer deadline.

The Liverpool midfielder upped his already impressive level last season, being named the club’s player of the year, but collectively the team went into reverse with Arne Slot losing his job as a consequence. The poor title defence from a team that won the Premier League comfortably in Slot’s debut season should, Szoboszlai insists, prompt a reaction in Andoni Iraola’s debut campaign as Liverpool head coach.

“I can’t wait [for the new season], honestly,” said the Hungary captain following Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. “I feel that we are ready to go again and take motivation from last season because it was not the best. We didn’t end up where we wanted to. So now we’re going to go for it again.

“Everyone is motivated. I think I see in everybody’s eyes that he wants to play and, if you want to play, you have to give your best. And from there the manager is going to decide who is going to play. But everybody is on zero right now.”

Liverpool have added the central defender Jérémy Jacquet and the versatile forward Victor Muñoz this summer but, while they remain in pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, a squad that has seen Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konaté depart as free agents remains light in several positions.

Szoboszlai said of Liverpool’s transfer activity: “It’s not my job to tell you who we have to sign or if we have to sign someone. If the guys above and the manager decide to sign someone, then we are very happy and are going to welcome him – or them – well. If they decide not to, then we have to do something special with this squad.”

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s new head coach, Andoni Iraola, cuts a thoughtful figure during the US pre-season tour. Photograph: Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images

The Liverpool midfielder revealed Iraola prefers not to address his players in the immediate aftermath of a game, a trait he discovered after the pre-season friendlies against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds. “He doesn’t speak after the game,” Szoboszlai disclosed. “I think every manager is different in his own way. That’s how he is. He always would rather speak the day after the game, which is fine for everyone. We have to get used to this.”

Iraola has also not spoken to Szoboszlai – or any other player for that matter – about filling one of the vice-captaincy positions vacated by Robertson and Salah. But the 25-year-old, who captained Liverpool on the US tour, says it would be a huge honour to be asked.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He added: “There hasn’t been any conversation. We have Virgil [van Dijk] as the captain, we have Ali [Alisson], we have Joe Gomez [as vice-captains], so there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here and Joe is injured. Let’s see. It’s not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain of Liverpool, you’re going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me but I respect everybody. Whoever it’s going to be, we’re going to follow them.”

The captain’s armband became an issue for Curtis Jones when Szoboszlai passed it to Kostas Tsimikas during the win over Wrexham in New York. But Szoboszlai, who recently signed a new five-year contract at Anfield, insisted there was no problem with his fellow midfielder.

“It was never a debate between us three,” he claimed. “We just discussed something on the pitch. After, you guys make it very big. But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. Nobody was angry. It’s all cleared. We are cool, everybody.”

Sports.title: Alverca: the Portuguese club thriving with help from Vinícius Júnior
Sports.content:
Alverca have been busy in the last few years. They have shot up the Portuguese pyramid while changing owners, buying a whole new squad and bringing in one of the world’s most famous footballers as a co-owner. The club’s sporting director, Fernando Malta, says they want to be “gamechangers”.

Historically a satellite club for nearby Benfica, Alverca were first promoted to the top flight in 1998 but folded in 2005 after a costly relegation. The club reformed and gradually made its way through the regional divisions before earning back-to-back promotions to take them to the Portuguese top flight in 2025.

But their rapid success came at a cost. Their owners at the time, the Vicintin family, already owned a club in the top flight. Alverca, who were run by Ricardo Vicintin, and Santa Clara, who were overseen by his son Bruno, were on a collision course, so a decision had to be made. “How could a father face his son? I’m talking about the heart,” said Ricardo at the time. “I could never cope with having to face the team that my son loves so much. A father’s role is to let his children grow. And I’m no different.”

View image in fullscreen Vinícius Júnior attends Alverca v Benfica game in 2025. Photograph: Filipe Amorim/AFP/Getty Images

Perhaps more pertinently, the Vicintin family were forced to sell up as they were not allowed to own two clubs in the same division. That’s where Vinícius Júnior came in. The Real Madrid forward was part of a group of investors who bought Alverca in February 2025, while they were sealing promotion to the top flight.

Vinícius’s agent Thassilo “Tata” Soares is the majority shareholder, with the player taking on a withdrawn role. “Our relationship with Vinícius is remote,” says Malta. “We say he is the club’s most famous fan.” Vinícius is not the only big name involved. His Real Madrid teammate Eduardo Camavinga and the singer Travis Scott offer the club “communication and marketing” services. Although not hands-on, Vinícius brings the club publicity and is a draw for new signings, especially at the academy level.

Footballers investing in clubs is becoming increasingly common. The Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois has invested in Le Mans, who have also secured promotion to the first division. There hasn’t been the same degree of success for Kylian Mbappé, whose SM Caen side were relegated to the third tier of French football a year ago. Their failure incited protests against the France captain. A few former Real Madrid players are also investing in clubs. Luka Modric is involved at Swansea; Cristiano Ronaldo is co-owner of Spanish club Almería, and the former Brazil striker Ronaldo was the majority shareholder in Real Valladolid as well as his hometown club, Cruzeiro.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid keeper Thibaut Courtois has invested in Ligue 1 side Le Mans. Photograph: Pascal Pochard-Casabianca/AFP/Getty Images

Vinícius was present for the club’s game against Benfica at the start of last season. He saw a squad of players who barely knew each other. The club made 35 signings last season – a record in Portuguese football. Such a drastic overhaul was necessary as so many of their players were on loan from Santa Clara. By the time Alverca started the season, just one player from the previous season remained – and he left in January.

“Mad” is how the club’s chief scout Dominique Castro describes last summer’s transfer window. Bastien Meupiyou, who joined the club from Wolves last summer, says the players “exceeded expectations” given their standing start. “Our team was made up of entirely new players,” says the young centre-back. “No one knew each other, but we managed to adapt, which happened naturally, and we managed to get along well.

“Everyone in Portugal expected us to be in the relegation zone for the whole season,” adds Malta. Instead, Alverca finished 11th. There was perhaps a degree of smug satisfaction when Santa Clara finished two places below them.

Meupiyou, who has been nominated for this year’s Golden Boy award, was the team’s standout performer. “He’s the player that every high-level club wants to know about,” says Malta. The 20-year-old centre-back – who could become Alverca’s record sale if he moves on this summer – sums up the club’s strategy of developing and then selling players.

View image in fullscreen Highly rated Alverca defender Bastien Meupiyou has been nominated for this year’s Golden Boy award. Photograph: Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images

Portugal is a hotbed of talent and the Lusophone link makes the country a popular destination for young Brazilian talents arriving in Europe. The club’s owners have established a relationship with Athletic Club in Minas Gerais. They are also picking up players from the Île-de-France region, perhaps the greatest hotbed of talent in the world.

Castro was previously chief scout at Lens, so knows the French market inside out. “Along with São Paulo, it is the region that creates the best young players in the world,” he says. “In France, there is a considerable production of talent. There is maybe even too much talent for the academies and clubs to get the maximum out of all of their players. You find players who are not really being used properly. For some, the only solution is to leave. The talent in France is extraordinary and multicultural, which means players adapt to life abroad quickly and well.”

Alverca are very happily exploiting that surplus talent. Gil Vicente are the only club in the Portuguese top flight with more French players. “We are not a big club in terms of size, so we need to be creative in our scouting and use of data,” says Malta. “The club’s main objective is staying in the top division but the second is selling players. It’s a league that is not sustainable for the owners.

Sustainability and survival are the priorities at Alverca. Malta says he will “never focus” on challenging the top clubs “because they are not from our league”. That is not defeatism but rather realism. The “big three” in Portugal – Benfica, Porto and Sporting – have only been pipped to the title twice in 92 years: by Boavista in 2001 and Belenenses in 1946. If this were an Opta tweet, it would end with the word: “Dominant.”

Alverca know where they sit in the pecking order but they are optimistic and have conviction. “There is space for new things. We strongly believe in our method and that we will be gamechangers,” says Malta, who draws inspiration from Braga’s recent rise.

Having spent much of their history in the shadow of larger, more famous, club. Emboldened and backed by new, big-name investors, they are stepping into the light.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino is accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA in extraordinary statement
Sports.content:
Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino is accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA in extraordinary statement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein has accused Gianni Infantino of blackmail as pressure continues to mount on the FIFA president.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition - including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and Concacaf - the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean - are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Jordan, meanwhile, are the first Asian nation to rebel against Infantino - taking the total to 91, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

In a statement Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Gianni Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein

‘There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time,’ Hussein said

‘We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

‘First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted VISAS, even though they had tickets - which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‘Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‘This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

‘Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

Daily Mail Sport have contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho is forced off injured in just his second Aston Villa match since sealing acrimonious Chelsea departure
Sports.content:
Aston Villa forward Alejandro Garnacho left the field injured in just his second game for the club after joining from Chelsea.

Former Manchester United man Garnacho has moved to Villa Park on a year-long loan, and sources say the conditions are easily achievable and the total package meets the Blues' initial £43million valuation of the player.

But he has got his career with his new side off to a nightmare start, being substituted injured in the first-half against BG Pathum in Thailand during Villa's pre-season tour.

Having made his debut against the Indonesia All Stars last week, he was hoping to kick on but had to be replaced after being fouled by Ryan Edwards.

He needed medical treatment on the field, and made way with what was understood to be a facial injury.

Villa won the game 3-1, but also lost captain John McGinn to injury after he hurt his knee.

Alejandro Garnacho was taken off injured in just his second game after joining Aston Villa

The winger is hoping to reboot his career again after leaving Chelsea for Villa Park

Emi Buendia, Victor Lindelof and Boubacar Kamara were on the scoresheet for Unai Emery's men.

Garnacho had previously been of interest to Villa before he left Man United last summer for the Blues.

The Argentine winger played 43 matches for Chelsea last season in all competitions, but missed out on a spot at the World Cup.

Garnacho featured 24 times in the Premier League for the Blues, scoring one goal and providing three assists.

He scored eight times in total for Chelsea, with half of his goals coming in the Carabao Cup.

He has struggled to nail down a starting spot since Ruben Amorim took over at Old Trafford but will be hoping life at Villa Park is a fresh start.

Emery is a big fan of the 22-year-old and is understood to have played a key role in the move.

Villa will face Borussia Monchengladbach and Bayern Munich in friendlies before kicking off their Premier League season away to Brighton.

They will also take on Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup after winning the Europa League.
