Sports.title: How Austin MacPhee will transform Chelsea's dire set-piece record: His 'NFL playbook' that can dismantle any opposition, late-night texts to players, a formula for scoring screamers and the numbers that prove his remarkable impact
Sports.content:
Austin MacPhee was already bossing the Chelsea players about. Xabi Alonso’s new set-piece coach, just hours after the club confirmed his arrival, strode around the packed penalty area at one end of the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong, notepad in one hand, the other pointing and gesturing, as the huddle of players crowded around him and hung on his every word. Alonso clearly has so much faith in his new, long-haired Scottish dead-ball guru that while he worked on the attacking shape with his forwards, he let MacPhee lead the set-piece drills and just get on with the job. While it’s been the £117million arrival of British-record signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa that’s caught most of the headlines this summer, Chelsea will hope the other man they've poached from the Midlands club will have just as big an impact. So important have set-piece coaches become in elite football that even they have release clauses in their contracts these days. Chelsea coughed up short of £1million to trigger it and MacPhee flew over at the weekend to join up with the Blues on their pre-season tour. No time to waste. It’s an area in which Chelsea have floundered (while Villa flourished) and must improve if they are to stand any chance of mounting a title charge. So little progress was made under previous set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva since joining from Brentford two years ago, both in attack and defence, that Alonso shunted him to a new analyst role behind the scenes and away from the training pitch. Chelsea had a frustrating habit last season of conceding the same type of goal from set-pieces, where a corner or free-kick would get flicked on at the near post and tapped in at the back stick by someone left unmarked. They conceded that exact goal again in their most recent pre-season friendly against Western Sydney Wanderers. Austin MacPhee is already getting to work in his new role as Chelsea set-piece coach on their pre-season tour of Hong Kong MacPhee (second left) alongside the rest of Xabi Alonso's backroom team The Scot has forged a reputation as one of the best set-piece coaches in world football thanks to his work under Unai Emery at Aston Villa Only West Ham and Leeds conceded more Premier League goals from corners than Chelsea last season while MacPhee continued to turn Aston Villa into one of the best set-piece teams in Europe. Arsenal and Tottenham were the only two clubs to score more goals from corners than Villa last season. Since MacPhee took over as Villa’s set-piece specialist ahead of the 2021-22 campaign, they have scored 72 goals from dead-ball situations, not including penalties, behind only Liverpool and Arsenal. Chelsea, over the same period, scored 14 fewer. Those 72 strikes made up 25 per cent of Villa’s total non-penalty goals, behind only Everton as the highest percentage among ever-present Premier League sides. In 2023-24 alone, only Bayer Leverkusen scored more set-piece goals, excluding penalties, across Europe's big five leagues. Last season alone, Villa boasted a set-piece goal difference in the league of +four, joint-fourth in the division, while Chelsea managed a dismal -three.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

MacPhee’s numbers on their own are impressive enough but what set Villa apart under the Scot was the variety and creativity with which they scored their goals. It wasn’t just the same unplayable tactic over and over again, like England’s ‘Love Train’ from the 2018 World Cup when everyone just stood in a line before darting in different directions so Harry Maguire could head it. Villa’s repertoire was much more akin to an NFL playbook. A host of unique moves, tailored to the opposition, and with each player given a specific set of instructions. So drilled does MacPhee want his players to be that even after the long hours honing the moves on the training pitch, he sends his charges home with animations of the individual movements sent to their phones. Few of them will endure quite so iconically as Youri Tielemans’ opener in the Europa League final, which set Villa on their way to lifting the trophy. Lucas Digne played a corner from the left short to Rogers, who floated the ball into the box. Tielemans, who started the move stood alone 30 yards from goal, bent his run to meet it and then thundered a volley into the net. Villa's opening goal in the Europa League final, scored by Youri Tielemans, was a fine example of MacPhee's quirky set-piece routines Emi Martinez, the Villa goalkeeper, didn’t even bother running over to celebrate with his team-mates and made a beeline for MacPhee, who was busy receiving the embrace of every single player on the bench. Rogers, the provider that night, scored a beauty of his own in Villa’s 4-2 victory over Liverpool in May. Digne played the corner deep to John McGinn, a good 40 yards from goal, who then returned the ball to Digne out wide. That pass drew out Liverpool defender Milos Kerkez, who closed down Digne to stop the cross but inadvertently left Rogers unmarked inside the penalty area. Digne slipped the ball inside to Rogers, who turned and curled it into the top corner. Villa's set-piece trickery proved too challenging for Liverpool to handle in their 4-2 loss at Villa Park in May All of this was part of the plan. Villa became renowned last season for scoring belters from long range but, again, much of that was due to MacPhee orchestrating routines to get their best ball-strikers in the best positions to shoot from distance. And few Villa fans will forget the free-kick McGinn scored against Manchester United a couple of seasons ago when MacPhee ordered Leon Bailey to stand behind goalkeeper Andre Onana. Bailey then took it upon himself to start singing at his opponent, distracting him, and then ran away as McGinn ran up to the ball and sent it zipping past the bewildered Onana and into the net. Every single part of it, bar the impromptu singing perhaps, is planned. There’s a video on YouTube of MacPhee giving a short masterclass into Villa’s set-piece exploits, breaking down every part of a free-kick routine they used to score against Leicester. His presentation shows the team practising the runs they needed to make on the training ground, the players who needed to make them, as well as a graphic covered in arrows of how MacPhee wanted the move to play out before cutting to a replay of Villa putting it into action. Tielemans puts his hands up, looking as though he’ll dink the ball into the box, only to slip in Jacob Ramsey, who ran from deep into the penalty area, and then squared the ball for Amadou Onana to tap in from close range. MacPhee even highlights how a Villa player pushes a Leicester defender in the scrum on the edge of the box, shoving him back far enough so that if Tielemans decides to dink it to the far post after all, Ezri Konsa would now be onside. In the end, it didn’t matter. Villa, as usual, scored from Plan A. Jacob Ramsey's run caught Leicester defenders by surprise in Villa's 2-1 win there back in August 2024, thanks in part to some helpful blocking by Pau Torres The experienced MacPhee (pictured giving instructions to Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo) has worked with several national teams

Your browser does not support iframes.

Before joining Villa, MacPhee worked for clubs like FC Midtjylland – a side now famed for their set-pieces, and one that pins their goal difference from dead-ball situations to the wall above the coffee machine at their training ground – and Hearts and had stints with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Portugal. It was under Michael O’Neill at Northern Ireland where he was first given responsibility for set-pieces. They scored 11 goals from set-plays in ten games to qualify for Euro 2016, where they reached the last 16. Chelsea can only hope MacPhee has the same instant impact.

Sports.title: Italian football legends arrive in Milan for funeral of AC Milan hero Franco Baresi - who passed away aged 66 last week
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Milan was plunged into mourning as the city paid tribute to Italian football legend Franco Baresi at his funeral on Tuesday morning, after his death last week at the age of 66.

The AC Milan captain was named their Player of the Century in 1999 after spending the entirety of his 20-year career at the San Siro - including two stints in Serie B in the 1980s.

After he hung up his boots, the club retired the No6 shirt worn by their eternal 'Capitano', with the fans that lined the streets surrounding the venue for the ceremony at Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio waving replica jerseys in tribute.

Among those who attended the ceremony were some of Baresi's most famous team-mates, including his defensive partner and mentee Paolo Maldini.

The Milan icon and newly minted technical president of the Italian Football Federation arrived wearing dark glasses, alongside fellow Ballon d'Or winner Marco van Basten, who was later to act as a pallbearer for Baresi's coffin.

Roberto Baggio, Pietro Paolo Virdis, Mauro Tassotti, Clarence Seedorf, Demetrio Albertini, Alessandro Costacurta and Dida also made the pilgrimage to remember their late team-mate.

Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini was among the mourners at Franco Baresi's funeral

The legendary No6's coffin was greeted by fans outside of Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio in Milan

Also in attendance were Daniele Massaro, Roberto Donadoni, Filippo Galli, Angelo Colombo and Giovanni Galli, the Milan players who joined Van Basten in carrying Baresi's coffin into the church.

Costacurta, Virdis, Massimo Ambrosini, Marco Simone and Alberico Evani then accompanied the coffin out.

The current AC Milan cohort were represented by injured players Christian Pulisic and Santiago Gimenez, who are not on tour with the team currently undergoing pre-season in Australia.

The players will don black armbands in Perth on Wednesday when they play Inter Milan Down Under.

AC Milan chairman Paolo Scaroni and the club's owner RedBird's founder Gerry Cardinale were also in attendance, but booed on their arrival according to Gazzetta dello Sport.

When Baresi's coffin arrived, fans watching chanted 'there's only one captain' and 'you are forever Franco Baresi', before singing 'You'll Never Walk Alone'.

Baresi's former manager at Milan Fabio Capello was applauded as he arrived at the church, while ex-Milan players Dejan Savicevic and Daniele Massaro arrived bearing his white signed captain's armband.

A number of representatives from the Italian national team and other Serie A sides were also in attendance, including a cohort representing AC Milan's greatest rivals Inter Milan.

His former team-mate Clarence Seedorf was also in attendance in the northern Italian city

The great and the good from AC Milan's recent past including goalkeeper Dida (left) and former manager Fabio Capello gathered to say goodbye to Baresi

Marco van Basten (left) was one of the pallbearers on a difficult day in the centre of Milan, while Claudio Ranieri also paid tribute to Baresi

While the current AC Milan squad are currently on pre-season duty in Australia, injured players Christian Pulisic and Santiago Gimenez represented the team

The club's chairman Paolo Scaroni was also in attendance but roundly booed by the fans

Baresi's 1994 World Cup team-mate Roberto Baggio was another boldfaced name in Milan

Supporters from the San Siro's Curva Sud group made their presence known with flares

A number of Baresi's former Milan team-mates were among those who carried his coffin

Songs were sung referring to Baresi as Milan's only captain, plus 'You'll Never Walk Alone'

Baresi's No6 jersey was retired at the end of his playing career and there were a number of his jerseys among the mourners

His former rival in blue and black - and great friend - Beppe Bergomi read the first reading once the ceremony began.

Bergomi had helped Baresi during his last public appearance, with the two legendary captains bringing the Olympic flame into the San Siro for the Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony in February.

The defender, long considered one of the best of all time, served as captain for 14 years, and helped Milan claim six Serie A titles and three European Cups among numerous other honours.

Baresi had initially been rejected by Inter Milan's academy as a junior player, after being deemed too small and frail for the rigorous demands of 1970s football, with his eventual rivals instead taking on his elder brother Giuseppe.

That twist of fate brought Baresi to Milan's academy, and he would go on to make his debut for the senior team at the age of 17 - after being given his nickname Piscinin by the club's masseur at the time, Paolo Mariconti, which means 'little one' in Milanese dialect.

Baresi stuck with AC Milan throughout the match-fixing Totonero scandal which saw the club relegated in 1980, and a second relegation in 1982, before going on to see Milan through their heavily decorated glory years under legendary managers Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello.

His role as the bedrock in Milan's all-Italian defence saw him written into the club's legend, and in 1989, named Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Baresi also won the World Cup with Italy in 1982 as a squad member, later coming heartbreakingly close to claiming a second when the Azzurri reached the final in 1994 before defeat to Brazil on penalties.

Baresi had previously undergone lung surgery in August 2025 to remove a pulmonary nodule, and later was treated with cancer-prevention immunotherapy.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford's future explained: Why Man United think he will stay, the rivals trying to sign him and how Michael Carrick can reintegrate his former team-mate
Sports.content:
A year ago today, Marcus Rashford was scoring his first goal for Barcelona on loan from Manchester United in a pre-season win over Daegu in South Korea.

It was the start of an exciting new chapter in Rashford’s career after a summer in which he had been banished by United boss Ruben Amorim and forced to train separately with the ‘bomb squad’ at Carrington.

Rashford won the La Liga title during his season at the Nou Camp, playing well enough to earn a recall to the England squad for this summer’s World Cup. Yet Barca declined to trigger a £26million option to buy him before their deadline in mid-June – despite head coach Hansi Flick admitting over the weekend that he will miss the player – and no other clubs have been prepared to meet United’s £40million valuation.

As it stands, the feeling at United and within Rashford’s camp is that he is likely to return and play for his boyhood club next season. But with a month of the transfer window remaining, there is still uncertainty over the 28-year-old’s future.

Daily Mail Sport assesses Rashford’s situation and the options on the table as he prepares to report back for pre-season training.

A year ago, Marcus Rashford was banished by Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim and forced to train separately with the ‘bomb squad’ at Carrington

Rashford won the La Liga title during his season on loan at Barcelona, playing well enough to earn a recall to the England squad for this summer’s World Cup

Why hasn’t Rashford left United this summer?

Any exit would have to factor in his £325,000-a-week salary, which was agreed when he signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford in 2023. It is one of the reasons why United have been looking to move Rashford, and also why that has not been easy.

Suggestions that Rashford, comfortably United’s highest earner since Casemiro left this summer, could take a pay cut are unrealistic. Barca paid the entirety of his wages during the season on loan, but were only prepared to offer half the £26million price tag to make the move permanent.

United rejected any attempt by the Catalans to take Rashford on loan for a second season, and once Barca signed his England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle to play on the left side of their attack, it always looked as though they had moved on. Rashford issued a heartfelt message last week thanking the club and its fans for ‘a positive and unforgettable experience’.

Once the deadline for Barca to sign Rashford expired on June 15, United made it known that they would listen to offers of £40million from other clubs – with the exception of Manchester City and Liverpool – for the Wythenshawe-born player until that option ran out in mid-July.

Daily Mail Sport understands that a number of clubs from the Premier League – including two with a particular interest – as well as from Italy, Germany, Turkey and Saudi Arabia are still weighing up a move, most likely on loan.

Barcelona turned to Rashford's England team-mate Anthony Gordon (right) on the left wing this summer, in a £70million move from Newcastle

Liverpool were one of two clubs excluded from a £40m option to sign Rashford last month

When is he due back at United?

Rashford is among the final group of World Cup players due to report back next week, along with his England team-mate Kobbie Mainoo and Argentina’s Lisandro Martinez.

However, it’s a measure of the sensitivity that still surrounds his situation that United are not confirming a return date. If he does reappear next week, it remains to be seen if that will be to Carrington or Maynooth, where Michael Carrick’s squad are training at Carton House before a friendly against Leeds at Croke Park next Wednesday.

It comes a year after intense scrutiny over his comings and goings at the training ground, following Amorim’s decision to keep Rashford and the rest of the bomb squad away from Carrington until the rest of the first team had left, in what was politely described as ‘a coordinated return’.

It’s unthinkable that Carrick would take a similar stance to Amorim, who famously said he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeper coach Jorge Vital than Rashford in January last year, days before the player joined Aston Villa on loan. Carrick is a more conciliatory character than Amorim, having played alongside Rashford, coached him and managed him in the decade since he exploded onto the first-team scene under Louis van Gaal in 2016.

Intriguingly, Rashford’s first game back for United could be against Amorim's AC Milan in Wroclaw a week on Saturday.

Rashford scored the first goal of the Amorim era, in a 1-1 draw at Ipswich Town, but their relationship quickly deteriorated

Rashford (left) and Carrick (second right) have a relationship going back 10 years to when they were team-mates at United, winning the FA Cup together in 2016

Can Rashford be reintegrated at United?

In principle, his return makes total sense. United have been in the market for a left-sided attacker, and they already have one under contract for another two years who has the ability to be one of the most dynamic wide players in Europe on his day. Why wouldn’t the club be open to welcoming Rashford back to the club where he grew up?

Perhaps the cost of a replacement has made United think again too. This summer they have been priced out of a number of deals – notably for Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes – and spent just £85million so far, on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Gordon went to Barcelona for £70million and Crysencio Summerville, one of the players on United’s list, joined Al Hilal for £68million from West Ham. Suddenly the cost of keeping Rashford doesn’t seem so high.

His form dipped during his last two seasons at United, but there is nothing to say that Carrick and his staff can’t have the same rejuvenating effect on Rashford as they have on Mainoo. Like Mainoo, Rashford’s main beef was with Amorim. That’s not to say there won’t be any lingering issues with other figures at United, but nothing that would rule out a return.

Yet still there are no guarantees that Rashford will be a United player when the window closes next month. Might the club be tempted to accept an offer – a permanent move or loan – as the deadline draws near? With only Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu to play on the left wing, would United have time to sign a replacement if he leaves?

After it appeared for a long time as though there was no way back for Rashford at United, it now seems more likely than not that he will play for the club again. But with the clock counting down to his return, the fact there are still as many questions as answers speaks volumes.

Sports.title: Former Tottenham hero Erik Lamela is appointed KITMAN of Mexican side to exploit bizarre loophole in coaching rules
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham forward Erik Lamela has been appointed as the kitman of Mexican side CF Monterrey.

The Argentine, 34, retired last summer after a long battle with injury, struggling to fight a hip issue, with his final club AEK Athens in Greece following a stint at Sevilla after he left Tottenham.

He had returned to Sevilla in his retirement to work on the coaching staff under Matias Almeyda, but is now moving clubs.

Almeyda left Sevilla in March and swiftly moved to North America, where he would take up the role of head coach at Monterrey, and Lamela has followed him.

But he cannot take up the role of a coach due to the lack of required qualifications. Liga MX rules say coaches in the league must have official certification through the Federation Mexican de Futbol, and, since Lamela does not reach the standards, he isn't allowed to work the role.

But he has exploited a loophole by instead being appointed kitman of the club, meaning he can be on the bench during matches.

Former Tottenham hero Erik Lamela has been appointed kitman of a team in Mexico

It is understood that Lamela is working towards obtaining his UEFA Pro license, and will likely be promoted when he earns that.

Monterrey's goalkeeping coach Fabian Donelli finds himself in a similar situation.

Though he never quite reached the heights hoped of him after joining Tottenham for £30million in 2013 following Gareth Bale's departure, Lamela did play for the north London club for eight years.

In that time, he played 257 times for Spurs, scoring 37 goals, and was an unused substitute in the 2019 Champions League final defeat by Liverpool.

He also won the Puskas Award in 2021 for an impressive rabona goal against rivals Arsenal in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans go wild for Mykhailo Mudryk as he returns from doping ban - and Xabi Alonso reveals Ukrainian is in line for first appearance in 20 months
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has revealed Mykhailo Mudryk may make his first appearance for Chelsea in 20 months on Wednesday to officially mark his return from the footballing wilderness.

Mudryk participated in an open training session with his team-mates in Hong Kong on Tuesday at the Kai Tak Stadium, where the loudest cheer from the local fans was reserved for when the 25-year-old Ukrainian was shown on the big screen.

Chelsea face Juventus in a pre-season friendly at the same stadium on Wednesday.

Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024, when he started and scored away at Heidenheim in the Conference League. An £89million signing from Shakhtar Donetsk, he was then suspended from football after failing a doping test for the banned substance meldonium.

However, his ban ended this week after a resolution was reached with the FA.

Speaking from Hong Kong ahead of their Juve friendly, Alonso said about Mudryk: ‘Yes, he could play. Maybe 90 minutes is too early, but he can be selected. He's selected, so he can play.

Mykhailo Mudryk could play his first game in 20 months for Chelsea on Wednesday

'He trained yesterday, came directly from the airport to the hotel. So yesterday was more about the feelings, more about the emotions, to be back with the players to assess the fitness level.

'We are thrilled that Misha could be with us. You could see his smile, how great the feeling is for him to be part of the team because he has been training on his own for a long time.

'Fitness level, we will see, but he has been working hard, and now it's about trying to get him back into things with team-mates and integrating into the dynamic. But the first feeling for everyone is that we are happy he is back with the team and us.'

Daily Mail Sport reported this week how multiple clubs have approached Chelsea to ask about Mudryk, with Coventry, managed by Frank Lampard, among those interested in a potential loan.

All options are open from the perspective of Chelsea, who want to assess their player in this pre-season first. That has been relayed directly to Mudryk upon his return.

Meanwhile, Austin MacPhee was also involved in Chelsea’s open training session after arriving from Aston Villa to take over as their new set-piece specialist. Danny Welbeck is also in contention to face Juventus after signing from Brighton.

Sports.content:
Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow

Commonwealth Cup winner Venetian Sun has been ruled out for the rest of the season after trainer Karl Burke confirmed the sprinter has suffered a tendon injury

View 3 Images Tony Bloom (second left) with Venetian Sun, who followed up her success at Royal Ascot with a Group 1 victory in France (Image: PA)

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine Venetian Sun has suffered an injury setback that will sideline her for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Among last year's top juveniles, the lightning-quick daughter of Starman – owned by Brighton & Hove Albion chairman in partnership with Ian McAleavy – has maintained her brilliant form this season, claiming a second Royal Ascot triumph when storming to Commonwealth Cup glory.

‌



Her most recent outing saw her produce an excellent runner-up effort against older rivals at Newmarket in the July Cup, and she had been under consideration for a trip to France for this weekend's Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, the venue where she captured the Prix Morny as a two-year-old.

‌



Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing READ MORE :

Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

Nevertheless, plans for the remainder of her three year old campaign have been shelved following the discovery of a tendon problem.

Her trainer Karl Burke said: "It's a big shame and unfortunately it happens. It's a long way from being a career- or life-threatening injury, but obviously is going to take time and it's very disappointing.

"We had more or less decided to swerve Deauville anyway because the ground was very fast out there last weekend with no sign of any rain and the French not watering like they used to do.

‌



View 3 Images Celebrations on the track after Venetian Sun's Royal Ascot victory (Image: Getty Images)

"It's just one of those things, we have a feeling she may have initiated it at Newmarket during the July Cup but she came back from there with a nasty little cut and she had been on antibiotics and anti-inflammatories and we think that may have masked it to a degree."

Venetian Sun has triumphed in six of her nine career starts to date, with her connections eagerly anticipating an autumn schedule that could have featured appearances in Haydock's Sprint Cup, at Ascot on British Champions Day and at the Breeders' Cup.

‌



Explaining the setback, Burke added: "It's basically a strain to the tendon, it happens a lot with jumping horses – it's unusual really at this stage in a sprinter's life, but can happen.

View 3 Images Venetian Sun sprinted to victory at Ascot (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"It's a time thing now and she will have the next six or seven months on the easy list and then be reassessed from there.

Article continues below

"The little bit of work she has done the last few days has just aggravated it and we've had the vets in this morning and they weren't 100 per cent happy with a little bit of heat in the leg and that is what it turns out to be.

"The plan before today was if she finished the season in good shape she would stay in training and that may still be the plan, but that is a discussion for later on."

Sports.title: World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning
Sports.content:
World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning

Doubt has now emerged on the legitimacy of one World Cup title after shocking claims have emerged

View 2 Images France won their first World Cup title in 1998 (Image: Popperfoto via Getty Images)

The France national team were allegedly exempt from unannounced anti-doping tests for an entire year before winning the World Cup in 1998. That is according to Marie-George Buffet, who served as minister of sports under former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin from 1997 to 2002.

‌



Her revelations have come 13 years after denying such claims in front of a Senate Committee. The politician made the new statement during the documentary 'Zidane: The Making of a Legend', which focuses on the newly-appointed national team boss and his legendary playing career.

‌



However, it was overshadowed by Buffet's admission, which she said was sparked by a surprise anti-doping test during a training camp in Tignes in 1997. The tests were slammed by the players, then-manager Aime Jacquet and the French Football Federation (FFF), who accused the ministry of disrupting their preparations.

‌



All the urine tests had come back negative, but the furious reaction led Buffet to tell Alan Garnier - the doctor who carried out the tests - to no longer bother the team with anti-doping tests, according to Garnier himself.

According to Le Parisien, he said: "I was no longer to bother the French team until the World Cup. In short, no more unannounced tests." The doctor claimed the "verbal directive" was confirmed by Buffet, who acknowledged she faced pressures "of all kinds" when it came to leaving the national team alone.

When asked about the origins of the decision to eliminate anti-doping tests for the national team, Buffet responded: "We must have been given instructions at the ministerial level."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan

Gianni Infantino's is under more pressure than ever before and it appears things are only getting harder for the beleaguered FIFA president

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's position at FIFA may be coming under threat (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino has been blasted in a leaked email by FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom. The pressure is mounting on the beleaguered FIFA boss, who was forced to ditch his contentious plan to create a commercial subsidiary which can essentially sell stocks in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

‌



A furious backlash from the football world forced Infantino into ditching his reviled vision, after UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation publicly revoked his pitch. At the time of writing, the Welsh Football Association, the Swedish FA and the Serbian FA have withdrawn their support for him, with many more tipped to follow suit.

‌



Infantino's grand plan has also been hated from within, as his senior adviser on global strategy and governance Carlos Cordeiro resigned, while Arsene Wenger also publicly stated ditching the vision was "the right thing to do." The anger has not stopped there, as a leaked email from Grafstrom demonstrated.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In an extraordinary message sent to those who work for the governing body of world football, Grafstrom appeared to suggest Infantino's days as the boss of FIFA are numbered.

It read: "A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

‌



"We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 Member Associations, hand in hand with all relevant stakeholders and in full compliance with the FIFA Statutes and FIFA Regulations.

View 3 Images Grafstrom (right) lashed into Infantino (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

‌



"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.

View 3 Images Infantino seemingly has a mutiny on his hands (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"I also want you to know that my door remains open for you, and I will continue to support our teams, our work and our mission every hour of every day for as long as my work is valued by those we serve."

‌



Grafstrom is the latest senior figure within FIFA to have communicated his anger at the recent drama, either publicly or from within. The pressure looks set to be cranked up on the Swiss football bureaucrat.

UEFA threatened to launch legal action against Infantino's plan, warning him it's "actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints" while also warning him "any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice – or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated – may constitute spoliation of evidence."

Sports.title: Man Utd exploit Premier League loophole to announce world-leading £20m deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd exploit Premier League loophole to announce world-leading £20m deal

Manchester United have announced a substantial new sponsorship deal with Betway ahead of the 2026/27 season, when gambling companies will be banned from the front of shirts

View 3 Images Manchester United have struck a £20m-per-season deal with Betway (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have struck a multi-year sponsorship deal worth £20million per season with Betway. The gambling company will be visible on United's training kit and around Old Trafford on matchdays as part of the deal, which covers the men's and women's teams.

‌



The Premier League giants went the 2025/26 campaign without a training kit sponsor and are delighted to have changed that ahead of the new season kicking off. Despite being worth less than their previous deal with blockchain company Tezos, which brought in £24m-a-season, United are delighted with a deal bigger than any other standalone training kit or playing shirt sleeve deals in world football.

‌



Marc Armstrong, chief business officer at United, said: "The scale of our exciting new partnership reflects our growth strategy, the enduring global strength and appeal of Manchester United, and our ability to attract leading brands that want to engage with our vast worldwide fanbase."

‌



The sponsorship will run alongside United's £60m-a-season sponsorship deal with electronics company Snapdragon, who will continue to be displayed on the front of their shirts.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

The 2026/27 Premier League season is the first in which gambling companies are not allowed on the front of shirts. Premier League clubs agreed to get rid of gambling companies back in April 2023 and the rule has now come into effect.

‌



However, although gambling companies are gone from the front of shirts, they are still allowed on the sleeves and training kits, as well as being plastered all over stadiums via advertising hoardings.

It is a loophole that campaigners warned the Premier League about last year after research showed how teams in foreign leagues that had implemented a similar gambling ban easily found ways around it.

View 3 Images Betway will be visible on Manchester United's training kit (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



As Nick Harvey from the Coalition to End Gambling Ads (CEGA) told Mirror Football: “With tens of thousands of ads still plastered across stadiums, shirt sleeves and the media, removing shirt-front logos is already just a gesture."

While six top-flight clubs have been able to swap out their previous gambling deals for non-gambling front-of-shirt sponsors, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland are currently set to begin the campaign without a sponsor, having been unable to strike a deal. Meanwhile, Chelsea are also sponsor-less after their short-term deal with AI company IFS expired.

Although United are yet to find a sleeve sponsor for the upcoming season, they are right to flag their "enduring global appeal". Manchester Evening News reports that United held off agreeing deals with other companies in order to wait for a better one with Betway.

‌



View 3 Images Snapdragon are still Manchester United's front-of-shirt sponsor (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Sean Connell, editor of The Sponsor, an independent sponsorship research and valuation publication, recently told Mirror Football about the widening gap between the 'Big Six' Premier League sides and the rest when it comes to sponsorship.

"The gambling ban has taken what was already a shrinking pool of sponsors and removed a healthy chunk of those," Connell said. "It’s created what I believe is the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment that Premier League clubs have ever faced."

‌



Before the ban, Gambling companies had been willing to pay mid-table Premier League sides twice what other companies offered for sponsorship deals. It means that many clubs have been forced to shake hands on sponsorships worth considerably less this season.

Betway have become United's 'principle partner' but are also betting partners of Arsenal, Manchester City, Chelsea, Brighton, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Fulham in the Premier League.

Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai explains Liverpool post-match 'spat' and change players will make

Dominik Szoboszlai has poured water on any possible spat with Curtis Jones after the pair were seen having a heated conversation after a Liverpool pre-season outing

View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones were seen clashing after Liverpool's game last week

Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai has cleared up any talk of a bust up with Curtis Jones - but admitted that frank discussions should take place in the changing room, rather than on the pitch

‌



‌



The pair were seen clashing following the win over Wrexham in New York last week. The academy graduate was visibly frustrated at full-time and was seen having words with Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas.

‌



The issue reportedly came about after Tsimikas was given given the armband once Szoboszlai came off in second-half and videos of the discussion went viral on social media, forcing the Hungarian to address the situation.

Szoboszlai has played down the magnitude of the incident but maintained he would love to step up into a leadership role following Andy Robertson's exit - leaving the vice captaincy absent.

He said: "It was never a debate between us three. We just discussed something on the pitch. What (which) actually after you guys make it very big.

‌

4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality READ MORE :

"But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. But no, nobody was angry at no one. It's all cleared. We are cool, everybody. No, there hasn't been any conversation [about the vice captaincy]. Obviously we have Virgil as the captain.

"We have Alisson. We have Joe Gomez. So there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here. Joe is injured. I was very proud moment to have it. And let's see. It's not my choice. It's not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain in Liverpool FC, you're going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me. But I respect everybody."

View 2 Images The Hungarian had been wearing the armband and is keen for a leadership role

‌



Liverpool have maintained that clashes like that are part of an elite environment and Szoboszlai and Jones have since been seen laughing together at an opening training session in Chicago.

Jones has just under a year remaining on his contract at Anfield and Liverpool are naturally trying to avoid losing him on a free transfer. Inter Milan have made repeated attempts to try and sign the versatile Reds star but have now seen three bids turned down.

The Premier League side are sticking to their valuation, which is a minimum of £35million. The Reds were dealt a reality check in the US when they blew a lead to lose 4-2 to Leeds as Andoni Iraola continues his push for more new signings.

Sports.title: Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing
Sports.content:
Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing

The top jockey received the hefty sentence by Sandown stewards for easing up on a horse who was subsequently beaten by a nose last month

View 3 Images Thunder Home (far side) is caught on the line by Zero Error (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Rossa Ryan won a partial victory against a massive 28-day riding ban at an appeal hearing on Tuesday.

‌



The 26-year-old rider, who is in third place in the Flat jockeys championship behind Billy Loughnane and Oisin Murphy, was found guilty of ‘failing to take all reasonable and permissible measures to obtain the best possible placing on a horse that would have finished first’ when he rode Thunder Home, who finished second in a race at Sandown last month.

‌



The James Horton-trained runner had led nearly all the way until he was caught right on the line by the fast-finishing Zero Error who won by a nose under Jamie Spencer.

‌



Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

At an appeal before a BHA disciplinary panel, BHA regulatory counsel Catherine Daly said Ryan’s mount had been four lengths clear with half a furlong of the 7f race to run but the jockey then “places both his hands back on the reins” and then “can be clearly seen to stop riding with said vigour” for about three strides, or one second.

“It is my case that this horse clearly would have won this race had Mr Ryan not eased off,” he said. “It’s not a matter of ‘could’ have won.”

In his evidence Ryan described Thunder Home as an inexperienced two-year-old who had “worked incredibly hard” to establish his advantage.

‌



View 3 Images Rossa Ryan: had his ban reduced to ten days (Image: PA)

“I put my stick down because the horse has given me everything,” he said. “When I put my stick down my horse’s speed is decreasing. His stride isn’t but his speed is. I am really starting to feel the hill in Sandown.

“He’s been alone in front from the get-go. Late on he has changed his legs to try and stretch again and he can’t. What the BHA argue I don’t agree with. I’m actually adjusting my body.. I have never stopped riding my mount.”

‌



He later added: “I think Mr Spencer would have won either way.”

During cross-examination Daly quoted the Sandown inquiry transcript in which Ryan had admitted he ‘thought he had the race won’ and that he expected Thunder Home to ‘coast to the line, not a problem. There is one stride I missed where you can make an argument that I didn’t fully extend my hands’.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Daly asked: “Did you ease off and stop applying the same pressure because you expected he’d coast to the line?”

Ryan said: “I didn’t ease off. I adjusted what I’d seen fit to the horse on the day. When I emphasise ‘coast’ I mean as in he doesn’t need the stick. He’s given me everything.”

He admitted not knowing Spencer was closing. Daly asedk: “If you had realised Mr Spencer was there you would have kept riding with the same vigour that you had been riding and your horse would have won the race, wouldn’t it?” “No.” said Ryan.

‌



Ryan’s solicitor Rory Mac Neice said: “Keeping a horse in balance is imperative. This horse is a two-year-old. It was the first time in its life it had been in front for the whole race. It was tiring. It shifts left at the very point we see the alteration in Mr Ryan’s riding. The horse then changed its lead which allows the horse to flatten and Mr Ryan immediately flattens with it.

“That adjustment is reasonable in the circumstances of this race and the horse he is riding.”

View 3 Images Jockey Jamie Spencer: rider of winner Zero Error

‌



Panel chair HH James O'Mahony said the BHA had presented “a classic case of a jockey easing down when he thought he had the race won”, adding, “And he hadn't realised that with a typical, perhaps, Jamie Spencer, run, if I may be permitted to say that, he was coming with great knots on his outside to, as it were, nick the race.”

Ryan’s case was that he adjusted his riding “by moving his body weight to the rhythm of the horse in circumstances where the horse was declining in strength and impetus at that stage of the race, and that that was a perfectly proper thing for a jockey to do”.

He added: “On the balance of probabilities, we prefer the BHA account, and we conclude that it is the correct account.”

Article continues below

However the panel ruled that this race was one Ryan “could, and not would” have won. ”And in those circumstances, it's not compulsory to impose a sanction of 28 days. The appropriate figure is one of 10 days.”

The ban will begin on August 6.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
