World.title: President Hichilema Orders Jobs for Mufulira Volunteers
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has directed that all volunteer nurses and teachers in Mufulira District be employed.

Speaking during a community engagement meeting in Mufulira District, President Hichilema instructed the United Party for National Development (UPND) aspiring Members of Parliament candidates to compile a list of the names of volunteers for employment.

The President reiterated his commitment to continue creating more jobs for youths, highlighting that in the last four years, his government has employed 45,000 teachers,20,000 health workers and many more officers in the army, Zambia National Service,and Police.

“I Hakainde Hichilema,umubomfi wenu (your servant) have made a decision that all volunteer teachers and nurses will be employed, “the President said.

“God works through people and today He has used me to employ you,” Mr Hichilema added.

Meanwhile, the President urged Mufulira residents to vote for the UPND in order to enable them complete the various infrastructural projects being undertaken in the district.

“Vote for us so that we complete the Mufulira-Ndola Road, Mufulira-Mokambo Road, Kamuchanga Modern Market, and the Mufulira District Hospital,” Mr Hichilema said.

He stated that once re-elected, the UPND will continue with the social cash transfer programme, the cash for work Programme and the free education.

“In the Patriotic Front government children were failing to go to school due to lack of school fees, but due to our free education policy,2.5 million children have gone back to school, “he said.

Meanwhile, Mr Hichilema said he wants youths to conduct mining activities safely and legally.

Mr Hichilema said he is in the process of facilitating for youths to legally and safely mine at dump sites urging them to be patient and desist from illegal mining activities.

“No responsible parent would want their children to go and mine in where they can die, Bally is a responsible parent and I want youths to mine safely, no guns and no violence, “the President said.

President Hichilema said his government will also embark on the construction of Township Roads in Mufulira.

Meanwhile former Copperbelt Minister, Elisha Matambo highlighted some of the achievements of the New Dawn government.

Mr Matambo said the UPND government has constructed 6 level one hospitals, and also commenced construction of Mufulira District Hospital which had stalled for several years.

“Hospitals had no equipment and no drugs but under our government we bought equipment and medicines are now available,” he said.

Mr Matambo said the UPND have made several scores including resuscitating Mopani Copper Mine and Konkola Copper mine, the Free Education and building up of government reserves.

World.title: President Hichilema Salutes Dr Monze’s Exemplary Public Service
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has described late Southern Province Permanent Secretary Namani Monze as a dependable public servant who served the Zambian people with integrity, commitment and humility during his tenure in public office.

Dr Monze was laid to rest at his family farm in Bwacha Ward of Choma District, where mourners gathered to pay their final respects, with First Lady Mutinta Hichilema among those in attendance.

The President, in a speech read on his behalf by Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa, said Dr Monze distinguished himself through dedicated service across key sectors including health, education and infrastructure development.

“He was a dependable public servant who served with integrity, commitment and humility,” he said

President Hichilema further paid tribute to Dr Monze’s calm leadership style, noting that he was a civil servant who avoided controversy and instead focused on delivering results for the people.

He said such qualities were rare and worthy of emulation by those currently serving in government.

” Dr Monze understood public office and executed his duties with diligence, his death was a profound loss to the public service and the nation at large”, he said.

He also emphasized that government would remember Dr Monze not only for his professional contributions but also for his ability to work with communities and traditional leaders in fostering development at the grassroots level.

The President said his spirit of collaboration had helped strengthen service delivery in Southern Province.

The Head of State further extended his condolences to the bereaved family, urging them to take comfort in the legacy of service and respect that Dr Monze left behind.

“I encourage you to remain strong, as the nation stands with you during this difficult period of mourning”, he reiterated.

And Chief Hamusonde, speaking on behalf of other traditional leaders in Southern Province, praised Dr Monze for his responsiveness and inclusive leadership style.

“He was always prompt in responding to the needs of the people and made it easy for chiefdoms to work with government,” he said.

The Chief remarkably commended Dr Monze ‘s humility saying that his genuine interest in people knew no social status.

The chief also urged family members to continue comforting the widow and the children and warned against property grabbing.

The church, represented by Dr Vanny Munyumbwe, offered words of comfort to the bereaved family, urging them to remain strong and anchored in faith during the period of mourning.

“He was a dedicated Christian who supported the church and lived a life guided by faith and service,” she said.

And widow, late Dr Monze’s wife, Joleha Monze, described her late husband as a loving and respectful man who valued family and treated everyone with kindness.

“He was a caring man who showered me with love and respect and always put his family first,” she said.

The children remembered their father as a joyful and principled man who instilled values of integrity and humility in the family.

“My father was a cheerful man who lived with integrity and humility and always encouraged us to do what is right,” she said.

Family members, including his sister Kabanga Malekwa, described Dr Monze as a pillar of strength whose leadership extended beyond his professional life into the wider community.

“He was a pillar of strength to our family and a man who united everyone around him,” she said.

Though Dr Namani Monze has been laid to rest, mourners said his legacy of humility, dedication and service to the people of Southern Province will continue to inspire future generations.

The burial was also attended by former Southern Province Minister Credo Nanjuwa and, former Minister of Information and Media Cornelius Mweetwa.

Others who attended the burial include Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo kawana, Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe and other senior government and UPND officials.

Dr Monze 52, died on 28th July 2026, and he is survived by a wife and four children.

World.title: Government Calls for Collective Action Against GBV
World.content:
Government has called for collective action to address teenage pregnancy, Gender Based Violence (GBV) and substance abuse among young people in Chadiza District.

Speaking during an Adolescent Health Awareness Walk held in Chadiza under the theme “Breaking the Cycle: Preventing Teenage Pregnancy, GBV and Substance Use,” Acting District Commissioner (DC)Masauso Mwale said child marriages, drug abuse, school dropouts and sexual abuse continue to affect many young people.

He said this in remarks made on his behalf by Chadiza District Community Development Officer, Charles Situmbeko.

The Acting DC said the challenges not only affect individual lives but also socio-economic development in the community.

“I encourage parents, teachers, traditional leaders, religious leaders, health workers, cooperating partners and young people to continue working together to protect every adolescent,” he said.

He mentioned that young people need safe spaces where they can learn, receive guidance, develop skills, access information and stay away from harmful activities.

Meanwhile, Chadiza District Health Director, Bless Shimuunza, said the awareness walk is worthwhile because it has brought positive change in Chadiza, specifically for adolescents.

Dr Shimuunza said government, in partnership with organisations such as Plan International and She Soars, is conducting sensitization programs in different areas of Chadiza to educate adolescents.

“We go round in different areas of Chadiza sensitizing adolescents,” he said.

World.title: President Hichilema Promises Revival of Chambishi metals
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called on the residents of Chambishi to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the forth coming general elections on August 13th to enable the government to continue implementing its agenda.

The Head of state explained that voting for the UPND means continued development in the country.

Speaking during the community engagement at twalubuka schools grounds in Chambishi, in Kalulushi district on the Copperbelt Province, President Hichilema says his government will work on the reopening of Chambishi metals if re-elected in the August 13 general elections.

“We are going to re-open the Chambishi metals if you are going to vote for us in the forthcoming elections,” President Hichilema said.

The Head of state said government will continue engaging stakeholders over the Chambishi dumpsite to enhance mining activities, while stressing the need for legal and safe mining practices.

” We want to work on legalising mining activities, no parent wants to see their children dying anyhow like that,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that he will work on paying all the ex-miners that were not paid a long time ago.

He advised the residents of Chambishi not to make a mistake of voting for political parties that were busy copying the UPND manifesto.

The Head of State also disclosed that if re-elected into office, the UPND administration will pay for 16,000 people in Kabaso area to be connected to the national gride.

President Hichilema added that farmers will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser once the UPND is re-elected.

” When you vote for us in these coming elections, I assure you that you will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that the Food Reserve Agency will be paying farmers within two days through their mobile money accounts.

He further directed Zesco limited to connect about 16,000 people from Kabaso area to the national electricity grid, stating that high connection charges should not prevent citizens from accessing power.

President Hichilema further announced that government will improve radiology services at Chambishi Hospital and rehabilitate township roads in the area.

He added that government remained committed to resolving the outstanding payments for former miners who are yet to receive their dues.

The President noted that the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) has been increased from K1.8 million to K40.8 million per constituency to accelerate community development in the country.

World.title: Nora demands action as Beijing ‘withholds’ Mukoma from WAFCON
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia has officially complained to FIFA and CAF over the failure by Chinese Women’s Super League side Beijing to release Copper Queens striker Fridah Mukoma for the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

Mukoma was among the 26 players summoned by Zambia coach Nora Häuptle for WAFCON and was expected to join camp by 20th July.

Speaking ahead of Zambia’s decisive Group C match against Malawi on Wednesday night, Häuptle confirmed the matter has been escalated.

“Fridah Mukoma was not released by her club in China. She is one of our top players and she is not getting released by her club,” Häuptle said.

“We have escalated this matter to CAF and now to FIFA. We expect action from CAF and FIFA because clubs must respect the release of players to national teams,” she said.

“I mean national teams have authority over players. I expect punishment from her team in Beijing. This is a clear issue,” Häuptle added.

The non-release has deprived the Copper Queens of a key attacking option as they fight to advance to the quarterfinals.

Zambia must beat Malawi on Wednesday night to progress from Group C.

FIFA regulations compel clubs to release players for official national team duty during international windows, with sanctions possible for non-compliance.

World.title: The Dangerous Return of PF Staged Political Violence
World.content:
By Michael Lombe

Zambia has been here before. And we must not go back. The Patriotic Front has a documented history of manufacturing crises to play the victim and stoke division. The most notorious chapter came under Mr Steven Kampyongo as Minister of Home Affairs, but the script was written earlier.

Under the late President Michael Sata, the PF conjured an imaginary group called “Tonga under Oaths”. The then Lusaka Province Police Commissioner, Ms Charity Katanga, was deployed to give it weight. The claim was grotesque: that the group had killed a Bemba child in Mazabuka and was ordering all Bemba people out of Southern Province.

President Sata saw through it. While swearing in Mr Wynter Kabimba as Justice Minister, he dismissed the tale outright. Turning to the then Defence Minister, Mr Geoffrey Bwalya Mwamba, one of the architects of the plot, he said the idea was fake and must be dropped immediately before it caused war.

The PF did not stop. Next came the story that Bemba fishermen were being chased off the Kafue River. The Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit delivered tents to “displaced” people who did not exist. The lie collapsed.

Then came the market fires and the gassings. Hundreds died including schoolchildren. Paid voices were lined up to blame the then opposition leader, Mr Hakainde Hichilema and the UPND. That too failed, because Zambians refused to be baited.

Now, in opposition, the PF and its Tonse Alliance appear to be dusting off the same playbook.

Leaked reports reveals a plan to stage attacks on their own campaign teams as they tour Southern Province. Recruits, it is said will be hired, masked, and instructed to stone their own vehicles in Monze, Choma and Kalomo. Media teams will be on standby. The purpose is clear: run back to Eastern and Northern provinces with video and say, “This is what Southerners are doing to us.”

If these allegations are true, they are not politics. They are sabotage.

This is the politics of arson, not argument. It seeks power not through policy, but through fear, tribal baiting, and staged blood.

Zambians rejected this in 2016. They rejected it in 2021. They will reject it again in 2026.

We owe it to the market traders, the schoolchildren, and the farmers who paid the price last time to say it plainly: do not light this country on fire for votes.

The law must act. The public must watch. And the media must not be used as a prop in a staged drama.

The past has instructed us. Let us not repeat it.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 4, 2026
World.content:
DR Congo Audit Confirms Oil Pollution Findings

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Hydrocarbons expects to complete and publish a full environmental audit of oil company Perenco by the end of September. This comes after preliminary findings that identified pollution linked to the company's operations. A ministry official said the audit found negative impacts on soil and air quality, with ageing infrastructure and pipelines contributing to environmental damage. The findings broadly support a recent Human Rights Watch report alleging that Perenco's activities, including gas flaring, open burning of oil waste and oil spills, have polluted air, soil and water sources and posed health risks to nearby communities. Perenco has denied causing pollution. However, the government said that the final report will recommend environmental remediation measures and infrastructure upgrades.

Benin Launches New Senate Chamber



Benin has launched its new Senate, a second chamber of parliament designed to beef up legislative oversight and protect the country's constitutional order. The Senate will scrutinise laws, request second readings of bills and has the power to block constitutional, electoral and political party reforms it deems a danger to democracy, peace or national unity. It can also suspend or revoke the political rights of public officials accused of undermining state institutions or social cohesion. Supporters say the chamber will provide better checks and balances and preserve Benin's democratic traditions. Its legitimacy has been challenged by critics, who warn that, because its members are appointed, not directly elected, it could undermine democratic accountability.

AI-Enabled Cybercrime on the Rise Across Africa

More than half of all reported cybercrimes across Africa are now powered by artificial intelligence, according to INTERPOL's 2026 African Cyberthreat Assessment Report. The report found that 55% of reported cybercrime incidents involved AI-enabled tools. Cybercrime is becoming increasingly automated and transnational, with financial losses across the continent more than doubling since 2024 to an estimated $484 million, the report said. The most common threat remains online scams, where criminals are increasingly using AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems and commit fraud. INTERPOL also highlighted the growing threat of phishing, ransomware and mobile money fraud, calling on governments and businesses to shore up cybersecurity as organised criminal networks exploit AI to mount faster and more sophisticated attacks across Africa.

Zimbabwe's Examination Board Releases June 2026 Exam Results

The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results. Candidates are able to access them online via the ZIMSEC portal. The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell to 3%, down from 5.87% in 2025. The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates passing at least two subjects rose by 11.88% points to 67.74%. ZIMSEC said the online results portal will remain open for five days. Printed results will be available for collection by examination centre heads from regional offices.

Close 

UN Opens Major Ebola Treatment Centre in DR Congo

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest-ever Ebola outbreak. The virus has spread to 49 health zones across several provinces, with Ituri accounting for the vast majority of infections and deaths. In response, the United Nations and its partners are opening the country's largest Ebola treatment centre, with a capacity of 100 beds, alongside a new transit centre to improve early detection and referrals. WHO has warned that a major scale-up of response efforts is urgently needed. They cite conflict, displacement, cross-border movement and worsening humanitarian conditions as key factors driving the rapid spread of the disease.

World.title: South Africa: Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban - South African News Briefs - August 4, 2026
World.content:
Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban

Residents of Adams Mission, south of Durban, have accused government water tanker drivers of selling water that should be supplied free of charge, following the death of 43-year-old Celani Zungu, reports EWN. Community members allege Zungu was trying to stop a tanker from leaving without delivering water to residents when he was struck and killed by the vehicle. Local councillor Thembelihle Makhanya said there is no concrete evidence of water being sold. He condemned the allegations if proven true. Police are investigating a case of culpable homicide, while the eThekwini Municipality has launched an internal investigation.

Westbury Residents March Against Gang Violence



Residents of Westbury in Johannesburg are set to march, demanding decisive action to curb persistent gang violence and drug-related crime, reports SABC News. Community leader Bishop Dulton Adams said residents are calling for long-term solutions rather than temporary police deployments. He argued that law enforcement has a lack of a visible presence in the neighbourhood. He criticised authorities for failing to patrol the area adequately and urged stronger policing and sustained interventions to tackle gangsterism.

Parliament Defends GBVF Council Picks

Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities has defended its recommendations for the newly appointed Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Council, rejecting criticism from COSATU over the absence of a labour representative, reports EWN. Committee chairperson Liezl van der Merwe said the selection process was fair, legally compliant and based on candidates' experience and expertise. COSATU maintains the council should include organised labour and plans to challenge the appointments. Parliament has said that legal advice confirms that labour representation is not a legislative requirement under the GBVF Act.

World.title: Somalia: Cabinet Officials Brace to Relinquish Kenyan Passports After Presidential Ultimatum
World.content:
A mounting cohort of senior Somali government ministers is poised to surrender their Kenyan passports and national identity documents within days, heeding President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's ultimatum that dual citizens holding public office must forswear their foreign nationality or immediately vacate their posts, according to multiple informed sources.

The impending wave of surrenders represents the most aggressive enforcement of citizenship integrity standards within the executive branch in recent memory, building on Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji's unilateral decision to return his Kenyan travel documents,a move that effectively set a binding precedent for his cabinet colleagues.

Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji became the first senior figure to bow to the directive when he formally handed over his Kenyan passport to the Kenyan Embassy in Mogadishu earlier this week.



In a terse statement, Jibril asserted the move was designed to guarantee "complete transparency" in the execution of his official duties and to preempt any challenge to his national allegiance.

Sources who spoke to Dalsan on condition of anonymity, citing lack of authorisation to engage publicly on the matter, disclosed that several ministers and state ministers are now finalising arrangements to submit their Kenyan travel credentials and identification cards to the diplomatic mission. The sources indicated that the officials are acting with haste to avoid being perceived as defying the President's edict, which was first articulated during a closed-door cabinet sitting last Thursday.

"The President made it unequivocally clear that retaining a foreign passport while occupying a senior government portfolio is untenable," one source told Dalsan. "Those who intend to retain their cabinet seats are moving swiftly to comply, and a series of handovers is widely anticipated before the week concludes."

The directive has cast a harsh glare on the prevalence of dual citizenship among Somalia's political elite--a sensitive issue long left unaddressed but now thrust into the open.

Although Somalia's provisional constitution does not explicitly outlaw dual nationality for public officials, the President's order effectively imposes a new litmus test for the upper echelons of power, compelling officials to choose definitively between their Somali responsibilities and foreign entitlements.

The enforcement drive comes against the backdrop of heightened scrutiny of senior officials' travel documentation, with some figures having recently encountered obstacles at Kenyan ports of entry.

State Minister at the Presidency Abdirashid was among those reportedly turned away by Kenyan immigration authorities, although it remains unclear whether that incident directly precipitated the presidential directive.

Close 

Villa Somalia has yet to issue a formal communiqué on the enforcement timeline, and the Kenyan government has likewise refrained from commenting on the expected influx of surrendered documents. However, insiders suggest the list of compliant officials will expand as the President's unannounced deadline looms, with further developments expected imminently.

World.title: West Africa: Ecowas Pledges U.S.$250,000 for June 29 Flood Victims
World.content:
An area in Accra flooded after heavy afternoon rain (file photo).

THE Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has pledged US$250,000, equivalent to about GH¢3 million, to support victims of the June 29 floods that ravaged parts of Ghana.

The donation, announced by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, is expected to bolster ongoing relief efforts for thousands of people affected by the disaster.

In a Facebook post, Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had received official notification from the ECOWAS Commission on the assistance.

He said the funds would be transferred in full to the appropriate state institutions immediately after they are received by the ministry.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Related Articles

"The transfer will be done in the interest of transparency and accountability," the minister assured.

Mr Ablakwa expressed the government's gratitude to ECOWAS for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of solidarity and genuine African compassion at a difficult time for the country.

The June 29 floods affected communities in seven regions, claiming lives, displacing thousands of residents and destroying homes, roads and other infrastructure.

Government agencies, supported by humanitarian organisations and other stakeholders, have since been providing relief to affected families while efforts continue to restore livelihoods in the flood-hit communities.

The ECOWAS support is expected to complement the government's ongoing response to the disaster and bring relief to victims.

The June 29 floods, triggered by hours of torrential rainfall, submerged several communities across seven regions, including Greater Accra, causing widespread destruction to homes, businesses, roads and other public infrastructure.

The disaster claimed several lives, displaced thousands of residents and left many households stranded, with emergency response teams undertaking rescue operations while government agencies and humanitarian organisations provided relief items to affected families.

President John Dramani Mahama subsequently visited some of the worst-hit communities, describing the situation as a national tragedy and assuring victims of government's commitment to provide immediate relief and support reconstruction efforts.

The ECOWAS intervention is expected to complement ongoing government and humanitarian assistance aimed at easing the plight of affected families and supporting the recovery of flood-hit communities.

World.title: Uganda: 14 Killed As Truck Crashes Into Taxi in Lwera
World.content:
At least 14 people have been confirmed dead in a grisly accident in Lwera swamp along the Kampala -Masaka Highway.

The accident according to Greater Masaka Regional Police spokesperson, Twaha Kasirye, happened at around 11pm on Monday at Kamunga Trading Centre in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District.

"The accident involved a Toyota Hiace taxi (UA 662AQ) and a Sino truck (UBS 040F) transporting sand. Fourteen (14) people died on the spot, all from the taxi," Kasirye said.

He added that four other people, including two occupants from each vehicle, sustained injuries and were rushed to Masaka Regional Referral Hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said police officers visited and documented the scene, while investigations into the cause of the crash are ongoing.

"Investigations are underway as efforts to trace the fleeing driver are ongoing."

The development comes as concerns over fatalities on Ugandan roads continue.

At least 37 people died in major road accidents within 10 days in July 2026, with four major crashes involving public transport vehicles, including three school buses carrying learners on educational trips and one passenger service bus.

The deadliest incident occurred on July 17 in Kapchorwa District, where 21 people, including 20 pupils of King David Junior School in Ndejje, Kampala, and one adult, died after their bus crashed while returning from a study tour at Sipi Falls.

The Isuzu bus, registration number UA 108BQ, reportedly developed mechanical problems before the fatal crash at Chekwatit Village, Kimawa Parish, Kawowo Sub-county.

Police preliminary investigations indicated that the driver lost control of the vehicle, which veered off the road, struck a large stone and overturned.

The tragedy raised concerns over the safety checks conducted before school trips and whether vehicles transporting learners meet the required safety standards.

Days earlier, on July 7, 2026, another fatal crash at Bobi Trading Centre along the Kampala-Gulu Highway claimed 14 lives and left 28 others injured.

The crash involved a passenger bus, registration number UBE 110H, belonging to OPIT Travellers Company, and a Mercedes-Benz Actros trailer, registration numbers KBS 564D/ZE 7948.

According to police findings, the bus driver was speeding and lost control while attempting to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road, resulting in a head-on collision with the trailer.

The police annual traffic report for 2025 indicated that Uganda registered 26,044 road crashes, indicating a 3.7% increase from the figure registered in 2024.

Close 

Of these, 4,602 were fatal, rising from the 4,434 reported in 2024 while 18,444 people got serious injuries and 3,668 got minor injuries.

In the accidents, men accounted for 83% of all the deaths while October with 523 deaths registered the highest fatalities.

World.title: South Africa: Anger After Farmers Dump Rotting Fruit Near Homes
World.content:
Farmers would never do this in their own suburbs, say Eastern Cape residents

Residents of Patensie, Eastern Cape, say farmers dumped truckloads of rotting fruit, nets and other farm waste on land earmarked for a housing project.

Kouga Local Municipality removed 14 truckloads of waste and says the illegal dumping has been referred to law enforcement for investigation.

Acht Boerdery says it has a longstanding arrangement to provide waste fruit for animals and denies dumping the nets and cables. Waterwiel Boerdery says it only left flood-damaged netting at the site after people requested it, and has since removed the material. Quacha Boerdery did not respond.

Residents of Patensie in the Eastern Cape have accused farmers of dumping truckloads of oranges and lemons, as well as farm equipment on land near their homes. They say farmers "would never do this in their own suburbs".

The rotting fruit attracted insects, as well as pigs and cattle, and created a heavy stench over Ramaphosa Village. Meanwhile, discarded nets, cables and irrigation pipes littered the site.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Kouga Local Municipality has cleared the area, removing 14 truckloads of waste.

The open land in Stuurmanskop is earmarked for a housing project.

Community leader Eric Blaauw posted on the What's Happening in Patensie Facebook page on 19 July: "New illegal dumping site by our farmers around Patensie. This is not good at all for the health and safety of our kids. This area is for housing development, not dumping. We're really being undermined."

Ward 10 councillor Mbandana Msingathi Gerald said he was alerted on 19 July to complaints about the stench from rotten lemons. Residents accused Acht Boerdery and Quacha Boerdery of dumping the fruit.

"I contacted local farmers' association chairperson Grewar Oosthuizen and gave him the names of the alleged dumpers. He promised to act immediately. Nets, wires and irrigation pipes were scattered across roads in Ramaphosa Village," Gerald said.

He said cattle ate the oranges but not the lemons.

Residents had previously buried fruit and vegetables at the site, but this stopped once the site was designated for housing.

Gerald said Patensie's only dumping site closed a year ago. Residents now have to travel 15km to Hankey to dispose of waste, and many cannot afford it. He said there is no local transit site, which is a serious issue for a town that exports fruit internationally.

Kouga Local Municipality spokesperson Monique Basson said officials had acted immediately after seeing reports on social media.

Basson told GroundUp: "We removed 14 truckloads of waste. The waste management section conducted a site inspection which confirmed illegal dumping.

"The matter was referred to law enforcement for investigation with the aim of identifying those responsible and taking legal action in terms of municipal by-laws," she said.

Acht Boerdery director Christof Opperman said the farm had a longstanding arrangement with the local livestock farmers' committee and the councillor's office to provide waste product for cattle, pigs, goats and chickens in an area where the animals already graze.

Opperman said recent floods and market pressure linked to the conflict in the Middle East had affected export and juicing channels, leaving fruit it believed still suitable for livestock.

"We also use the Hankey municipal dump for other waste and were not advised that the livestock product was excessive," he said.

Opperman said the farm was not involved in dumping the nets and cables. "We remain committed to sustainable farming and would not knowingly endanger the community, its people or its animals."

Opperman said staff may take waste fruit home for personal use and for their livestock, while remaining waste fruit is taken to the agreed grazing area and residual waste is mulched.

Close 

Charl Malan of Waterwiel Boerdery said his farm only dropped off flood-damaged covering nets at the site after people requested them. He denied dumping any fruit.

"After the floods, people asked me for netting that was damaged. After it was dropped off in heaps, it was scattered around by people taking the nets. I was unaware that fruit was dumped there. That must have happened afterwards and was not done by me," Malan said.

Malan said he did not anticipate the netting would become a health hazard.

Malan said the farm regularly experiences vandalism and theft. He said he hoped giving away damaged netting would reduce theft from the farm.

Malan said that as soon as he became aware of the problem, he sent his own workers and machinery to remove the netting. GroundUp saw workers using one of Malan's tractors to collect the nets.

Quacha Boerdery did not respond to requests for comment.

World.title: Zimbabwe: ZIMSEC Releases 2026 June Exam Results - O-Level Pass Rate Drops, A-Level Performance Improves
World.content:
The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results, with candidates able to access them online from 6pm Monday.

The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell by 2.87%, from 5.87% recorded in 2025, to 3% in June 2026.

The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates who passed at least two subjects (Grade E or better) increased by 11.88% from last year, to 67.74% in 2026.

Speaking during a media briefing in Harare, ZIMSEC board chairperson Professor Paul Mapfumo said the results would be available on the examination body's online portal for only five days.

"The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council board and management would like to advise the nation of the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results.

"With effect from today, 3 August 2026 at 6pm, Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results will be accessible to all candidates and authorised personnel online through the ZIMSEC portal accessed via the ZIMSEC website.

"Please take note that this portal will be open for five days only," said Mapfumo.

Mapfumo also said heads of examination centres would begin collecting printed results for their respective schools and centres from ZIMSEC regional offices on Tuesday.

World.title: Tick-borne 'rabbit fever' spreads with cases reported near major metro area
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Health officials on Long Island are warning residents about a rare but potentially serious tick-borne illness.

Three probable cases of tularemia — also known as "rabbit fever" — have been confirmed by the Suffolk County Department of Health Services (SCDHS).

"SCDHS currently has three probable cases of tularemia this year," the agency said in a statement provided to local outlets. "Confirmation of a tularemia diagnosis requires a combination of laboratory testing and fulfillment of specific clinical or epidemiologic criteria. The laboratory testing to confirm a tularemia diagnosis may take several weeks."

NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

One case involved a 9-year-old patient who was bitten by a tick while playing outside, according to NBC4 New York. After the tick was removed, he later developed high fever, severe head and neck pain, swollen lymph nodes/glands, body aches and extreme fatigue.

After multiple doctor visits and nearly a month of illness, an infectious disease specialist diagnosed the boy with tularemia.

Although the family's yard is home to wild rabbits, the patient's mother said he never handled the animals. Doctors believe infected ticks likely fed on the rabbits before biting the boy, transmitting the bacteria, according to reports.

What to know about rabbit fever

Caused by the bacteria Francisella tularensis, the disease commonly infects rabbits, hares and rodents. However, it is zoonotic, which means it can spread from animals to humans.

The bacteria is a "tier-1 select agent," a classification given to agents and toxins that "present the greatest risk of deliberate misuse with significant potential for mass casualties or devastating effects to the economy, critical infrastructure or public confidence, and pose a severe threat to public health and safety," per the CDC.

TICK BITE ER VISITS HIT HIGHEST SEASONAL LEVEL IN YEARS AS DOCTORS WARN OF DISEASE SURGE

Although tularemia remains rare, with 196 U.S. cases reported in 2023, the disease has become more common in recent years. CDC surveillance found 2,462 cases between 2011 and 2022 — a 56% increase in incidence compared with the previous decade (2001–2010).

Daniel Ruderfer, M.D., chief of the Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Hackensack Meridian K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital in New Jersey, believes that the increase in cases is mostly due to improved microbiology detection methods.

"The traditional method of confirming cases has historically been via growth in culture and antibody testing," he previously told Fox News Digital.

"However, newer detection methods, such as PCR testing, are likely a major contributor to the increase in reported cases."

CLICK HERE TO 

Humans can contract the disease through bites from deer flies or ticks, contact with infected animals, or exposure to contaminated water or aerosols, the same source stated.

Symptoms of tularemia can vary depending on the type of disease. General symptoms include chills, headache, malaise, fatigue, anorexia, myalgia, chest discomfort, cough, severe sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, according to Ruderfer.

"Depending on the location of the infected bit or scratch, people can develop localized lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes) and a cutaneous ulcer at the infection site," he said.

"Other manifestations include conjuctivitis, pneumonia and potentially even bloodstream infections."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The death rate from the disease is typically low, less than 2%, but the CDC noted that it can be as high as 24% in rare, severe cases.

Tularemia can be treated with antibiotics, but no vaccine is currently available.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics," said Ruderfer.

Those most at risk include children between 5 and 9 years of age, older men, American Indian and Alaskan Native people, and those living in central U.S. states, according to the report.

"The infection is absolutely dangerous and potentially life-threatening if not treated with appropriate antibiotics."

The general population is not at an "obvious" risk for infection unless they come into physical contact with an infected rabbit, tick or deer fly, the expert noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Those who hunt or interact routinely with rabbits should see a doctor if they develop any concerning symptoms, he advised.

"Many factors might contribute to the higher risk for tularemia in this population, including the concentration of Native American reservations in central states and sociocultural or occupational activities that might increase contact with infected wildlife or arthropods," the CDC wrote.

World.title: WNBA fan goes viral for half-court shot horror show that left him sprawled on the court
World.content:
Few things in sports can get a fan's nerves up like being told you get to take a half-court shot at an NBA or WNBA game for cash or a car.

Sure, you could, by some miracle, make the shot, but you're more likely to embarrass yourself in front of an arena full of people... at least the ones who are still in their seats and aren't in line for a beer or the bathroom.

But, at least we can all be sure that if you take a shot, the odds of it being a worse display than one put on by a Portland Fire fan over the weekend are very, very low.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT CAUGHT HITTING LAUGHABLY BAD GOLF SHOT AFTER ALLEGEDLY DITCHING INTERVIEW

The Fire (whose logo I only just realized is a flaming rose. Seriously, I've had an easier time decoding death metal band logos) have a half-court shot competition according to their website. It's sponsored by Toyota, meaning that draining the shot earns you a brand new Toyota.

Hopefully a Land Cruiser. Those are cool.

One fan got this golden opportunity on Sunday when the Fire took on the Los Angeles Sparks and... well, let's just say that Portland area Toyota dealers were not sweating it on this one.

Oh, dear God...

ATLANTA BRAVES FAN TAUNTS THE FREEZE WITH A BLOWN KISS AND GETS PASSED IN SPECTACULAR FASHION

Rule No. 1 of half-court shots should be that whatever you do, your biggest goal is to at least hit the backboard. I'd argue it's much better to airmail that ball into the club level seats than it is to barely get it past the free throw line.

That's a rough look as it is, but imagine putting every last drop of mustard you have on the ball to the point that you go scrawling across that flaming rose logo (seriously, did anyone else not pick up on that at first?). That tells the entire crowd in attendance you gave it your all... which is normally good, but that's not enough "all."

The big winner in all of this is that guy's glasses. Talk about a snug fit. Those things were on there!

That was maybe the only thing that went right for him. If those specs had gone clattering across the hardwood, I think he would've had to change his name, move out of Portland, and start rooting for a new WNBA team.

World.title: French trans phenom Julie Tétart looks WNBA-ready — so why hasn’t the ‘inclusive’ league called?
World.content:
French trans basketball player Julie Tétart is waiting for a call from one of the inclusive WNBA teams who needs a 6'3 scoring and rebounding machine.

During the 2025-26 season for a club team in Monaco, Tétart dominated the second-tier French women's basketball Ligue 2 by dropping 21 points per game while grabbing 20 rebounds. With those numbers, the WNBA should be knocking down Tétart's door, right?

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

Far better? Are you sure?

Tétart's season was so dominant that French media was stunned when the shredded center didn't win league MVP honors. The season was still good enough to win Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year and Domestic Player of the Year.

Woke WNBA fans swear there's no clear and present trans danger to biological women. They swear this is some sort of delusion cooked up by MAGA.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

"Despite top-tier athletic performance on the court during the 2025/2026 season by Julie and Aurore, voters for the Ligue 2 Féminine de Basket Awards deliberately decided not to grant them any awards," activist group TRANSpire cried on Instagram.

Former WNBA player Audrey Sauret, who's French, spoke out in April after the MVP drama and sounded a warning to leagues around the world as to what's coming if they don't protect biological females.

"Ligue 2 serves as a kind of testing ground, to introduce trendy ideas, but by allowing them to participate in professional competitions, we create unfair competition, especially for younger players," Sauret wrote. TRANS ATHLETE WINS NEW YORK STATE GIRLS' SHOT PUT TITLE, BEATING SECOND PLACE BY MORE THAN 2 FEET

The question we had for Tétart was simple: Would you ever consider trying out for the inclusive WNBA? The trans scoring and rebounding machine seemed confused at first before realizing we were 100% serious.

"Obviously, it's a childhood dream just like for any female basketball player, but unfortunately, it's not possible," the French native wrote back.

Wait a minute, why not? The WNBA is inclusive. What are we missing here?

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"The league, yes. The country, no, haha," Tétart fired back while hinting at some sort of problem with Donald Trump's presidency.

World.title: Second lady Usha Vance gets candid about new baby, juggling four children and motherhood

FIRST ON FOX: In her first interview since the birth of her fourth child with Vice President JD Vance just a few weeks ago, Usha Vance described the joy of being a new mother all over again during a candid interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday, August 4.

The interview came on the same day the newest episode of her popular podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady," was set to go live.

"It's been really lovely so far," she said of the experience of having four children, speaking from the Vice President's Residence. "One of the things that has just been beautiful to see is how excited my older kids are about their new brother. They're always fighting over holding him. When we do diaper changes or clothes changes, one of them is always there helping. They're willing to burp him, they want to grab things for him, they want to entertain him."

JD VANCE AND WIFE USHA WELCOME FOURTH CHILD, REVEAL BABY BOY'S NAME

She added, "So there's this really great way in which their needs are complementary with his."

Vice President Vance and his wife announced the birth of their fourth child in a July 20 Instagram post, as Fox News Digital previously reported. The couple said their baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born on Sunday morning, July 19.

"We are excited to announce that our baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born this morning," the couple wrote. "Usha and the baby are happy and healthy, and our kids are overjoyed to meet their little brother."

On Tuesday in her on-camera interview with Fox News Digital, Mrs. Vance called out the importance of doing things one on one with each of her children and the baby.

"I'm sure there are going to be hiccups here and there! But for right now, they seem to be really thriving."

"They feel like they're getting their own personal time with both of us," she said.

"For example, we go out [of the residence] and do something every day. And we've been doing that since the day we came home from the hospital. So yesterday was my middle child's day, and we went to a bookstore, we went to lunch — we did a quick return at a shop, and the whole time, it was just really special.

IVANKA TRUMP AND BETTINA ANDERSON'S CLOSE BOND ON DISPLAY AT MAR-A-LAGO BRIDAL SHOWER

"And we're trying to do that all the time. Now, I'm sure there are going to be hiccups here and there! But for right now, they seem to be really thriving."

She added, "My older kids see this as only good for themselves. Like, there's only one more kid to add to their pack. The parents are now outnumbered two to one!"

She referenced the jitters she had a bit ago — and how those were swiftly put to rest, and now part of the past.

"I would say I had all sorts of angst about this. My family [had] felt so complete. My kids were growing into a new phase," said Mrs. Vance.

Now, she said, "I'm really glad that we took this plunge. I'm really glad that we decided to move into the unknown and do something that felt like a little bit of a risk to a settled and happy family dynamic because it's only become happier."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"And we're looking forward to seeing what the next few years bring."

She is also continuing to expand and develop her podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady."

The latest episode features author Jackie Oshry reading her children's book about summer camp. Mrs. Vance said the podcast is designed to encourage children not only to read books but also to imagine creating stories of their own.

"One of the things we're trying to do with this podcast is highlight authors of books to show [the children] that it's not just reading that you can do," she said. "You can imagine your own stories. You can write them yourself."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

So why this signature issue for her as second lady — and not others that she might have chosen? Mrs. Vance said that reading has long been one of her favorite hobbies and something she enjoys sharing with her own children.

She said she chose literacy as one of her key initiatives because she wanted to make "a concrete change" while serving as second lady. She noted how critical it is that children in America develop a love of, and facility with, reading from a young age.

She is also encouraging children in kindergarten through eighth grade to participate in the White House Summer Reading Challenge by reading 12 books before the end of August. Families who complete the challenge will be entered to win prizes — including a chance to visit the White House, she said.

In the waning weeks of summer, Mrs. Vance said her family is preparing for a new school year by gathering school supplies, organizing clothes and spending as much time outdoors as possible before classes begin for her older children.

"We're trying to make it a celebratory thing," she said of the family's back-to-school traditions.

"Over the month of August, we slowly get everything prepared so it doesn't come as too much of a shock when they have to wake up at 6:30 again every morning."

President Donald Trump declared in a Truth Social post right after the Vances' new baby was born, "Congratulations! A perfect baby boy for the wonderful Vance family."

World.title: Embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller requests an Ethics investigation into himself
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Embattled Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, said Tuesday he will request the House Ethics Committee to investigate domestic abuse allegations made by his ex-wife — an unusual move to try to exonerate himself amid a messy custody battle that is playing out in public view.

“In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and family. I have absolutely nothing to hide,” Miller, who has vehemently denied the allegations, said in a post on X.

“We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves,” Miller continued.

01:39 Rep. Miller vows to stay in reelection race amid abuse allegations 00:00 00:00

The two-term congressman did not say when he planned to ask the panel to probe the matter — such an investigation would likely take weeks, if not months. The House is out on its August recess and will return in September.

But the fact that he is making the request suggests Miller is not planning to drop out of his race for re-election, despite a declaration from his former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, a fellow Ohio Republican, that Miller is not fit to serve in Congress.

Earlier this week, Moreno issued a stunning statement saying Miller “needs serious psychological help” and is “a danger to my daughter,” Miller’s ex-wife, Emily Moreno, adding, “I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter.”

“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them,” Moreno added. “He should not serve in the House of Representatives.”

In the Capitol on Tuesday, Moreno became emotional when telling reporters about the toll this public feud with Miller has taken on his daughter, granddaughter and wife.

“This is truly the seventh level of hell. This has been a horrific experience for my entire family,” Moreno said.

Moreno said his daughter lives in constant fear of Miller and said he met Miller at a police station on Sunday to pick up his granddaughter.

So far, President Donald Trump is standing by Miller, though the allegations are unsettling for some congressional Republicans. Trump on Monday called the situation “a very sad thing” and said Miller, a political ally, is a “good person.”

The president said he wanted to let the families figure things out.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said the allegation that Miller engaged in domestic abuse is “none of my business. But the senator added: It just it doesn’t help. Just gives people more one more reason to be disgusted with Congress.”

Lawmakers typically do not request Ethics investigations into themselves, but it has happened before. In 2008, then-House Ways and Means Chairman Charlie Rangel, D-N.Y., asked the Ethics Committee to investigate allegations that he had improperly used congressional letterhead to rally support for an educational center named after him.

But the strategy backfired for Rangel. After a two-year Ethics probe, the panel found the longtime congressman guilty of violating 11 House ethics rules, and he was censured by the full House. Rangel had to relinquish his powerful Ways and Means gavel in the process, and he did not seek re-election in 2016.

World.title: ‘Game of Thrones’ author George R. R. Martin opens up about experiencing depression
World.content:
George R. R. Martin, author of the wildly popular “Game of Thrones” book series, shared that he’s pulled back from updating fans via his blog as he “battled sadness and depression.”

“This year has been… stressful, to say the least,” Martin wrote in a blog post published this week, titled “Better Late Than Never.” “So much has been happening, it’s been overwhelming. Some great things, exciting things. Dreams coming true. But there have been nightmares too. I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression.”

The entry marked Martin’s return to blogging since since Feb. 19. In his latest post, he thanked his “great staff of assistants,” who he said have worked tirelessly to keep him from “falling further and further behind.”

In recent years, the fantasy author has been called out by readers who complain about the delayed publication of the sixth “Game of Thrones” book, “The Winds of Winter.”

Martin addressed the criticism last year, writing in a May 2025 post that he “ought to get some other writer to pinch hit for me… I am going to die soon anyway, because I am so old. I lost all interest in ‘A Song of Ice and Fire’ decades ago. I don’t give a s--- about writing any longer, I just sit around and spend my money.”

In Monday’s post, Martin referenced his age again, writing, “The worst may be yet to come. I turned seventy-seven last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun.”

He told fans that the combination of age and depression could mean his “posts are likely to [be] short and rushed” in the immediate future, adding that his “minions” may be helping him more.

But 2026 hasn’t been all sadness for the author, he said. In his post, he highlighted the nine Emmy nominations bestowed on his “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms” on HBO Max.

Martin has won four Emmys, all as co-executive producer for “Game of Thrones.” The show won Emmys for outstanding drama series in 2019, 2018, 2016 and 2015.

This year’s awards show, which will air on NBC, takes place on Sept. 14 in Los Angeles.

“I hope to attend…” Martin wrote, “but that depends on… well, on a lot of things.”

The “beloved flyweight fighter” was “found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep,” according to a statement from UFC.

“Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene,” the UFC continued. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan’s family, friends, teammates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.”

The 5-foot-8, 125-pound Nascimento went 22-7 in his UFC career that dates back to 2011.

He lost his last bout in a split decision to Mitch Raposo on June 20 in Las Vegas.

Nascimento’s sudden death stunned the mixed martial arts community.

“Today I lost a brother — a guy who was truly one of a kind — and the pain is unbearable,” No. 3-ranked lightweight and longtime friend Charles Oliveira said in a statement.

Brazilian middleweight Caio “The Natural” Borralho called Nascimento “one of the most kind fighters that’s I’ve ever met!”

“Polite, good energy and always in good spirits! He will be missed,” he said in a social media post.

And UFC correspondent Evelyn Rodrigues called Nascimento one of “the kindest souls I’ve ever had the privilege of knowing through MMA. Rest in peace, Allan.”

World.title: Video shows moment drone burst into fireball on Russian beach
World.content:
The beach was packed, many vacationers lounging near the turquoise waters when the drone slammed into the white sand and burst into a fireball.

Russian officials said seven people, including three children, were killed and 58 others injured by the explosion in the Black Sea resort town of Gelendzhik on Monday. The explosion was captured on video and shared on social media, and verified by NBC News.

Moscow accused Ukraine of targeting civilians, which would constitute a war crime, and unleashed a barrage of aerial strikes on its neighbor. Ukraine’s attacks inside Russia come as its own civilians faced deadly Russian bombardment throughout the summer.

Ukrainian officials did not confirm they were responsible, but they also did not deny it.

“What happened today was a deliberate strike by the Kyiv regime against the civilian population — people who have absolutely no connection to military infrastructure,” Veniamin Kondratyev, the governor of the Krasnodar region, said on his official Telegram channel. “There can be no justification for such a cynical and inhumane terrorist act targeting children.”

A screen grab of a drone explosion on a beach at the holiday village of Arkhipo-Osipovka, Gelendzhik resort area, in Russia on Monday. via Reuters

The explosion comes amid a concerted Ukrainian effort to push the war’s front line closer than ever to Moscow, with strikes targeting shipping vessels, oil sites, warehouses and ammunition depots in recent weeks.

Since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched his large-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Kyiv has honed an innovative and lethal strategy of using cheaply manufactured drones as it seeks to pressure Moscow into a peace settlement. Some hit their targets, while others are often shot down.

Between July 24 and July 31, at least 61 people were killed and more than 320 wounded in Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Friday.

After the explosion in Gelendzhik, Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council’s Centre for Countering Disinformation, said: “Russian air defense shot down a drone onto people lying on the beach.”

“It was Putin who killed these Russians,” he said in a statement. “Had he not started the war and the strikes on Ukraine, they would be alive.”

Kovalenko also accused Putin of downplaying Ukrainian attacks on Russia, creating an “illusion of peace” that has made the public complacent.

“Had they acknowledged the war on their own territory, people would have reacted more actively to the alert, which in some places in Russia is not even announced,” he said.

A separate attack had also hit a warehouse in Leningrad, its regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said early Tuesday.

World.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy murder trial focuses on prescription pills
World.content:
The Lindsay Clancy murder trial resumed for a sixth day Tuesday with more testimony from prosecution witnesses and a focus on her prescriptions.

Clancy, 35, has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children — 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan — at their home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on Jan. 24, 2023.

You can watch the trial live in the embedded video, on CBS News Boston or on the CBS News Boston YouTube page once testimony begins.

Testimony about Lindsay Clancy's prescription pills

Massachusetts State Police Lt. Joseph Rabbit said he found four prescription pill bottles in a kitchen cabinet when executing a search warrant at the Duxbury home after the murders. He said Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband Patrick Clancy and a lawyer came to the district attorney's office on Feb. 6 with more prescription pill bottles in a CVS bag.

Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham pulled out pill bottles one-by-one and asked about how many pills were prescribed compared to how many were left in the bottle. The prosecution has argued that while Clancy was prescribed several drugs for her mental health struggles, she was not taking many pills from each bottle.

Lindsay Clancy's prescription medications CBS Boston

The defense maintains she was overmedicated, and say a cocktail of several prescription drugs sparked a postpartum psychosis that led to Clancy killing her children.

"These were all pills that were issued on prescriptions in about a three-week period of time," defense attorney Kevin Reddington said in his questioning.

Crime lab workers testify

Several prosecution witnesses employed at the Massachusetts State Police Crime Lab took the stand on Tuesday. There was testimony about blood collected from the home in Duxbury - jurors were shown the blood-stained knife previously seen in Clancy's bedroom.

Two Crime Lab technicians also testified that prescription drugs were detected in blood and urine tests done on Lindsay Clancy. The tests are unable to pinpoint exactly how many different drugs Clancy had in her system, they explained.

South Shore Hospital surgeon testifies

The prosecution's first witness of the day was Dr. Cristina Karpio, a general surgeon at South Shore Hospital who treated Clancy immediately after the murders. She said Clancy's complex spinal injuries from her fall out of the second-story bedroom window required a transfer to Brigham & Women's Hospital in Boston.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington asked Dr. Karpio about the severity of Clancy's injuries. The defense has tried to counter the prosecution's argument that Clancy's suicide attempt was faked.

"Did you know that your patient had coded shortly after being brought to Brigham & Women's hospital?" Reddington asked.

"No," Dr. Karpio said.

"Did you know that she had to have massive transfusions right after being brought to the hospital in Boston?" Reddington asked.

"No," Dr. Karpio said.

Lindsay Clancy agrees to "stipulation of facts"

Before the jury entered the courtroom on Tuesday, Lindsay Clancy agreed to a "stipulation of facts."

She was sworn in by a court officer and answered questions from the judge, confirming that she and the prosecution agree on certain facts in the case.

"This stipulation basically relieves the government of having to bring in dozens if not more witnesses to prove chain of custody of blood, fluids, the bands, DNA, all of that," defense attorney Reddington said. "Rather than have days of testimony, the stipulation will avoid that."

What's happened in the Lindsay Clancy trial this week?

The jury in Plymouth Superior Court heard entries from Clancy's diary Monday and testimony about her state of mind before and after the murders. She admits to killing her children but claims it was due to severe postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors say her suicide attempt was fake and premeditated and the murders were planned.

The jury has heard from 32 witnesses after five days of testimony.

If convicted, Clancy faces life in prison without a chance of parole. If she's found not criminally responsible for the deaths of her children, she will be sent to a state mental health facility in Massachusetts.

If you or someone you know is in emotional distress or a suicidal crisis, you can reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988. You can also chat with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline here.

For more information about mental health care resources and support, The National Alliance on Mental Illness HelpLine can be reached Monday through Friday, 10 a.m.–10 p.m. ET, at 1-800-950-NAMI (6264) or email info@nami.org.

World.title: Behind closed doors, Trump, White House aides hope Rep. Max Miller exits race
World.content:
Washington — Some White House officials hope embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller exits the congressional race in Ohio immediately, and President Trump has expressed a similar sentiment behind closed doors, multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter tell CBS News.

Mr. Trump called Miller on Monday and raised concerns about his reelection bid following allegations that Miller assaulted his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their 2-year-old daughter, two sources directly familiar with the call confirmed to CBS News. But Miller, who has adamantly denied the allegations, told the president he has no plans to leave the race, according to one of the sources.

Miller, the GOP nominee, has until 4 p.m. Wednesday to withdraw his candidacy and give Republicans a chance to replace him on the ballot in November. Semafor first reported that the president and some White House aides said privately that they wanted Miller out of the race.

On Tuesday morning, Miller said he would file the paperwork to launch a congressional ethics investigation into himself in an effort to clear his name.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and family," Miller wrote on X. "I have absolutely nothing to hide. We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail[ed] examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

On Monday, the president said he thought Miller was a "very good person" and said he would let the families involved resolve the situation.

"Well, it's a very sad thing," the president told reporters in the Oval Office Monday. "I know Max, he's a good person, I mean, I always thought he was a very good person. And I'm going to let the families figure that out. Those families, I know they're working on it. It's a very sad thing. Especially when you know somebody so well to be going through that. But it's accusations. And I'm going to let them figure that out."

In an earlier statement to CBS News on Monday, Miller said: "If I dropped out of this race, it would mean we as a nation have fallen so far from our American values. I will not validate false claims by removing myself just to please the court of public opinion. I am innocent of all of the allegations that have been attributed to me. I have done well representing my constituents' interests. Why would I drop out?"

Emily Moreno, Miller's ex-wife, is the daughter of Ohio GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno. The senator said in a statement on Sunday that Miller "should not serve in the House of Representatives" and "needs serious psychological help."

World.title: More adult children live at home now than during the pandemic
World.content:
A record number of adult children under 35 in the U.S. are moving back in with their parents, either because they can't afford homes of their own or because they want to save money amid the rising cost of living, according to a recent study.

In 2025, 25.2 million adults under 35 lived at home, according to Realtor.com, which found that the share of adults living with their moms and dads was higher than it was during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Many of these adults moving back in with their parents are employed, but their wages aren't keeping up with inflation. Among the 25- to 34-year-olds living at home, roughly 7 in 10 have jobs, the online real estate firm found.

Karleigh Gaudreau, a 34-year-old business coach and online content creator, is among the Americans who recently moved back home, telling CBS News she couldn't afford to live on her own after breaking up with a boyfriend she had been living with in South Carolina.

Gaudreau, who earns about $60,000 a year, said she could afford to split rent but couldn't cover the full cost alone.

"To be able to afford that on top of your student loans or car payment, it's really hard to function off of anything, I believe, less than $85,000," Gaudreau said.

""Society as a whole has to respond"

She's hardly alone in her financial struggles, as the dream of homeownership slips further out of reach for many Americans amid rising home prices and higher mortgage rates. Fewer than 4 in 10 non-homeowner households can afford a typical starter home, according to a recent LendingTree analysis.

"Society as a whole has to respond," Susan Wachter, a professor of real estate at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School of Business, told CBS News. "It's affordability across the board. It's not just the price of the home and the mortgage."

Gaudreau's plan seems to be paying off. After saving money on rent by living with her parents, she plans to move into a place of her own in November.

World.title: Eaton Fire in Altadena sparked by SoCal Edison electric tower, probe finds
World.content:
The Los Angeles County Fire Department on Tuesday released the conclusion of an 18-month investigation into the origins of the deadly and destructive Eaton Fire, determining that electrical arcing on an out-of-service transmission tower was allegedly to blame.

The report, conducted jointly between the LACFD's Arson Fire Investigation Unit and Cal Fire, determined that the arcing events "ejected hot metal particles that fell to the receptive fuel beds consisting of dry vegetation below the towers," which sits on a ridge above the Eaton Wash.

Los Angeles County Fire Department Eaton Fire Investigation Supplemental Report Page of

Starting Jan. 7, 2025, the Eaton Fire destroyed or damaged more than 9,000 homes primarily in the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena, and also affected nearby Pasadena.

The blaze took the lives of 19 people, according to the LA County Medical Examiner.

CBS LA reached out to Southern California Edison for comment, but did not immediately hear back. Last month, the utility company announced it paid more than $314 million to victims of the fire through its Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program.
