World.title: Los socios de la UE rebajan las críticas a España por la crisis de Ceuta y le muestran ahora su “total solidaridad”
World.content:
Bruselas admite que “no hay relación directa” entre la regularización y la avalancha en la frontera, aunque apunta que la medida “no es una buena señal para el resto de la Unión”

Las contundentes críticas a España por la crisis de Ceuta de los primeros días han cedido. El ministro de Interior español, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, no ha tenido que escuchar los reproches que 22 primeros ministros de la UE —todos menos cinco— lanzaron el pasado sábado en una carta contra la política migratoria española. En la reunión con sus homólogos, “no ha habido críticas reales” por la regularización, ha admitido al acabar el comisario de Asuntos de Interior, Magnus Brunner, quien ha hablado de “total solidaridad con España alrededor de la mesa”. El tono del encuentro ha sido “constructivo”, ha señalado el ministro español y corroboran varias fuentes diplomáticas conocedoras de lo sucedido en las casi cuatro horas de reunión.

“La UE está unida y dispuesta a apoyar a España. Le felicitamos por su rápida respuesta ante la situación en Ceuta y expresamos nuestro más sentido pésame por la pérdida de vidas humanas”, ha destacado el ministro de Interior irlandés, Jim O’Callaghan, quien ha presidido la reunión por ser su país el encargado del Consejo de la UE este semestre. También el titular francés del ramo, Laurent Nuñez, se ha sumado al apuntar que todos los Estados miembros “han elogiado la gestión española de la crisis y la cooperación con Marruecos”.

“Sobre la regularización, no hubo críticas reales porque no podemos ver un vínculo directo en este momento entre la medida y los incidentes de Ceuta”, ha admitido el comisario Brunner. Desde el viernes, los principales ataques contra España lanzados desde varias capitales europeas −también desde toda la derecha del Parlamento Europeo, desde la moderada hasta la más ultra− tenían un flanco: la regularización masiva de migrantes puesta en marcha hace meses. Pero este martes los golpes no han llegado por ese flanco, según el comisario austriaco y otras delegaciones. No obstante, Brunner, una de las voces más duras con este tema en Bruselas, sí ha añadido en sus respuestas al asunto: “Como siempre digo en este debate, no es una buena señal para el resto de Europa. Entiendo que España lo hizo porque son principalmente latinoamericanos que hablan la misma lengua y tienen la misma cultura, pero la señal para el resto no es buena”.

A la hora de buscar causas, Brunner y los ministros han optado este martes por mirar hacia “las redes criminales de tráfico de personas y también la desinformación”. Como tampoco ha hecho en España buena parte del Gobierno, el comisario austriaco no ha señalado a Marruecos en ningún momento, pese a que la avalancha de 72.000 personas llegó de su territorio. Ha hablado del país norteafricano como un “país seguro”, es decir, un Estado al que se pueden devolver migrantes de forma rápida sin temor, en teoría, a que corran grandes riesgos.

Este argumento está en consonancia con lo señalado por los ministros durante la reunión. Ellos han apuntado a “la necesidad de mejorar el conocimiento compartido de la situación, lo que podría lograrse mediante un mayor desarrollo de los sistemas de alerta temprana, como la información de inteligencia previa a la frontera y la vigilancia de las redes sociales”.

La intervención de Brunner ha seguido la línea de lo que ya hizo el lunes la presidenta de la Comisión, Ursula von der Leyen, en la carta que envió al presidente del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez. Asumió que la crisis en la frontera ya está prácticamente resuelta cuando se ha devuelto a Marruecos la gran mayoría de los que cruzaron irregularmente la frontera entre el jueves y el viernes. “Europa ha superado claramente esta prueba. No se logró entrar en el espacio Schengen y la seguridad en la frontera se restableció con rapidez. La clave ahora es que la Unión Europea actúe”, ha destacado en su versión inicial. No obstante, después, cuando se le ha preguntado si tenía sentido entonces plantear la suspensión de España del área de libre movimiento de personas, como hizo Italia, se ha resistido a lanzar reproche con el argumento de que las imágenes que se vieron pueden preocupar a los ciudadanos europeos. “Cuando Italia adoptó esa decisión, no disponíamos todavía de esa información”, ha justificado, utilizando el dato de que nadie de quienes cruzaron la frontera en la ciudad española del norte de África y Marruecos ha llegado a la península.

Acerca de las críticas recibidas por la fría reacción inicial de la Comisión y las diferencias con otros episodios parecidos, como los de 2021 en la frontera de Polonia y Lituania o las llegadas a Lampedusa en 2023: “La situación actual es completamente diferente porque, como he dicho antes, Marruecos es un país seguro. Y eso marca una diferencia fundamental también a la hora de proceder a los retornos, es decir, a la hora de poder repatriar a las personas. Así pues, la situación es diferente, pero nuestra reacción fue muy clara y también muy rápida”.

También desde Roma se ha buscado rebajar algo la tensión con Madrid. El titular de Interior, Matteo Piantedosi, ha tratado de rebajar las tensiones con Madrid al apuntar que ha trasladado al Gobierno español su “sincera solidaridad de Italia”. También ha apuntado que el restablecimiento temporal de los controles en las fronteras aéreas y marítimas italianas no está dirigido contra España, sino que responde a razones de seguridad y gestión de los flujos migratorios. “Se trata de una medida de carácter preventivo y organizativo, destinada a salvaguardar la seguridad nacional y la solidez de todo el sistema europeo de controles en un momento de gran presión, tal y como ha ocurrido en muchísimos otros casos”, ha señalado en la reunión con sus homólogos europeos.

Lo que sí ha hecho Piantedosi es lanzar un reproche velado a sus socios comunitarios. “Italia comprende demasiado bien la presión que está sufriendo hoy España”, ha afirmado, evocando la crisis migratoria que se registró en Lampedusa en 2023. Según el ministro, Roma tuvo que afrontar entonces la emergencia prácticamente en solitario, sin la solidaridad que esperaba de sus socios y bajo la presión de evitar los llamados “movimientos secundarios” hacia el norte de Europa. También ha criticado que, en ese contexto, Roma tuvo que hacer frente al “intenso activismo” de los barcos humanitarios de las ONG, a los que acusó de “trasladar sistemáticamente a los migrantes rescatados a puertos italianos”.

Por su parte, Núñez, el ministro francés, recordó que su país ha reforzado los controles terrestres en la frontera franco-española, que ya existen desde 2015, y se hará lo propio en la frontera con Italia. Subrayó, además, que las entradas de inmigrantes irregulares en la UE “han bajado significativamente” desde 2025.

También Brunner ha subrayado esos datos en su intervención inicial ante la prensa. “La migración ilegal ha caído un 55% en los últimos dos años, casi un 40% en lo que va de este”, ha querido destacar. “Europa nunca ha tenido tanto control sobre la migración en las últimas décadas”, ha remachado en línea con estos números. “Pero, por supuesto, los sucesos de Ceuta —eso también está bastante claro— demuestran que esas imágenes dramáticas superan, de hecho, a las mejores estadísticas, y eso es también, por supuesto, una de las lecciones aprendidas", ha zanjado.

World.title: Un verano contra el fuego en una base de León helitransportada inútil: “Tardamos hora y media en llegar en coche y volando serían 15 minutos”
World.content:
La base helitransportada de El Oterico (León) costó casi dos millones de euros, se anunció en 2022 y se destacó que a finales de 2023 estaría “prácticamente terminada”. Los bomberos que trabajan en ella en el verano de 2026 no la han podido utilizar hasta hace unos días para los medios aéreos para los que se concibió porque incumplía lo necesario en términos de seguridad y operatividad y no terminaba de estar concluida: “Tenerla inoperativa un 1 de agosto sería un error terrible”. La base, con suelo de arenisca que inhabilita la mayor parte de sus pistas, está cerrada simplemente contra el ganado por un pastor eléctrico que han dispuesto los brigadistas y los depósitos de combustible han pasado semanas desprecintados. Pese a la reciente apertura, apenas hay cobertura ni cuentan con teléfono fijo y tampoco funcionan las duchas en unas instalaciones clave para dominar la montaña central leonesa, recurrentemente castigada por los fuegos como los que a menudo se ven muy cerca desde Oterico. Un bombero expresa así el trastorno de incendios recientes: “Tardamos hora y media en coche y volando serían 15 minutos”.

Los problemas que genera esta base se añaden a que allí están desplazados los brigadistas de Camposagrado, donde no había agua potable por un escape de queroseno sobre las tuberías. Este personal entiende el primer traslado pero ven absurdo que la anterior se haya cerrado sabiendo que la nueva es inútil.

Un bombero de León conocedor de la situación censura que la única protección, un cierre perimetral con un pastor eléctrico para que no entren las vacas cercanas, la han dispuesto los propios empleados del operativo leonés: “Es un pastor eléctrico para que no entre ganado, ¿cómo vas a tener un helipuerto rodeado de un pastor eléctrico? Es de chiste”. Que no entren vacas no implica que no acceda gente a un lugar donde se posa un helicóptero valorado en dos millones, casi igual que las instalaciones completas, bajo riesgo de gamberradas o estropicios porque no está videovigilada ni vallada: “Es inaceptable, pueden ir unos chavales a tocar algo y al día siguiente volar nosotros”. La manguera de abastecimiento del carburante solo llega a una de las siete helipistas, mal menor porque se pueden ir moviendo los vehículos aéreos, pero significativo. EL PAÍS ha consultado por esta base a la consejería de Medio Ambiente pero no ha obtenido respuesta.

La ubicación, explica esta fuente, es positiva porque domina la montaña central leonesa y sería un soporte estupendo para reforzar incendios en cualquier otro sector sensible de la provincia, pero no estando a medias: no hay comunicación efectiva, la emisora sufre problemas de cobertura, carece de teléfono fijo y los trabajadores ni siquiera pueden ducharse. La bomba de aspiración no funciona, comenta este informador, y tras horas entre el humo y las llamas los compañeros de ese emplazamiento deben tirar a sus casas sin asearse.

“Riello tiene problemas de abastecimiento de agua pero hay bombas que funcionan”, suspira el confidente. Este se exaspera especialmente con el suelo de la base, otro elemento crucial que no permitía su uso hasta ahora. “Se levanta mucha arena porque es suelo rellenado, no es operativo, produce falta de seguridad y visibilidad. Es tierra de mineral, no va a crecer hierba, y no hormigón”, critica, sin que los remedios posteriores sean mejores: “Se les ocurrió la brillante idea de poner hierba artificial clavada con clavos de 10 centímetros, no tienen sujeción y es como clavarlo en la playa. Pueden salir volando y tocar una pala del helicóptero”. Ahora solo hay en uso una de las siete pistas porque los compañeros están “desesperados por trabajar” y han tenido que poner bloques de hormigón sobre la hierba artificial para que no “saliera volando”. “Todo se arregla con parches”, expone.

Los bomberos consideran que con este lastre quedan muy desprotegidas zonas dañadas por los incendios de 2025 y con mucho margen aún para arder. “Hubiera sido clave en el episodio de incendios de junio y julio en El Bierzo”, comenta, tras múltiples focos que se veían fácilmente desde Oterico, con sus trabajadores impotentes por tener que ir en coche hora y media al frente de llama cuando volando sería un cuarto de hora. Los brigadistas, pese al trastorno que genera, admiten que con este panorama no se debía usar la base de Oterico por el alto riesgo que acarreaba. Lo ideal sería volver a Camposagrado una vez solventada la fuga de queroseno que la cerró: “Podrían habernos dejado allí, tiene poco uso ahora y ya no es helipuerto cuando podría haberse mantenido. No se ha sustituido sino perdido, podríamos volver a ella y salvar lo que queda de campaña pero a ver qué político echa atrás una base nueva”.

World.title: Naufraga el polémico plan que pretendía crear en Canarias la primera granja de pulpos del mundo
World.content:
Fin al polémico proyecto de implantar la primera granja de pulpos del mundo en el Puerto de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Nueva Pescanova informó la pasada semana a la Autoridad Portuaria de su solicitud de desistimiento del procedimiento de otorgamiento de concesión demanial —un permiso oficial que da el gobierno para usar un bien público de forma exclusiva, con un tiempo límite y pagando una tasa— para la instalación de una “Granja de Cultivos Marinos” en el puerto canario.

Más información El dilema ético de la primera granja comercial de pulpos del mundo proyectada en Canarias

Según ha informado el organismo público, la empresa ha concluido “que no resulta oportuno continuar impulsando la solicitud de concesión presentada en los términos actualmente planteados”. Argumenta para ello “las circunstancias concurrentes sobrevenidas” durante el procedimiento y ante “los nuevos requerimientos administrativos” demandados por la Comisión Autonómica de Evaluación Ambiental. La empresa matiza en su escrito que esta decisión “no implica reconocimiento alguno” sobre la eventual viabilidad futura de otras alternativas técnicas, ambientales o de ubicación que pudieran analizarse en su caso.

Puerto de la Luz, en Las Palmas de Gran Canaria.

En 2022, trascendió que la compañía gallega tenía previsto poner en marcha en el plazo de un año unas instalaciones de 52.000 metros cuadrados en el Puerto de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. En ellas se emplearía a 300 personas, que producirían unas 3.000 toneladas de pulpos al año. Los planes contaron desde un primer momento con la oposición de numerosas organizaciones científicas y en favor de los derechos de los animales.

Elena Lara, la responsable de investigación de la organización internacional Compassion in World Farming, explicaba en 2022 su rechazo a estos planes. “Los pulpos son animales extremadamente inteligentes y complejos, necesitan mucha estimulación en su entorno”, subraya. “Son especies solitarias, no adaptadas a las condiciones intensivas en las granjas. Sería irresponsable ponerlos en tanques vacíos sin ningún estímulo”.

La científica Lara había elaborado poco antes un informe en el que reclamaba al Gobierno español que hiciese “lo correcto, lo moral y lo ético y no permita que Canarias, ni ningún otro lugar del país, sufra el deshonor de abrir este centro de exterminio de pulpos”. Recalcaba que este tipo de instalaciones no son comparables a las granjas tradicionales con otros seres. “Estos son animales salvajes, no los hemos domesticado, a diferencia de lo que sucede en las granjas tradicionales. Sabemos cómo mejorar las condiciones de vida de los cerdos y los pollos. Los pulpos, en cambio, son muy frágiles: no hay forma de sacrificar a un pulpo de manera humanitaria”.

Nueva Pescanova ha rehusado hacer declaraciones a este periódico sobre esta decisión. En su comunicación a la Autoridad Portuaria, la empresa explicó que dicha decisión “responde exclusivamente a consideraciones empresariales y regulatorias derivadas de la evolución del procedimiento administrativo”. Durante la tramitación afloró la necesidad de atender las “observaciones y condicionantes” de distintos órganos sectoriales, además de someter al proyecto al procedimiento de evaluación ambiental ordinaria “al apreciar la posible existencia de efectos ambientales que requerían de un análisis adicional”.

“Todas estas circunstancias”, según indica Nueva Pescanova y recoge el organismo público, “aunque no afectan a la viabilidad ambiental del proyecto, han supuesto una modificación sustancial de las condiciones, alcance, plazos y requisitos regulatorios del proyecto inicial, lo que ha obligado a la empresa a replantear su configuración y estrategia de desarrollo”.

En el fondo del debate está el éxito del pulpo entre los consumidores. Los cefalópodos —pulpos, calamares y sepias— representaron el 7% de las exportaciones mundiales de productos acuáticos animales en 2024, según el informe Sofia de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO), con un valor total de exportaciones de 12.700 millones de dólares (10.990 millones de euros). Esto supuso un descenso del 2,5 % respecto a 2023, tras una caída del 8,6 % en 2022.

China, Marruecos y Mauritania concentran la mayoría de las capturas mundiales de pulpo. Entre los exportadores, destacan China, España, Marruecos, Indonesia y Vietnam. España también es uno de los principales importadores en términos de valor, junto con Italia, China y Japón.

“El tema es mucho más complejo”, explicaba en 2022 a EL PAÍS Eduardo Almansa, investigador del IEO, del Centro Oceanográfico de Canarias y de la Universidad de La Laguna, que colaboró con Nueva Pescanova en el desarrollo de la granja ahora abandonada. “¿Queremos seguir comiendo pulpo? Porque la demanda está aumentando a escala mundial, y a este ritmo, las pesquerías no van a poder cubrirla. Nosotros tratamos de buscar alternativas para producir un alimento del que hay demanda, de una manera viable y sostenible y que se asegure el bienestar animal”.

Polémica

Las granjas marinas han ocupado titulares en las islas en los últimos meses. En noviembre, saltó la noticia sobre la misteriosa muerte de miles de lubinas que estaban siendo criadas en jaulas en Melenara, en la costa este de Gran Canaria. El propietario de las instalaciones es Aquanaria, una empresa de origen cántabro dedicada a la crianza de lubinas de gran talla para uso gastronómico que opera en Canarias desde 1987. Cuenta con 48 viveros en la isla, donde cría entre 40.000 y 50.000 ejemplares al año. Este hecho provocó el cierre de más de una docena de playas en la isla.

Las causas de este suceso siguen sin resolverse: la Fiscalía de Medio Ambiente abrió diligencias de investigación tras detectar “numerosas irregularidades” en la gestión de la EDAR (depuradora) cercana. Aquanaria, que también presentó una denuncia como afectada —murieron 2.500 toneladas de lubinas y sufrió unas pérdidas económicas estimadas en 30 millones de euros—, desmontará esta granja marina antes de que expire la concesión administrativa en abril de 2029, si bien reforzará otras tres explotaciones de mayor capacidad situadas en Tufia, Arinaga y Castillo del Romeral.

World.title: El Ibex conquista por primera vez los 20.000 puntos con unas Bolsas en nuevos máximos
World.content:
Los operadores recordarán la sesión del 4 de agosto como una de las más simbólicas de los últimos años. En una sesión marcada por la caída del precio del petróleo y las expectativas de una desescalada en Oriente Próximo, las principales Bolsas mundiales han alcanzado nuevos máximos históricos. Récords que también han llegado al parqué español. El índice Ibex 35 ha logrado por primera vez conquistar la cota de los 20.000 puntos, un hito psicológico que viene a poner la guinda a una fuerte revalorización. Desde que el pasado 27 de octubre cerró la brecha abierta tras la quiebra de Lehman Brothers y recuperó máximos históricos, el selectivo ha ido superando todas las resistencias que ha encontrado en su camino. Con una subida del 0,2% este martes, el índice cierra por primera vez sobre los 20.000 puntos. Pero esta recuperación no es fruto de una única sesión. Después de firmar en 2025 su mejor año en tres décadas, con una revalorización del 49%, en lo que va de ejercicio se anota ya un 15,7%.

Los mercados siguen demostrando una capacidad de resistencia poco común y el movimiento va más allá del mercado español. Las compras se extienden a ambos lados del Atlántico. Con avances de entre el 1% y el 0,6%, el Dax alemán, el Cac francés, el Euro Stoxx 50, el Stoxx 600 y el Mib italiano se han sumado a la fiesta y han marcado nuevos máximos. En Estados Unidos, los inversores han dejado en un segundo plano las dudas que habían rodeado al sector tecnológico en las últimas jornadas y vuelven a inclinarse por la renta variable. Al cierre de los mercados europeos, el Dow Jones y el S&P 500 avanzan hacia nuevos récords, mientras el Nasdaq se sitúa a apenas 770 puntos de los máximos registrados el pasado junio. A juzgar por el comportamiento de los mercados, nadie diría que la economía mundial atraviesa uno de los momentos de mayor incertidumbre geopolítica de los últimos años. El aumento de las rentabilidades de la deuda, las dudas sobre la inflación o la creciente concentración de las ganancias bursátiles han quedado, al menos por ahora, relegados a un segundo plano.

La moderación de los precios del petróleo ha vuelto a actuar como combustible para las Bolsas. Tras semanas en las que la escalada militar en Oriente Próximo alimentó el miedo a una crisis de suministro, las noticias procedentes de Qatar y las declaraciones del secretario del Tesoro de EE UU, Scott Bessent, han reforzado las expectativas de un próximo acuerdo para reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz. El portavoz del Ministerio de Exteriores qatarí, Majed Al-Ansari, ha asegurado que ya existe un borrador y que el texto está siendo compartido entre las partes implicadas, mientras Bessent declaró a CNBC que existe “la posibilidad de alcanzar un acuerdo hoy o mañana para reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz”. La respuesta del mercado ha sido inmediata: el brent cae de 80 dólares por barril a medida que el mercado descuenta una reducción de la prima de riesgo geopolítica.

El acuerdo, con todo, sigue siendo frágil, tal y como se pudo comprobar hace un mes. Cualquier declaración desafortunada o incidente en el Estrecho podría echar por tierra los avances y devolver la tensión tanto al mercado energético como a las Bolsas. No obstante, los expertos siguen señalando que los costes de la guerra son demasiado elevados para todas las partes y que, con las elecciones de mitad de mandato a la vuelta de la esquina y la popularidad de Trump en mínimos, la Casa Blanca tiene pocos incentivos para alimentar una nueva escalada que termine disparando los precios de la energía y reavivando la inflación.

Si las conversaciones terminan cristalizando en una solución duradera, los analistas creen que la renta variable europea tiene margen para seguir avanzando. Los estrategas de Citi señalan que, aunque el Stoxx 600 cotiza ya en máximos históricos y buena parte de la prima de riesgo geopolítica se ha evaporado, la recuperación sigue siendo desigual. “Numerosos sectores y compañías permanecen por debajo de los niveles previos al conflicto, una situación que podría dar paso a una segunda fase de las subidas, caracterizada por una mayor rotación entre sectores y una extensión de las ganancias”, remarcan. En este contexto, el banco mantiene una visión especialmente favorable sobre sectores como la tecnología sanitaria, la automoción y el cuidado personal, mientras que entre los mercados europeos muestra preferencia por la Bolsa alemana.

La caída de los precios del petróleo no solo está sirviendo de impulso a las Bolsas, sino que también da un respiro a la renta fija, un mercado que en las últimas semanas había comenzado a lanzar señales de alerta. La moderación de las expectativas de inflación reduce el temor a que los tipos de interés permanezcan elevados durante más tiempo y favorece una relajación de las rentabilidades de la deuda. Los bonos a diez años de la zona euro y de EE UU registran descensos de alrededor de 10 puntos básicos y se alejan de los máximos alcanzados semanas atrás. La deuda francesa, que la semana pasada llegó a superar el 4%, se relaja ahora hasta el 3,89%. Por su parte, el bono estadounidense a 30 años, aunque sigue en niveles elevados, toma distancia de los máximos de 2007 registrados tras la reunión de la Reserva Federal. La inacción de la institución y las dudas del mercado sobre su compromiso para controlar la inflación habían impulsado previamente las rentabilidades a largo plazo.

La pregunta ya no es si los mercados han descontado una solución, sino cuánto recorrido les queda si esta termina materializándose. Por ahora, los inversores han dejado en un segundo plano la tradicional apatía estival y siguen apostando por los activos de riesgo. Las próximas pruebas de fuego llegarán con los resultados de gigantes tecnológicos como SpaceX (esta noche al cierre) o Nvidia (26 de agosto), así como con las señales que envíen los bancos centrales sobre el rumbo de los tipos de interés. Un mensaje más duro de lo esperado por parte de los responsables monetarios podría poner a prueba una confianza que, hasta ahora, ha demostrado ser extraordinariamente resistente.

World.title: Pistas para un viaje de verano a Portugal: de las playas del Algarve a los azulejos de Lisboa
World.content:
Ciudades y pueblos llenos de encanto, pistas para comer bien y barato y algunos trucos para descubrir el país

Año tras año, Portugal es un destino de vacaciones recurrente. Pero decir Portugal puede tener muchos significados: están las playas del Algarve que acogen a los amantes del surf, los pueblos del centro del país llenos de encanto y calles empedradas o los paisajes que dejan el Duero y el Tajo a su paso por el país vecino. Además del magnetismo de Lisboa y Oporto, dos ciudades llenas de vida y de historia.

Esta es una guía de destinos para quienes este verano viajen a Portugal.

Además, dos pistas gastronómicas para saber dónde comer y qué pedir en Lisboa y Oporto. Así como una visita cultural imprescindible en la capital lusa.

Y la experiencia viajera en primera persona de Paco Nadal, dispuesto a regresar una y otra vez al país.

World.title: Local mayors step up pressure to end border checks after crashes
World.content:
The mayor of a border town has urged transport minister Vincent Karremans to hold talks with his German counterpart about border checkpoints following a string of serious accidents.

Four people have died in collisions near the border and at least 10 have suffered serious injuries since Germany reintroduced stricter checks in December 2024.

In the most recent incident last Friday, three people were injured in a crash involving four vehicles, including two lorries, on the A12 at Babberich, just before the border.

The German government has said it wants to extend the controls into the autumn, despite the implement of the European Migration Pact, which Dutch foreign minister David van Weel said would make the checkpoints “a thing of the past”.

Aad van Oosten, acting mayor of Zevenaar, urged Karremans to raise the issue with German interior minister Alexander Dobrint, who is a supporter of extending the controls.

“We have tried to raise awareness of our situation with other councils in the area, both in the Netherlands and Germany,” he told Omroep Gelderland. “All we get in reply is that there is no alternative.”

Chaos on roads

Van Oosten is not the first Dutch local politician to raise concerns about the impact of German border checks. In March Mark Boumans, mayor of Doetinchem, called for them to be scrapped following another five-vehicle collision, also at Babberich, in which three people were injured, including a child.

The following month Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the council of Dutch regional safety boards, said the checks had cost millions of euros of damage and lost income and led to chaos on minor roads.

Bruls disputed the effectiveness of the checks after figures showed just under 3,500 people were suspected of trying to enter Germany illegally from the Netherlands and 1,750 were turned away at the border in six months.

Dutch officials checked the documents of 123,320 people at the border and turned 470 away in the first nine months after selected checks were introduced.

Van Oosten said the frequency of the accidents showed they could not be put down to inattentive motorists. “People should pay attention while driving, but this is a serious matter that is not as simple as just paying more attention,” he said.

World.title: Fourteen more councils placed under supervision over asylum
World.content:
Twenty-four councils are now under government supervision for failing to provide enough asylum accommodation, after asylum and migration minister Van den Brink added fourteen new names to the list.

His ministry publishes a monthly list of councils not meeting their legal obligation under the “spreading law”, which sets each council a share of the places the country needs. The first ten were named last month.

Being placed under supervision means the responsible councillors must come to the ministry to explain themselves and agree where and when an asylum centre will open.

The government uses a six-step escalation ladder. The 24 councils are on step three. At step six the cabinet can force a council to open a centre.

A ministry spokesperson said appearing on the list was a factual observation and doesn’t indicate a particular reason. It could reflect political unwillingness or other obstacles, which are established at talks with the ministry.

Only one of those talks has taken place so far, partly because of the summer holidays. That meeting was with Westland, which is required to house about 700 asylum seekers and has so far provided none. It has resisted the law for years, and its council previously said there was no local support for a centre.

The fourteen added are Aalsmeer, Bronckhorst, Brunssum, Bunschoten, De Ronde Venen, Dinkelland, Hardinxveld-Giessendam, Hellendoorn, Lopik, Montfoort, Oldebroek, Oldenzaal, Vlaardingen and Vught.

World.title: No plates, no fines: farmers escape penalty for A35 blockade
World.content:
Around 80 farmers who blocked the A35 motorway near Almelo last Thursday will not be fined, because the number plates on their tractors were taped over and police cannot work out who they were.

Officers filmed the protest, but a police spokesman told regional broadcaster RTV Oost that the footage is unlikely to lead anywhere. “We have insufficient information,” he said.

Covering a number plate is itself an offence under Dutch traffic law, but police said that in this situation there is little they can do about it, given they cannot identify the drivers.

The blockade, on the stretch between Wierden and Almelo, lasted less than an hour but caused a four-kilometre jam. The farmers were protesting against the cabinet’s nitrogen emission plans.

Demonstrators told RTV Oost that they considered it a success and described it as a spur-of-the-moment action.

It is the latest in a series of tractor protests along Dutch roads this summer. Police took a different approach to a separate motorway blockade last month, arresting 270 Extinction Rebellion demonstrators who occupied the A12 in The Hague.

World.title: Readers still prefer paper books despite rise of digital options
World.content:
Paper books remain by far the most popular reading format despite the rise of e-readers and audiobooks, a study by ABN Amro has found.

Figures from Dutch publishers showed that physical books accounted for 86% of the total market in 2025, broadly in line with other countries such as the United States where paper books account for four-fifths of all sales.

The share of the total revenue is even larger because printed books are more expensive to produce, allowing for larger profit margins. E-books accounted for 6% of the total Dutch sales volume of €42 million.

The resilience of books at a time of advancing technology partly comes down to their simplicity: books do not need to be charged up, cannot crash or be deleted and can be replaced cheaply if necessary.

But books also have a prestige that makes them attractive to readers, ABN Amro wrote in a report titled “the paper book is still king”.

“Readers value the contact with paper, turning the page and even the smell of a book,” they said.

Status symbol

“A paper book is a possession that stands out from the bookcase, a sign of identity and status. So paper books are still attractive in a digital age because of the old-fashioned, analogue and direct character of the reading experience.”

Research at Tokyo University using MRI scanners found that reading on paper stimulates different processes in the brain from using a screen, promoting deeper understanding in readers and better retention of the information.

Nearly half of readers use paper books exclusively, while another 43% use a combination of printed, electronic and audio books. Only 2% listen exclusively to audiobooks, while another 5% only read e-books.

Lisa Kuitert, professor of book studies at the University of Amsterdam, said she was unsurprised by the findings.

“Ever since the emergence of digital books people have been saying the end of paper books is on its way. But people who say that aren’t readers,” she told the Financieele Dagblad. “People who enjoy reading prefer paper.”

Challenge of AI

ABN Amro said paper books were here to stay, but other formats were becoming increasingly important alternatives – particularly audiobooks, which people can listen to while on the move or exercising.

Mario Bersem, senior economist specialising in media and technology and one of the report’s authors, told Dutch News that bookshops still had a healthy future despite a sharp decline in the sector in the last 15 years.

“The number of bookshops has fallen hugely since 2010, but the drop was mainly at the start, when people started buying more from webshops. That shift seems to be behind us,” he said.

“Bookshops have become places to meet, much more than they used to be, where you can get a cup of coffee or attend a reading. But they are also still the main places where people buy books: 55% of books are sold over the counter.”

The report also said that an increasing number of published books are using AI for research, editing, translating or even producing texts. By one estimate, half of ebooks published in the United States in 2025 showed signs of AI use.

The use of AI has led to rows about authorial rights and compensation, as AI models are trained on published texts. In June Dutch publishers signed a “book pact” to protect authors from intellectual property theft and create a mechanism for paying royalties.

“For publishers AI clearly represents both an opportunity and a risk,” ABN Amro said in their report. “Technology can help with developing and distributing texts, but it can also put pressure on the value of intellectual property.”

World.title: Rabobank profit flat as it braces for loan losses
World.content:
Rabobank made no profit growth in the first half of this year, reporting a net profit of nearly €2.7 billion, the same as in the first six months of 2025, after setting aside €562 million for loans that might not be repaid.

That is more than four times the €136 million it set aside a year earlier, the bank said in its results statement.

Chairman Stefaan Decraene told reporters the provisions related to two cases in South America but declined to name the companies or projects involved, broadcaster NOS reported.

Business in the Netherlands grew. Deposits at the Dutch retail arm stood at €375.1 billion, and lending at €293 billion.

Takeover talk

Decraene said Rabobank was open to buying another bank, telling NOS that scale is becoming more important.

Rabobank also said it will invest up to €2 billion in strengthening its data and IT systems and scaling up its use of artificial intelligence. Reuters reported that the spending will be spread over the next three years.

The bank’s return on equity was 9.5% and its core capital ratio 20.2%, which it said makes it one of the best-capitalised banks in Europe.

World.title: Man who held prison staff hostage given suspended jail sentence
World.content:
A man who held three prison staff hostage at knifepoint for several hours has been given a further suspended sentence of a year.

Corné H. seized and handcuffed his victims for several hours on December 5 last year at the jail in Vught after threatening them and five other colleagues with kitchen knives.

The 30-year-old had served a nine-month term for holding four staff at a bar in Ede, Gelderland, against their will in March the previous year.

At the time of the incident he was being detained in Vught’s psychiatric unit waiting to be given a place in a clinic under the Dutch compulsory treatment system (tbs).

The sentence was suspended to allow H. to continue his treatment, which began in June, meaning he will only have to go back to prison if he commits another offence.

The court in Den Bosch heard that H. suffered as a result of conditions including PTSS, schizophrenia and autism, which influenced his behaviour. A psychiatric assessment also said he had “anti-social and borderline personality traits”.

The judge said his victims feared for their lives and the incident “must have been dreadful for them”, but accepted H. had diminished responsibility and imposed a sentence that met the prosecution service’s demands.

At the earlier trial, H. was cleared of taking the bar staff in Ede hostage but convicted of depriving them of their liberty and threatening them.

Police sealed off the venue after he went in at closing time with guns and explosives and threatened to blow up the building, leading to a stand-off lasting more than eight hours.

World.title: Police raise concerns over sharp rise in weapon seizures
World.content:
Dutch police seized 5,165 gas and alarm pistols, air weapons and pepper sprays last year, up from 4,080 in 2022, according to figures given to broadcaster NOS – a rise of almost 27%.

Police said they did not know whether the increase indicates that more people are carrying such weapons, or if it reflects boosted efforts to find and confiscate them.

Gas and alarm pistols are the main worry because they are hard to tell apart from real firearms, police spokesman Martin van der Meij told NOS. Alarm pistols make a loud bang but fire no projectile, while gas weapons can release tear gas.

They are cheap, easy to obtain and relatively simple to convert into working firearms, he said. A converted pistol was used to kill the crime reporter Peter R. de Vries in 2021.

Buying these weapons in Germany or Belgium and bringing them into the Netherlands is a criminal offence, though people do not always realise it.

Herman Oldenkotte, who runs a gun shop in Gronau just over the German border from Enschede, told NOS that he estimated 80% to 90% of his customers were Dutch. In Germany the weapons can be bought without a licence by anyone over 18.

Police also say more weapons are arriving by post. The Netherlands has pressed the EU for years to bring in a licence requirement or a ban.

Pepper spray is banned for civilians under Dutch weapons law. The justice ministry said in June it planned to allow permits for people at particular risk, such as stalking victims, while ruling out legalising it for everyone.

World.title: Limburg wildfire smoke reaches Friesland and Drenthe
World.content:
Smoke from the wildfire in northern Limburg is drifting as far north as Friesland and Drenthe, where emergency control rooms have been swamped with calls.

Safety authorities have asked people not to ring 112 unless they can actually see a fire, broadcaster NOS reported. The smell of the smoke has also been reported across Gelderland, including in Apeldoorn, Nijmegen and Doesburg, and across the German border in the Kleve district, according to German broadcaster WDR.

The fire, which started in the Boschhuizerbergen nature reserve near Oostrum, burned through at least 100 hectares, the Limburg-Noord emergency services authority said. A possible thunderstorm this evening could help quell the blaze.

An NL-Alert was sent out warning people to stay out of the smoke and close windows, doors and ventilation.

A spokesperson said that tackling the fire was tougher than expected and that wildfires can behave unpredictably.

Venray mayor Michiel Uitdehaag said firefighting would continue until at least 9am on Wednesday but that so far there had been no property damage or injuries. A nearby campsite was evacuated on Monday.

Two military helicopters are dropping water drawn from the Maas.

The fire started in dense woodland and sand drifts that fire engines cannot reach, NOS reported, and the wind keeps turning, sending the fire in different directions.

Not enough vehicles

The Dutch fire service does not have enough specialist wildfire vehicles because such fires are rare, Daan Peeters of the Nederweert brigade told NOS.

The vehicles being used at Venray were brought in from the centre of the country. Other fire services already have them, and more brigades should, he said, adding that the question was not when the next forest fire would come but where.

World.title: Unexploded WWII ordnance discovered under busy Warsaw street
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Part of central Warsaw was shut down today after unexploded ordnance from World War Two was found buried under a major road during construction work. The discovery, which came just days after the city commemorated the anniversary of its wartime uprising against Nazi-German occupation, led to traffic being diverted and residents being warned to stay away from their windows and avoid going outside while bomb disposal experts worked to safely remove the item. W Al. Solidarności znaleziono niewybuch, najprawdopodobniej z czasów II wojny światowej. ℹ️ Czytaj więcej: https://t.co/Fv6oe84XiM pic.twitter.com/BfjQPZveYZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 4, 2026 The object, reportedly around 70 centimetres long, was found early on Tuesday morning on Solidarity Avenue, a major thoroughfare, during modernisation work on tram lines. “We were digging a trench and I literally just touched it with the tip [of my digger],” the operator of the excavator who found it told broadcaster TVN. Staff working at the site were immediately evacuated to a safe distance. Police later confirmed that the item is unexploded ordnance, and that initial findings indicate it dates from World War Two. Bomb disposal experts arrived at the scene in the afternoon. However, they have not confirmed precisely what type of ordnance was discovered or its origin, reports Polsat News. Warsaw was the site of major fighting during World War Two, beginning in 1939, when Nazi Germany invaded and occupied Poland. In 1943, the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, the largest single act of Jewish resistance during the war, took place. On 1 August 1944, the Polish underground Home Army launched the Warsaw Uprising, which was the largest single act of armed resistance anywhere in German-occupied Europe during the war. In response, the Germans destroyed much of the city, around 85% of which lay in ruins by 1945. Warsaw’s historic Old Town was meticulously rebuilt after the war. But many other parts of the city were redeveloped by the newly installed communist authorities, including Solidarity Avenue (which during the communist era was named after Polish-Soviet Red Army General Karol Świerczewski). Thousands of vehicles drove over the unexploded ordnance every day for decades. “Warsaw is marked by history, and there are many such surprises,” Witold Urbanowicz, spokesman for the city’s tram operator, told news website Interia. After the fall of the Warsaw Uprising – which began 80 years ago today – the German occupiers expelled the city's entire population. However, some survivors decided to remain among the ruins. They became known as "Robinson Crusoes" and this is their story https://t.co/UuVbfbcpQ4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 1, 2024 Unexploded ordnance is regularly found in Poland. In May this year, around 200 anti-personnel mines dating from World War Two were discovered at the construction site of a student dormitory at Kraków’s Jagiellonian University. In October last year, two men were hospitalised after an artillery shell that one of them had brought home from a forest exploded in his apartment while the pair were under the influence of alcohol. Earlier that year, wild boars unearthed 21 mortar shells buried in a forest since the war. In 2023, 72 unexploded artillery shells were discovered during renovation work at a primary school and four pieces of World War Two ordnance were found in the walls of a church undergoing renovation. Wild boars dug up 21 mortar shells from World War Two that had been buried in a Polish forest. The unexploded ordnance has now been safely removed without harm to either the animals or humans https://t.co/W9kaPr1BNw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Russia condemns Poland’s “sacrilegious” demolition of Soviet monument
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the demolition of a Soviet-era monument in Poland, calling the decision “sacrilegious” and a “flagrant violation” of an agreement between the two countries on respecting places of remembrance. However, Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which financed the demolition, says that the monument was a “Soviet propaganda object” that was removed under a law requiring the “decommunisation” of public spaces. On Friday, around 150 residents in Pyrzyce, a town of 12,000 in northwestern Poland, gathered to watch the demolition of a monument to the Red Army that had stood there for decades. Initially, a memorial had been established in the town alongside a cemetery for Red Army soldiers in the immediate aftermath of World War Two, when the Soviets had driven the Nazi German occupiers out of Poland but then introduced a new communist government of their own. However, the soldiers’ remains were later moved to a military cemetery elsewhere in the region and the monument itself was redesigned and moved to another location within Pyrzyce. Its final form, created in 1984, was a huge rectangular concrete structure weighing several hundred tons and featuring a relief depicting the head of a Soviet soldier. A plaque said “Eternal glory to the fallen heroes 1941-1945” (a timeline that ignores the Soviet invasion and occupation of parts of Poland in 1939). Such Soviet monuments remained in many Polish towns and cities long after the fall of communism in 1989. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. However, only in 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, did the removal of Soviet-era monuments gather pace, with dozens demolished since then. Those efforts were led by the IPN, in particular during the time that the institute was headed by Karol Nawrocki between 2021 and last year, when he was elected president of Poland. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 At the start of this year, the local authorities in Pyrzyce began public consultations on removing their Soviet memorial, finding that a majority were in favour of the move, according to the IPN. In February, the town council voted to remove the monument. It will now be replaced with a new one commemorating Polish independence. “We are aware that this change evokes various, often very strong, emotions among residents,” wrote the local authorities on social media. “We respect both the voices of those supporting the actions taken and those who differ in their assessment of the current monument and its place in the history of Pyrzyce.” “We hope that independence – as a paramount value for all Poles – will unite residents beyond differences of opinion and assessment of the past. We want the emerging space to be a space of shared remembrance, reflection, and a dignified celebration of the most important national ceremonies.” The removal of the monument drew condemnation from the Russian embassy in Warsaw, which announced on Monday that it had lodged a formal protest. It called the decision the “latest sacrilegious step by the Polish authorities” and said that it “constitutes a direct and flagrant violation” of a 1994 agreement between Poland and Russia on respect for graves and other places of memory. “The illegal dismantling of monuments is an overt attempt to falsify history, to erase from the consciousness of the Polish nation the memory of the heroism of Soviet soldiers,” added the embassy. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 31 lipca 2026 r. w Pyrzycach (województwo zachodniopomorskie) na podstawie decyzji władz polskich został przeprowadzony demontaż pomnika ku czci poległych w latach 1941–1945 bohaterów – żołnierzy radzieckich. ❗️Ten kolejny świętokradczy krok… pic.twitter.com/cKhfFxIL9s — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) August 3, 2026 In response to such complaints from Russia, Poland has regularly pointed out that the 1994 agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. The IPN notes that such monuments were “Soviet propaganda objects”, designed to support the Moscow-backed communist regime, rather than genuine places of commemoration. Attending the demolition ceremony in Pyrzyce on Friday, IPN deputy president Karol Polejowski pointed out that the final version of the monument had been established in 1984 shortly after the period of martial law in Poland, when the authorities brutally clamped down on the democratic opposition. “Local communist activists, eager to curry favour with their Soviet masters, erected a monument honouring the Soviet army. This is not a symbol of liberation – it is a symbol of enslavement!” he declared, as the monument was torn down. 💪 Sowiecki obiekt propagandowy zostanie zastąpiony przez Pomnik Niepodległości, a przestrzeń wokół nowego monumentu stanie się godną sceną dla uroczystości patriotycznych. pic.twitter.com/5x4KEzG3Vb — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) July 31, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%). The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value. “The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet. “However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added. On Monday, the biggest boosts to the WIG20 index were provided by PGE, Poland’s biggest power producer, and KGHM, a Polish multinational mining company, with their shares rising 3.3% and 1.6%, respectively. The surge was also supported by improving risk appetite across global markets following signs of a de-escalation in tensions in the Middle East. This has pushed WIG20 above the levels last seen 19 years ago, just before the index plunged almost 70% during the 2008 global financial crisis, and then suffered another sell-off during the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. Reform of one of the pillars of Poland’s pension system in 2014, which reduced the role of open pension funds, ushered in years of market stagnation and left the index struggling to meaningfully rebound in the following years. Another decline came during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in the aftermath of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In October 2022, however, the WIG20 started its rebound, rising by 195% since then. More than 30 Polish-listed companies have doubled in value over the past three years, including large-cap stocks such as Orlen, PKO BP, Bank Pekao, KGHM and Tauron, according to an analysis by economic journalist Rafał Hirsch published by news service WNP. Polish state energy firm Orlen has seen its market valuation rise to its highest ever level, and surpass Russia’s Gazprom for the first time https://t.co/w3po4izshJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 12, 2026 BNP Paribas’s analysts, however, note that, “despite a long-term upward trend and reaching record highs”, the Polish stock market “is still valued below many other European markets”. “Our stock market…remains significantly cheaper than the US market and most European markets, but at the same time, when viewed against its own historical performance, it is now relatively highly valued,” they said. Poland’s main stock index, the broader WIG, also closed on Monday at a record high of 148,428 points, having hit several records in recent months. Poland’s benchmark WIG stock index has passed the 100,000-point mark for the first time. Meanwhile, the Warsaw Stock Exchange has been the world’s best performing so far this year "It is a clear signal of the strength of our economy," says the PM's office https://t.co/fIgGWOLLn8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 25, 2025 Analysts warn, however, that unlike in the case of WIG, the WIG20’s record may prove short-lived because the benchmark is a price index, which excludes dividends. When companies in the index pay dividends, their share prices usually fall by about the same amount, which automatically pulls the index down even if nothing has changed in the companies themselves. Monday was the last day investors could buy shares in PKO BP and qualify for this year’s dividend. From Tuesday, the bank’s shares will trade ex-dividend, a move expected to reduce the WIG20 by about 0.8% because of PKO BP’s large weighting in the index. World.title: Morawiecki confirms breakaway Polish opposition group will form new party
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that the group he leads, Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), which is in the process of splitting from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, will soon form a party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes” over abortion or same-sex marriage. However, Morawiecki made clear he retains a hardline position on migration, saying he wants “zero Muslim migrants”, even legal ones, in Europe. He also categorically ruled out ever working with current Prime Minister Donald Tusk, but left the door open to potentially cooperating with the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which is part of Tusk’s current ruling coalition, and with the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), an opposition group. Morawiecki u Rymanowskiego: „Do 15 października założymy partię” No coraz ciekawiej 👀 pic.twitter.com/0FrMafvTEl — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) August 3, 2026 Development Plus was founded as an association by Morawiecki, a former PiS prime minister and current deputy leader of the party, in April this year. That immediately prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. Matters came to a head last month, when PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded that all the party’s lawmakers sign a pledge of loyalty and commit to leave any political associations they are part of. Morawiecki and his allies refused to do so, prompting Kaczyński to declare that meant they had effectively resigned from the party. Last week, Development Plus announced it had formed its own separate parliamentary caucus with 40 MPs in the Sejm, the most powerful lower house of parliament. The move immediately made it the third-largest group in the parliament, while also meaning PiS was no longer the biggest. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 Most MPs in Development Plus, including Morawiecki himself, are still technically members of PiS, a situation that will only change if they decide to quit the party or if they are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks to complete. However, on Monday, in a lengthy interview with journalist Bogdan Rymanowski, Morawiecki confirmed that he would establish a new, separate party. That will happen “at the latest on 15 October”, when Development Plus is planning to hold a major convention, he added. Morawiecki claimed that a small group of hardliners, associated in particular with the nationalist Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska) party that was absorbed into PiS in 2024, were “devouring” PiS from the inside, pushing it in a more “radical” direction and seeking to take control of the party and its finances. The former prime minister argued that it had been a “colossal mistake” by PiS to try to compete with two rising far-right groups, Confederation and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), while abandoning the centre ground. He noted that this had coincided with the party’s support in polls falling to below 25%, its lowest level in 14 years and well below the 35% that the party won at the 2023 parliamentary elections, when Morawiecki was prime minister. Morawiecki also traced PiS’s problems back even further, pointing to the decision in 2020 to push for a near-total abortion ban. He claimed that he had, at the time, “warned [Kaczyński] repeatedly…that it would lead to disaster”. Subsequently, PiS fell from support of over 40% in polls to around 30% within a year. Morawiecki told Rymanowski that he and many of his colleagues in Development Plus support a return to the pre-2020 abortion law. “Poland doesn’t need the fervour of ideological disputes” over issues such as abortion and same-sex marriage, especially during a time of “crises, wars and disruptions”, said Morawiecki. “I want us to talk about strengthening the economy, strengthening security, restoring the job market, and how to prevent young people from thinking about leaving Poland again.” Poland’s prime minister has admitted it was a “mistake” for the ruling party to push for the constitutional court to introduce a near-total abortion ban in 2020. He claims “he has always been a supporter” of the abortion law that existed before the ruling https://t.co/QObza3Raxk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 6, 2023 The former prime minister also made clear that his overriding aim is “removing [Tusk] from power and overthrowing the Tuskist system”, which he characterised as a combination of “idleness” and “profound cynicism”, with the lack of any significant reforms disguised by “political marketing”. Asked if he would seek to achieve this by forming a coalition with the far-right Confederation, Morawiecki refused to rule it out, saying that “voters will decide” on the strength of various parties. “But I certainly won’t form any coalition with Tusk,” he clarified. However, Morawiecki suggested he would be willing to work with PSL and its leader, current deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, if they left the coalition with Tusk. PSL is the most conservative part of the current government. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 While Morawiecki generally laid out a vision of a relatively moderate centre-right party that he wants to create, he also made clear that he retains a hardline position on opposing Muslim immigration. “I would say zero Muslim immigrants at all. In Poland, absolutely zero…even into Europe,” he declared. Asked by Rymanowski to clarify if he was talking about only illegal migrants, or legal ones as well, Morawiecki said he was also referring to legal Muslim migrants. “We cannot accept them, because they will destroy our culture,” said Morawiecki. “After what I see Muslims doing in Europe, I don’t want to turn Europe into a Muslim caliphate….The French and Germans…are making a colossal mistake: destroying their own culture, destroying security, and destroying peace.” An Islamic group wants to establish a new prayer centre in Kraków for the growing local Muslim community The idea has drawn concern from some local residents and protests from right-wing groups, who say Poland should avoid "the mistakes of western Europe" https://t.co/ClCwusyhhp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 23, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Pole becomes first person to swim 160km Baltic Sea route between Sweden and Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish swimmer Bartłomiej Kubkowski has become the first person in history to swim across the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Poland, covering a distance of just over 160 kilometres (99 miles). On Sunday evening, an exhausted Kubkowski clambered onto the beach in the town of Dziwnów on Poland’s northern Baltic coast, around 56 hours after he had set off from Kaseberga in Sweden on Friday. The achievement marks a personal triumph for Kubkowski, for whom this was the fifth attempt to complete the route. His effort this year has raised over 715,000 zloty (€166,000) for children’s cancer treatment so far, with donations to his fundraiser still coming in. View this post on Instagram A post shared by PURELY ATHLETICS (@purelyathletics) During the crossing, Kubkowski was unable to sleep and, although a support boat accompanied him and provided food and drink, he was not allowed to touch the vessel itself. His journey of around 160km was not far off the longest-ever continuous, unassisted open-water swim ratified by the Marathon Swimmers Federation, which was the 168.3 km swum by American Sarah Thomas in 2017 in Lake Champlain, between the US states of New York and Vermont. Kubkowski has been attempting to swim the route between Sweden and Poland since 2022, getting progressively closer to achieving the goal. Last year, he came within 11km of the Polish coast before extreme exhaustion and deteriorating weather forced him to give up, reported Eurosport. However, Kubkowski, a former competitive swimmer who now devotes himself to ultraswimming, did last year manage to break the world record for the longest distance swum in a swimming pool over 24 hours, after he managed to cover 103.6 km (64.5 miles). Another Polish swimmer, Karolina Szczepaniak, is also currently attempting to swim from Sweden to Poland along a slightly different route to Kubkowski’s. At the time of writing, she is around 110km into the 172km journey, and has raised almost 400,000 zloty for charity. Szczepaniak, a former Olympic swimmer, also attempted the feat last year, but was forced to give up after 57 hours amid worsening weather. However, the 146.7km she swam set a new record for the longest distance covered by a female swimmer in the Baltic Sea and a Polish record for open-water swimming by a woman. A Canadian multinational operator of convenience stores, Alimentation Couche-Tard, has announced plans to acquire Poland’s Żabka Group, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores. The company has offered 32 zloty per share, valuing Żabka at 32.6 billion zloty (€7.56 billion). Żabka’s main shareholders have agreed to sell their stakes, with final approval still required from stock market investors. If the transaction is completed, Żabka is likely to be delisted from the Warsaw Stock Exchange just two years after its market debut. Właściciel Circle K chce przejąć 100% Żabki. Cena w wezwaniu ma wynieść 32 zł za akcję =>https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB via @PawelBiedrzycki https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB — Strefa Inwestorów (@strefainw) July 31, 2026 The acquisition will be carried out through Alimentation Couche-Tard’s Polish subsidiary, Circle K, which runs petrol stations, and will cover all of Żabka Group’s more than one million shares. Alimentation Couche-Tard has already secured commitments to acquire at least 57.2% of the company. Heket, an entity linked to CVC Capital Partners owning 37.6% of Żabka’s shares, and PG Investment Company, holding 10%, have agreed to sell their entire stakes. A group of major individual shareholders, together controlling 9.6% of Żabka’s shares, has also agreed to sell its holdings to the Canadian buyer. The investors include members of the company’s management and former executives. They have also agreed to reinvest part of the proceeds from the sale into Alimentation Couche-Tard shares. The tender offer for the remaining shares was announced on Friday by Ipopema Securities, which is acting as the intermediary in the transaction. Alimentation Couche-Tard and Żabka expect subscriptions for the offer to open around 26 August, following a review of the tender document by the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF). The companies foresee the transaction closing by the end of the year. The Canadian company expects Żabka to continue operating independently, under the leadership of its current management team, and to retain its brand. Żabka shares jumped after the announcement, rising from 29.26 zloty to around 31.60 zloty on Friday afternoon, an increase of about 8%. Żabka, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores, has made its stock market debut in one of Europe’s biggest listings this year. Its IPO was the fourth largest in the history of the Warsaw Stock Exchange and valued the firm at €5 billion https://t.co/fmqLteZjdR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 18, 2024 If completed, the acquisition would be the largest takeover in the history of Alimentation Couche-Tard, which already owns 17,300 stores across 27 countries. Alex Miller, Alimentation Couche-Tard’s CEO, said the company is “committed to supporting the continued growth of the Żabka business while drawing from its strengths in areas such as food, digital engagement, customer loyalty, private brand, supply chain, logistics and innovation”. Żabka made its debut on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 2024 in one of Europe’s largest initial public offerings that year, with a valuation of around €5 billion. The company is Poland’s largest convenience store operator, with about 13,000 locations nationwide run by around 11,000 franchisees. It has also expanded internationally, opening its first stores in Romania and reaching 100 outlets there last year. Poland’s largest convenience chain, Żabka, has opened the 100th store of its Romanian brand, Froo, one year after launching there. “We are learning from local consumers and laying the groundwork for a long-term presence in Romania,” says Żabka’s VP.https://t.co/0CaZTaVhlB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2025 In mid-July, Japanese retailer Seven & i Holdings, which operates the global 7-Eleven chain among other businesses, also emerged as a potential investor in Żabka.
