World.title: Coop celebrates bigger market share but won't hike prices in wake of Prisma acquisition
World.content:
At the end of August, Coop Eesti Keskühistu will acquire Prisma Peremarket's stores in Estonia. By the end of November, all former Prisma stores will operate under the Coop brand.

According to Coop representative Rainer Rohtla, Coop and Prisma are currently working to finalize the transaction.

"We have signed a purchase agreement under which Coop will acquire Prisma Peremarket as a company, and based on that agreement, the Competition Authority has approved the completion of the transaction. Right now, all the preparations needed to complete the deal are underway, which means a great deal of work internally for both Coop and Prisma. The acquisition will take place on August 31, less than a month from now, after which Coop Eesti Keskühistu will become the sole owner of Prisma Peremarket," Rohtla said.

He added that during the second or third week of September, the current Prisma stores will be transferred to various Coop regional cooperatives, which will begin operating them.

On product selection, Rohtla said the goal is to preserve the assortment customers are accustomed to, though doing so will require a major effort from the company.

"Prisma's product range is very distinctive. It includes many Scandinavian products as well as many Coop private-label products that are not currently sold in Coop stores. This is one of the areas creating a significant workload for us. To keep Prisma's entire product range available in stores as it is today, we need to expand our logistics and supply chain capabilities. Nothing will be removed, but we will also add many of the products Coop customers already love. The rollout of Prisma's best-selling and most popular products to other Coop stores will take place during the first half of next year. By July next year, Prisma's most popular products will be available in Coop stores across Estonia," Rohtla said.

Rohtla also said there is no reason to fear price increases, citing current market conditions.

"Even if we wanted to raise prices, given how intense competition is in Estonia's retail sector, how much food prices have already increased in recent years and the fact that consumers' purchasing power and confidence remain low, there is simply no room in the market for price increases," he said.

One of the aims of the acquisition is to increase Coop's market share.

"Our market share in Tallinn is around 5 percent, compared with 23 percent nationwide. Now our market share in Tallinn will increase to 17 percent," Rohtla said.

Rohtla again declined to disclose the purchase price for Prisma's stores or say how quickly Coop expects to recoup its investment.

"Time will tell. We are very optimistic, knowing what we plan to do to make the investment pay off, but that's certainly not something I want to disclose today," he said.

Analyst: Prisma's exit will have no effect on food prices

Economist Raul Eamets agreed that a larger market share for one retail chain does not necessarily lead to higher prices.

"There is actually fairly strong competition in the grocery market, particularly since Lidl entered Estonia a few years ago. I don't think Prisma's transition to the Coop brand will have any significant impact on prices. If you look at the profit margins of the major retail chains — how much profit they make as a share of sales — we're talking about just a few percent. Simply having a larger market share doesn't suddenly give a retailer the ability to manipulate prices," Eamets said.

He added that food prices in Estonia are driven primarily by global factors.

"Price levels are influenced less by domestic competition than by food producers' prices and, above all, global market prices. Those are what determine food prices. We are highly dependent on imported food ingredients and finished products. According to the latest figures, prices for imported goods increased by 7 percent," the economist said.

Rocca al Mare keskuse Prisma, one of the largest outlets. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"The reality is that Estonia cannot fully feed itself, so we depend on what happens outside the country. Unfortunately, there is little we can do to influence that," he added.

On April 7, Coop Eesti Keskühistu and Finnish retail group SOK signed a purchase agreement under which Coop will acquire AS Prisma Peremarket and its 13 stores in Estonia, located in Tallinn and Harju County, Tartu, Narva and Rapla. The parties will also begin a strategic partnership to bring Finnish food and consumer goods to more than 300 Coop stores across Estonia.

The transaction does not include the Prisma brand or the Sokos Hotel Viru. The parties have not disclosed the value of the deal.

World.title: Iraq unveils tourism vision 2035 to attract 10 million visitors
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has unveiled an ambitious long-term strategy to transform its tourism sector, aiming to attract 10 million visitors by 2035 through infrastructure upgrades, workforce development, and the preservation of the country’s rich historical, cultural, and religious heritage.

The Iraqi Tourism Authority announced on Tuesday that it has finalized the Iraq Tourism Vision 2035, a roadmap launched under the slogan “A Prosperous and Competitive Iraq.” The initiative is designed to position Iraq as a leading tourism destination in the region while supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

Ali Yassin, spokesperson for the Tourism Authority, said the agency will begin organizing workshops in Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, Karbala, and Erbil to present the vision’s objectives and implementation mechanisms to stakeholders across the country.

The workshops aim to engage local governments, tourism professionals, and investors in executing the strategy over the coming decade.

According to the authority, the plan seeks to attract 10 million tourists by 2035, with a focus on promoting Iraq’s archaeological, cultural, religious, and natural attractions.

Officials said achieving the target will require significant investment in tourism infrastructure, including improving transportation, accommodation, visitor services, and restoring key heritage sites across the country.

The strategy also calls for the rehabilitation and maintenance of archaeological landmarks, museums, religious sites, and other destinations that showcase Iraq’s diverse historical legacy.

The Tourism Vision 2035 is built around three strategic pillars: integration, sustainability, and quality.

Officials said these principles will guide efforts to create a more competitive tourism industry while ensuring long-term preservation of Iraq’s cultural and natural resources.

The plan also emphasizes improving coordination among government institutions and the private sector to encourage investment and strengthen the country’s tourism ecosystem.

In addition to infrastructure projects, the Tourism Authority highlighted the importance of developing skilled professionals capable of supporting the industry’s growth.

The vision includes programs to strengthen the capabilities of workers in the tourism sector through training and capacity-building initiatives, recognizing that qualified personnel are essential to delivering high-quality visitor experiences.

The Tourism Authority said the long-term strategy reflects its commitment to restoring Iraq’s position as a prominent international tourism destination.

By combining investment in infrastructure, heritage preservation, sustainability, and workforce development, officials hope the plan will contribute to economic growth while showcasing Iraq’s unique cultural and historical assets to visitors from around the world.

World.title: Iraq liquidity crisis does not mean bankruptcy, says government financial adviser
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq liquidity crisis should not be interpreted as a sign that the country is running out of money or facing bankruptcy, according to government financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Salih. He emphasized that the Iraqi government retains sufficient financial and administrative tools to continue paying salaries and meeting its core obligations despite ongoing cash flow pressures.

Speaking to Shafaq News on Tuesday, Salih explained that the current challenge stems from timing mismatches between oil revenues entering the treasury and the government’s monthly expenditure commitments, particularly public sector salaries.

Salih stressed that Iraq’s financial pressures are primarily linked to liquidity management rather than a shortage of national wealth.

According to him, the government’s current challenges include:

Timing differences between oil revenue receipts and monthly spending obligations.

High levels of public expenditure.

Continued expansion of public sector employment.

Weak non-oil revenues.

Regional tensions affecting trade and oil exports.

He said these factors have created temporary liquidity pressures but do not indicate a severe financial crisis.

The financial adviser said the government can continue paying salaries and maintaining essential public services through several financial management tools.

These include:

Efficient liquidity management.

Prioritizing essential expenditures such as salaries.

Rescheduling non-urgent investment projects when necessary.

Improving tax and fee collection.

Reducing financial waste.

Increasing non-oil government revenues.

Salih also noted that domestic or external borrowing remains available if required, provided borrowing remains within safe public debt limits and supports financial stability.

Looking ahead, Salih said Iraq must accelerate long-term economic reforms to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

He highlighted several priorities:

Diversifying oil export routes.

Developing transportation and energy infrastructure.

Expanding non-oil revenue sources.

Building a more resilient economy capable of absorbing regional and global shocks.

He concluded that sustainable financial stability cannot rely solely on oil income and will require broader economic diversification and structural reforms.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports surpass 1.25 million bpd in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July 2026 by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June, according to Attaqa News.

Despite this partial recovery, Iraqi shipments remain significantly lower than pre-war levels, reflecting a 63 percent decline from the July 2025 figure of 3.38 million barrels per day.

With the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad’s major marine trade route, strains on the state budget are increasing due to declining oil earnings.

The decrease in revenue from oil exports has driven the Iraqi government to accelerate its search for alternative land routes to export crude oil via neighboring countries.

In July, Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports reached one million barrels per day for the first time since March 2026, marking the end of a steep fall.

The country’s oil exports totaled 3.31 million barrels per day in January, 3.34 million barrels per day in February, 542,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, 98,000 barrels per day in May, 493,000 barrels per day in June, and 1.25 million barrels per day in July.

The figures show that Iraq’s average offshore oil exports fell by 60 percent between January and July 2026, hitting 1.31 million barrels per day compared to 3.33 million barrels per day during the same period in 2025.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Iraq clarifies role in oil tanker transit through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has clarified that it is not responsible for the movement of crude oil tankers after they leave Iraqi export terminals, emphasizing that buyers assume full responsibility for transporting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The statement comes as Iraq continues to navigate regional security challenges affecting energy exports, while officials report gradual improvements in crude oil sales in recent months.

Oil Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said Iraq continues to sell crude oil under the Free on Board (FOB) system, meaning ownership and responsibility for the cargo transfer to the buyer once the shipment is loaded at Iraqi ports.

According to Al-Rikabi, tankers carrying Iraqi crude continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz after departing export terminals. However, he stressed that the ministry is not responsible for the vessels’ navigation routes or for securing the necessary transit approvals.

“The ministry sells crude oil at the port, after which the buyer assumes responsibility for transporting and managing the shipment,” Al-Rikabi said.

He added that the ministry neither owns the tankers nor oversees their operations once they leave Iraqi waters.

Despite transferring responsibility to buyers, Al-Rikabi said the Oil Ministry continues monitoring tanker movements through international vessel-tracking systems.

He noted that Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) follows shipments until they reach their destination refineries, allowing authorities to track export deliveries without directly managing vessel operations.

Some tankers transporting Iraqi crude carry cargoes of up to 2 million barrels, according to the ministry.

Al-Rikabi also indicated that Iraq’s oil export performance has improved steadily in recent months despite disruptions linked to the regional security situation and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said sales last month exceeded those recorded in the previous month, continuing a gradual recovery following earlier export challenges caused by tensions affecting maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes, carrying a significant share of global crude exports, making uninterrupted transit critical for Iraq’s energy sector and international oil markets.

World.title: Iraq launches 3,000-cubic-meter gas storage facility in Najaf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated a gas storage project as part of the Oil Ministry’s efforts to raise storage capacity in line with current operations to boost gas output.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry revealed Monday the start of trial operations at a new gas storage facility in the central Iraqi province of Najaf.

Undersecretary for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber said in a statement that the new gas depot has a storage capacity of 3,000 cubic meters and is part of efforts to boost production and storage capabilities, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The step also reflects the ministry’s efforts to develop the transportation, storage, and distribution systems of liquefied gas, according to Saber.

The Iraqi official explained that the inauguration of the depot at the trial operation stage is certainly an important milestone in improving the capacity of strategic reserves and increasing the flexibility of the supply system.

The initiative will ensure that the requirements for liquefied gas in the central provinces and other cities are adequately met.

The delivery of liquefied gas to the new depot via pipelines, as opposed to tanker trucks, will adhere to safety standards and enhance the stability of supplies.

World.title: Iraq dollar exchange rate rises in local markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq dollar exchange rate increased in local currency markets on Tuesday, with the U.S. dollar gaining 1,000 Iraqi dinars compared with the previous trading session, according to market data published by local outlets.

Despite the increase in parallel market rates, the official exchange rate set by the Central Bank of Iraq remains at 131,000 Iraqi dinars per $100.

Exchange rates recorded in major Iraqi cities were as follows:

City Selling Price (IQD per $100) Buying Price (IQD per $100) Baghdad 152,750 152,250 Erbil 152,000 151,500 Basra 152,250 152,000

The latest figures indicate that the parallel market continues to trade well above the official exchange rate, reflecting the ongoing gap between official pricing and street market demand.

Currency exchange rates in Iraq are monitored closely by businesses, importers, and consumers because fluctuations in the parallel market can affect the prices of imported goods and broader market activity.

World.title: Millions of Shia Muslims gather in Iraq’s Karbala to mark Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Millions of Shia Muslim pilgrims are gathering in the Iraqi holy city of Karbala to mark Arbaeen under tight security measures.

The tremendous procession follows the yearly 40-day mourning period for Imam Hussein, the Prophet Muhammad’s grandson.

Iraqi officials anticipate that up to 22 million pilgrims will visit the city. More than 4.5 million foreign travelers from 172 different countries have entered Iraq, including a significant number of Iranian pilgrims.

Thousands of security personnel have been deployed to protect the surrounding area and routes leading to the Imam Hussein Shrine.

Millions of pilgrims dressed in black walk the ancient 76-kilometer (47-mile) journey from Najaf to Karbala.

Arbaeen, one of the world’s greatest religious gatherings, has increased in popularity in the past few years.

It occurs 40 days after Ashura, the martyrdom anniversary of the Prophet Mohammad’s grandson Imam Hussein.

The event marks the end of a 40-day mourning period for the killing of Imam Hussein, the grandson of the Prophet Mohammed, by the forces of the caliph Yazid in 680 AD.

The holy city of Karbala in central Iraq represents the heart of Shiite Islam. It is where Imam Hussein and his brother Abbas are buried in two massive shrines that face one another.

Pilgrims openly demonstrate their sadness by weeping and crying in memory of Imam Hussein.

World.title: Iraq tightens security to prevent cross-border attacks amid regional tensions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi authorities have begun implementing tighter security measures to prevent rockets or drones from being launched from Iraqi territory toward neighboring countries, according to a report published Tuesday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada, citing security and political sources.

The report said security forces are increasing surveillance in Basra, the deserts of Najaf, Samawa, and Anbar, particularly in areas bordering Saudi Arabia and Jordan.

According to the sources, Iraqi authorities also plan to impose “strict penalties” on any security official found to have allowed attacks to originate from areas under their responsibility.

The reported measures follow an emergency security meeting chaired by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, during which the government announced the formation of a joint security committee tasked with preventing further cross-border attacks.

In a statement issued after the meeting, al-Zaidi instructed security agencies to enforce the law, strengthen stability, and ensure Iraqi territory is not used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries.

Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi also said in a televised interview that the prime minister’s firm position had helped avert what he described as a potential military strike against Iraq.

Despite the new measures, Al-Mada’s sources questioned whether Baghdad would be able to completely prevent future drone launches or avoid possible retaliatory action by neighboring states.

The report said U.S. officials believe some Iran-supplied ballistic missiles remain hidden inside Iraq. However, a senior figure from a major Shiite political party, speaking anonymously, told the newspaper that armed factions have temporarily stepped back from using such missiles following U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to halt what he described as a planned strike against Iran.

According to the report, Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) also ordered the evacuation of facilities in Nineveh as a precaution against potential future U.S. airstrikes.

Al-Mada reported that most members of the ruling Coordination Framework support the government’s official approach to responding to the regional crisis through diplomatic and, if necessary, military channels.

However, the newspaper said one influential Shiite leader continues to oppose the government’s position.

According to the report, armed factions have given the government until Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia following recent military developments, while some groups reportedly oppose Baghdad’s efforts to bring weapons under exclusive state control.

The newspaper also cited political analysts who argued that Iraq remains caught between broader regional tensions involving the United States, Iran, and Gulf countries, increasing the risk of further military escalation.

The claims published by Al-Mada are based on unnamed security and political sources and have not been independently confirmed by Iraqi authorities.

NEW DELHI: Govtâs rooftop solar initiative, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, has crossed the 50-lakh household milestone within 29 months of its launch in Feb 2024, achieving half of its target of one crore households by March 2027.According to new and renewable energy ministry, more than five lakh households installed rooftop solar plants in July, the highest monthly addition since the scheme began. Officials said nearly one lakh new households are being added under the scheme every six days, making it one of the fastest-growing clean energy programmes in the world.âThe pace of installation has increased 3.2 times over the last nine months, rising from 5,038 installations a day in Oct 2025 to nearly 16,328 a day in July 2026,â the ministry said in a statement.When the scheme was launched in 2024, the country had fewer than eight lakh rooftop solar installations.Of the schemeâs Rs 75,021-crore outlay, govt has already disbursed Rs 28,024 crore directly to beneficiaries through direct benefit transfer. So far, nearly 19 lakh households have recorded zero electricity bills in at least one billing cycle, significantly reducing their power expenses.The ministry said more than 12 lakh households earned a combined Rs 421 crore by selling surplus electricity to the grid in FY 2024-25, translating into an additional income of around Rs 3,500 a year per household.Cumulatively, 14.8 GW of rooftop solar capacity has been commissioned under the scheme so far.The ministry said 1.6 lakh installations have been completed for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana beneficiaries, Below Poverty Line families, and SC/ST households across four states under the utility-led aggregation model. The model enables low-income households to install rooftop solar systems while helping states reduce their power subsidy burden.Govt has also solarised 25,255 govt buildings with a combined rooftop solar capacity of 872 MW, against 41,542 buildings where installations totalling 1,418 MW are considered feasible. Overall, states have identified around 3.2 lakh govt buildings with an estimated rooftop solar potential of 4,400 MW. Of these, 81,329 buildings with a combined capacity of 1,450 MW have already been solarised, the ministry said.

World.title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel was struck by a projectile and sank off Yemenâs western coast on Tuesday. All 14 crew members aboard the vessel were rescued and brought to safety.

Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said the MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The crew comprised 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni sailor.

The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha, Sonowal added. No casualties were reported.

Ministry of External Affairs said the vessel sank in the Red Sea off the Yemeni coast on August 4 and confirmed that all 13 Indian nationals had been rescued.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh was coordinating with Yemeni authorities to ensure the safety of the crew and provide necessary assistance.

The government-affiliated National Resistance Forces said coast guard and naval units carried out a joint rescue operation after the vessel was attacked about 13 nautical miles (24 km) south of the Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah.

World.title: Child protection panel launches inquiry into Meta over alleged child sexual abuse material ads
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has decided to institute an inquiry into allegations that s related to Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) appeared on Meta-owned platforms, government sources said on Tuesday.

The move comes after the child rights body took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report last month alleging that s on

promoted child sexual abuse material.

NCPCR had issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc. on July 3 seeking an explanation, to which the company responded a week later.

Initiates formal inquiry

Following an examination of Meta's reply, the Commission has now decided to initiate a formal inquiry "to determine the facts of the matter", sources said.

Separately, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) had directed the Delhi Police to conduct a comprehensive probe into the allegations and examine whether Meta and other entities complied with mandatory reporting obligations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

The NHRC took cognisance of the BBC World Service report, which alleged that paid s on Instagram used specific keywords and redirected users to channels where child sexual abuse material was allegedly being offered for sale.

World.title: ‘No insurance, no fuel’: SC directs govt to prepare pilot project, flags 16.54 crore uninsured vehicles
World.content:
SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road

16.54 crore vehicles uninsured

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Centre to evolve a pilot project under which vehicles without valid third-party insurance could be denied fuel at petrol pumps until they obtain the mandatory insurance cover.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra took note of the large number of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads and said nearly 56% of vehicles remain uninsured, citing the Report of the Standing Committee on Finance 2024-25.The court directed the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), in consultation with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), to deliberate and evolve a pilot project linking fuel supply to a vehicle's valid insurance status.âAs deliberated upon in court, the IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority) in consultation with the MoRTH (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways) to deliberate and evolve a pilot project whereby fuel for vehicles to be linked with valid insurance status. In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps, until such time that valid insurance is obtained,â the bench said.The court said denying fuel to uninsured vehicles could help identify uninsured or unregistered vehicles and encourage owners to obtain valid insurance.âSuch projects would ensure ground-level compliance with the statutory mandate of Section 146 of the MVA. This may be done through the use of ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) cameras,â it said. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the court noted, has âin principle, no objectionâ to the proposal.The Supreme Court also directed that the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles be extended.In 2018, the court had mandated third-party insurance for three years for new cars and five years for new two-wheelers at the time of purchase or registration.âWe notice that despite eight years having passed from the said direction, a large number of vehicles remain uninsured,â the bench observed.It directed that third-party insurance henceforth be purchased for four years for new cars and six years for new two-wheelers, and directed IRDAI to issue the necessary directions immediately.The court said 16.54 crore out of 30.48 crore vehicles were uninsured, describing the figure as âstarkâ.It said the lack of insurance can delay or defeat the statutory safeguard of compensation for road accident victims.âThe object behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the MVA is not just that victims of road accidents are compensated, it is also that they are not drawn into prolonged litigation,â the bench said.It noted that uninsured vehicles often leave accident victims and their families facing prolonged litigation over the quantum and liability for compensation. The impact, it said, is particularly severe when a victim dies or suffers permanent disability.The court also directed IRDAI and MoRTH to deploy ANPR cameras in certain states, integrating them with data from the Insurance Information Bureau and the VAHAN portal.The system is intended to enable automatic issuance of e-challans to uninsured vehicles.The court also directed that state police be provided with handheld devices or downloadable applications linked to the Insurance Information Bureau and VAHAN data to verify the insurance status of vehicles in real time.âThis is to monitor real-time insurance status of vehicles and impose challans for violations, ensuring compliance with mandatory insurance on the ground,â the court said.The court further directed IRDAI to provide private vehicle owners with various policy options, including add-on covers, personal accident cover and own-damage cover, alongside a base policy offering the minimum coverage required under the Motor Vehicles Act.The court also took note of road accidents on national highways and the problem of long queues at toll plazas. It directed the Centre to implement pilot projects on selected corridors to replace stopping at toll plazas with automatic detection of vehicles passing through toll points.The directions were issued in a motor accident claim case, with the court observing that compliance with the statutory requirement for third-party motor vehicle insurance remains inadequate despite the existing legal framework.It said accident victims and their families often have to ârun from pillar to postâ to receive compensation.

World.title: ‘Will give fitting reply at appropriate time’: Sunetra Pawar on Congress’ ‘gungi gudiya’ jibe
World.content:
Sunetra Pawar (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister and NCP president Sunetra Pawar on Tuesday said she would give a "fitting reply" at an "appropriate time" after the Congress' state unit called her a "gungi gudiya" (mute/silent doll).âWhen the time comes, I will give a fitting reply,â Sunetra Pawar told reporters when asked about the Congressâ criticism.Her response came amid a political row triggered by a social media post by the Maharashtra Congress referring to her as a âgungi gudiyaâ, drawing sharp criticism from the NCP and its ruling alliance partners, the BJP and the Shiv Sena.NCP leaders, including the partyâs working president Praful Patel, condemned the remark as âderogatory and disrespectfulâ towards a woman leader.In a statement, Patel called the language used against Sunetra Pawar âinsulting.ââMaharashtra, which follows the progressive ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, B.R. Ambedkar and Yashwantrao Chavan, will never accept the insult of women. It is unfortunate and condemnable that the Congress has used such language against a woman leader despite the party being led by women leaders such as Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi,â the former Union minister added.Patel demanded that the Congress immediately delete the post and issue a public apology.The controversy escalated after a group of NCP workers entered the Congressâ Gandhi Bhavan office in Mumbai and staged a protest over the post.Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal condemned the NCP workersâ action, alleging that the protesters intended to resort to violence and accusing the BJP and the police of backing them.He, however, maintained that the Congress would continue to follow Mahatma Gandhiâs path of non-violence despite the provocation.Sunetra Pawar took over as Maharashtra deputy chief minister following the death of her husband, Ajit Pawar, in a plane crash in January. The following month, she became the NCP president, filling the vacancy created by his demise.

World.title: Farmers back ethanol in meeting with agriculture minister, say it will boost income, secure energy
World.content:
Farmers from seven states met Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and extended support to the ethanol policy

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A group of farmers on Tuesday voiced support for ethanol during a meeting with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan at Krishi Bhawan, amid general protests against the use of the E20 bio-fuel mix in vehicles, saying ethanol would increase farmersâ income and secure the countryâs energy.Chouhan told them that the central govtâs thinking was clear that the benefit of the ethanol programme should reach the entire chain from the field to the fuel tank, but the biggest share should go in the interest of the farmer.The farmers, under the banner of the Akhil Bharatiya Kisan Samanvay Samiti, told the minister that ethanol was a big opportunity for farming, provided its policy was farmer-centric and the right price of the crop reached the farmer directly.In India, sugarcane contributes to 30-35% of total ethanol production while the remaining 65-70% is derived from grains such as maize and rice.Farmers from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu were present at the meeting. They insisted that the real benefit of the ethanol programme should go to the farmer, not only to companies or middlemen.They said that with ethanol, farm produce would not remain limited to the mandis, but would reach petrol pumps and the energy market, creating a new and stronger market for farmers.They told the minister that if ethanol was made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstock, farmers would get more buyers, and crop spoilage or storage problems would be reduced.Extending their full support for ethanol, they said it was necessary that whether it was maize or sugarcane, farmers should get proper prices for any crop. Farmer representatives said, âWe want the ethanol policy to create a new path for farming, not a new worry for us.We are with ethanol, if ethanol also stays with us.âThe farmers demanded that the agriculture ministry and farmer organisations should jointly explain clearly which crops would benefit from ethanol and how, and how a shift could be made from water-intensive crops to drought-tolerant crops.Chouhan assured that the policy would be reviewed to maintain a balance in the prices and demand of maize, rice, sugarcane and other feedstock. He said decisions would be taken only from the perspective of farmer interest, especially the benefit of maize farmers. He added that the negative narrative on ethanol would be countered through scientific studies and technical reports, and a fact-based dialogue would be carried out in partnership with farmers.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami welcomes Kanwariyas in Haridwar, inaugurates health camp amid Kanwar Yatra
World.content:
CM Dhami also inaugurated the Chief Minister's Health Service Camp at the Alaknanda Hotel premises

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

HARIDWAR: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday welcomed Kanwariyas arriving in Haridwar for the annual Kanwar Yatra, showering flower petals on Shiva devotees from a helicopter and washing the feet of five pilgrims as a mark of respect.CM Dhami also inaugurated the Chief Minister's Health Service Camp at the Alaknanda Hotel premises and reviewed the medical facilities and arrangements made for the pilgrims. He interacted with Kanwariyas from different states and served food to the devotees.Addressing the gathering during the felicitation programme, Chief Minister Dhami said that the Uttarakhand Government is committed to ensuring that every Shiva devotee visiting Devbhoomi experiences a safe, convenient, and respectful pilgrimage. He said that the Kanwar Yatra is not merely a religious event but a grand celebration of India's Sanatan traditions, social harmony, and spiritual consciousness. The state government, in coordination with all concerned departments, is continuously working to ensure the successful conduct of the pilgrimage.The chief minister said that for the past five years, he has had the privilege of serving Shiva devotees during the Kanwar Yatra.He described Lord Shiva as the source of faith, strength, and devotion for millions of people. Despite challenging conditions, devotees undertake journeys of hundreds of kilometres while chanting "Bam Bam Bhole," reflecting their unwavering devotion. He added that the Kanwar Yatra also symbolises discipline, service, dedication, and social unity.Chief minister Dhami informed that more than one crore Kanwariyas have successfully collected holy Ganga water and continued towards their destinations this year. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, unprecedented efforts are being made to preserve and develop India's cultural heritage and sacred sites. Projects such as the Kashi Vishwanath Dham Corridor, Mahakal Lok, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi, the reconstruction of Kedarnath Dham, and the Badrinath Master Plan are giving Indian culture a new global identity.Referring to the 2013 Kedarnath disaster, the Chief Minister said that under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Kedarnath Dham has been transformed into a grand and divine pilgrimage destination through extensive reconstruction. Facilities such as the Aastha Path, Saraswati Ghat, the statue of Adi Shankaracharya, and accommodation for pilgrimage priests have been developed. He further stated that proposed projects such as the Ganga Corridor in Haridwar and the Sharda Corridor will provide fresh momentum to the state's development and religious tourism.The CM emphasised that the safety of pilgrims remains the government's highest priority. He said that CCTV surveillance, drone monitoring, ambulance services, health camps, and emergency response systems have been deployed along the pilgrimage routes. He also appealed to devotees to maintain discipline, uphold the sanctity of the pilgrimage, and respect religious traditions throughout the journey.He appreciated the dedicated efforts of the police, district administration, health department, sanitation workers, environmental volunteers, NGOs, and all personnel engaged in service during the Kanwar Yatra. He said that the successful organisation of such a massive event is possible only through collective commitment and teamwork.Chief minister Dhami also honoured five police personnel and five sanitation workers (Paryavaran Mitras) for their outstanding contribution to the successful management of the Kanwar Yatra. He said that the recognition symbolises the state's gratitude to all the frontline workers who work day and night tirelessly to ensure security, cleanliness, healthcare, and other essential services for millions of devotees.Earlier in the day, Dhami highlighted the religious significance of visiting Binsar Mahadev Temple in Ranikhet during the holy month of Shravan.In a post on X, CM Dhami wrote, "On the sacred occasion of the Shravan month, the worship of Lord Bholenath holds special significance. During this auspicious time, devotees arrive in large numbers at the Binsar Mahadev Temple, nestled in the lap of the dense cedar forests of Ranikhet (Almora), seeking faith, devotion, and spiritual peace.This region not only offers the pilgrims a divine experience but also a unique communion with nature. If you are travelling to Ranikhet during the Shravan month, be sure to visit this sacred abode of Lord Shiva for darshan and worship to attain the benefits of spiritual merit."Shravan (or Sawan) holds immense significance in Hinduism. It is believed that the Shravan month is the most beloved month of Lord Shiva. Worshipping Shiva in this month gives relief from all troubles. This year, the holy month of Sawan begins on July 30 and concludes on August 28.

World.title: From Hype To Help: How AI Is Solving India's Real Problems
World.content:
AI is often discussed in terms of chatbots, coding assistants, and workplace productivity. But a quieter transformation is taking shape across India, where AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges, from helping farmers cope with climate change to assisting teachers in rural classrooms, improving TB screening and making govt services available in multiple languages.

According to MeitY, Indiaâs digital economy contributed Rs 31.6 lakh crore, or 11.7% of the GDP, in 2022-23. By 2030, that share is expected to approach one-fifth of the economy. Increasingly, govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Education offers one of the clearest examples. Microsoftâs Shiksha Copilot, developed with the Shikshana Foundation using Azure OpenAI Service, is helping around 1,000 teachers prepare localised lesson plans for nearly 30,000 children across 750 govt schools in Karnataka.

What once took teachers hours can now be done in about 10 minutes. The programme is expected to expand to another 8,000 teachers across Karnataka and Telangana. The company has also announced a larger commitment to train 10 million Indians in AI by 2030 after achieving its earlier target of skilling 2 million people ahead of schedule.

Agriculture has emerged as another major beneficiary. Farmers increasingly face unpredictable rainfall, pest outbreaks, and rising temperatures, while agricultural extension services remain stretched.





AI-powered advisory platforms help bridge that gap.

Farmer.Chat, developed by Digital Green, provides advice through voice, text, images and videos in local languages. It offers recommendations tailored to crops, soils, weather, and local conditions. The platform reportedly expanded from 15,000 to 250,000 Indian users within a year while costing less than$1 per farmer annually. Digital Green also says it has reduced the cost of introducing a new farming practice from $35 to under $1 by using AI-driven advisory systems.

Non-profit institute Wadhwani AI uses similar technologies at a larger systems level. Its AI tools are now reported to have reached more than 190 million people. The organisation says its solutions have helped prioritise over 35,000 villages for tuberculosis screening, supported nearly 2.7 lakh teachers, delivered personalised learning support to 7.9 million students and resolved more than 5 million agricultural grievances.

Healthcare is seeing practical applications. Startup Qure.ai has developed an AI system that analyses chest X-rays for tuberculosis. A Health Technology Assessment by the Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar reportedly found the technology to be more cost-effective than conventional screening pathways. That could be significant in a country that accounts for nearly 28% of the world's new tuberculosis cases.

And, language is a barrier AI is beginning to address. Platforms such as Bhashini aim to make govt services accessible in more than 22 Indian languages. AI-powered translation is already being used for grievance redressal, Aadhaar transliteration, railway enquiries and several citizen services, reducing dependence on English or Hindi and making digital governance more inclusive.

Climate resilience is becoming another area of rapid innovation.

SatSure combines AI with satellite imagery to help banks assess agricultural loans, monitor climate risks, and evaluate farms. The company says its systems operate across more than 70,000 villages, reducing loan underwriting time while improving assessments for farmers who often lack formal credit histories.

India is also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to support this ecosystem. Enterprise AI adoption is estimated at 87%, while the IndiaAI Mission has expanded national computing capacity to 38,000 GPUs under an outlay exceeding Rs 10,300 crore. Nearly universal 5G coverage, digital public infrastructure such as AgriStack and a growing climate-tech startup ecosystem are providing the foundations for wider AI deployment.

The common thread across these initiatives is not the sophistication of the algorithms but their ability to solve everyday problems at scale.

World.title: Kudumbashree to organise 2,000 Onam fairs in Kerala
World.content:
The Kudumbashree will organise more than 2,000 Onam fairs across the State to ensure a wider market for products manufactured by its women entrepreneurs.

The fairs will be held from August 20 to 25. The State-level inauguration of the Onam fairs will be held at Alappuzha. Fairs will also be organised in the other 13 districts. Two fairs will also be held in each community development society (CDS) of the Kudumbashree.

Nearly 50,000 entrepreneurs will take part in the fairs, being organised to provide a wider market for local products and increase the income of entrepreneurs and neighbourhood groups.

Last year, the turnover from sale of products made by agro microenterprises and the sale of Onasadya and Onam kits was₹50.8 crore. The Kudumbashree hopes to surpass it this time.

The Kudumbashree has prepared detailed guidelines to make available quality products to consumers at fair prices and ensure transparency in prices.

Food products made by microenterprises and enterprises in the agriculture and animal husbandry sectors; handicrafts; apparel; value-added products; millets grown by women farmers from Attappady as well as value-added products made by them from sweet potato; products made by tribal women from Idukki; vegetables, fruits, and flowers cultivated as part of Onakkani and Nirappolima schemes will be available at the fairs.

Products will also be available through the Kudumbashree’s Pocket Mart e-commerce app.

World.title: Kerala University conducts surprise inspection at Kerala Law Academy
World.content:
Kerala University conducted a surprise inspection at the Kerala Law Academy on Wednesday based on complaints that alleged violations of the guidelines issued by the Bar Council of India (BCI)

According to official sources, the university received complaints that the college has admitted 300 students each in two shifts for its three-year LL.B. programme. Besides, it is alleged that no other college in the State conducts an undergraduate law programme under a shift system.

Moreover, the university is investigating whether law classes are being conducted at the law college after 7 p.m. in violation of strict guidelines issued by the BCI.

Based on directions from Kerala University Vice Chancellor in-charge Mohanan Kunnummal, a team comprising Syndicate members R.S. Sasikumar, S. Nazeeb, Ajay Jewel Kuriakose and the Head of the Department of Law, Sindhu Thulaseedharan, conducted the inspection.

The inspection report will be submitted to the Vice Chancellor for further action.

World.title: Had no intention of disparaging women, says Udhayanidhi Stalin
World.content:
DMK youth wing leader and Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, who was released on station bail on Tuesday night after being arrested on a complaint of making misogynistic remarks, maintained he did not intend to hurt or disparage anyone, especially women. He accused the TVK government of foisting the case against him to divert attention from the issues faced by farmers that he had raised during the protest in Thanjavur on August 3.

“My parents did not raise me like that. I have a wife, daughter, sister and a family. I treat all women as my family, mother or sibling,” he told journalists before boarding a flight to Chennai at the Tiruchi International Airport.

He thanked the DMK president M K Stalin, party office bearers and alliance leaders who “understood” him and condemned his arrest. “My only regret is some leaders, without hearing or examining my speech fully, have condemned my remarks as wrong. I did not speak in double entendre as alleged by some. I spoke straight. I only said water has not been released in the Cauvery and wanted it to be released in the river. I will say this again and again and will not be cowed down by such foisted cases. I will face this legally,” Mr.Udhayanidhi asserted. He added the present government, as a policy, used diversionary tactics to divert public attention from burning issues.

The government, which he termed as a ‘circus,’ had foisted the case for speaking in favour of farmers and was unable to reply to the issues he had raised during the party protest in Thanjavur on Monday. “On Tuesday morning, they cut and paste what I had not spoke and spread it even in national media. They arrested me and took me all the way to Sengipatti as if I was a terrorist. They let me off after asking various queries,” he said.

Chief Minister C.Joseph Vijay does not know the history of DMK. “The people are watching and they will give a fitting reply,” he maintained.

Asked what would be the DMK’s strategy henceforth, Mr.Udhayanidhi said he and other party leaders will meet the party president M.K.Stalin and act according to his advice.

World.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest LIVE updates: Leader of Opposition says statement wasn't intended as double entendre
World.content:
Leader of Opposition and DMK youth wing leader Udhayanidhi Stalin, who was arrested and brought to Thanjavur on a complaint alleging he made misogynistic remarks seemingly directed at a film actor, was released on Station Bail on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) night after being subjected to questioning at the Sengipatti Police Station.

Also read | Propriety in public discourse: On Udhayanidhi Stalin’s double entendre remarks

Earlier, amidst high drama and tension, Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin was brought to Thanjavur by road, after being arrested in Chennai. He was questioned for over an hour at the Sengipatti Police Station in connection with the case booked against him on charges of making offensive remarks against a woman actor during the DMK’s demonstration on the Cauvery issue in Thanjavur on Monday (August 3, 2026).

Mr.Udhayanidhi Stalin walked out of the station at around 8.15 p.m. to a boisterous welcome from the assembled cadres. He waved to the crowd standing through the car’s sunroof and accepted their greetings.

A petition seeking anticipatory bail was filed before the Madras High Court in the morning. During the hearing in the afternoon, Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan directed the police to release Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin today on station bail after questioning. He also directed the Leader of the Opposition to cooperate with the investigation and appear for inquiry as and when required. He is being interrogated at Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district.
